name: Decline push-up
form_cues: Put your feet on a bench or chair, hands on the floor under shoulders.; Brace your core so your hips don't sag.; Lower your chest to the floor, then press back up.
common_mistakes: Hips sagging into an arch; Head poking forward toward the floor
safety: Use a stable box or chair that can't slide out from under your feet.
notes: Higher feet shift more load to the shoulders.

name: Incline push-up
form_cues: Hands on a sturdy bench or counter, just wider than shoulders.; Squeeze glutes and brace so your body moves as one piece.; Lower your chest to the edge, then push the surface away.
common_mistakes: Hips sagging toward the floor; Only going halfway down
safety: Make sure the chair or bench can't slide or tip before you start.
notes: The lower the surface, the harder it gets.

name: Knee push-up
form_cues: Kneel with hands under shoulders and hips in line with knees and head.; Lower until your chest is a fist's height from the floor.; Keep elbows about 45° from your body as you press up.
common_mistakes: Piking hips up into the air; Dropping the head toward the floor
safety: Use a folded mat under your knees if kneeling is uncomfortable.

name: Push-ups
form_cues: Hands just wider than shoulders, body straight from head to heels.; Lower until your chest nearly touches the floor, elbows at about 45°.; Push the floor away and finish with arms fully straight.
common_mistakes: Sagging hips or arching the lower back; Flaring elbows to 90°; Cutting the range short
progressions: Decline push-up; Archer push-up; Ring push-ups
safety: Stop if you feel sharp wrist or shoulder pain; try fists or handles to ease the wrists.
notes: Add a weight vest or plate on the back to progress; slow 3-second lowering builds strength.

name: Wall push-up
form_cues: Place hands on the wall at shoulder height, slightly wider than shoulders.; Keep a straight line from head to heels.; Bend elbows to bring your chest near the wall, then press away.
common_mistakes: Letting hips sag or stick out; Flaring elbows straight out to the sides
safety: Stand on a non-slip surface so your feet don't slide.
notes: Step feet further back to make it harder. Great first step for beginners and shoulder rehab.

name: Wide push-up
form_cues: Place hands about one and a half shoulder-widths apart.; Lower your chest between your hands, keeping the body rigid.; Press up while squeezing your chest together.
common_mistakes: Going too wide and straining the shoulders; Letting the head drop first
safety: Keep the width moderate; very wide hands stress the shoulder joint.

name: Doorway row
form_cues: Grip both sides of a door frame, feet close to the threshold.; Lean back with straight arms and a straight body.; Pull your chest toward the frame by squeezing shoulder blades.
common_mistakes: Bending at the hips instead of staying straight; Shrugging up
safety: Hold firmly; a slipping grip means a fall backward.
notes: Walk feet closer to the frame to make it harder. One-arm version works too.

name: Table row
form_cues: Lie under a sturdy table and grip the edge, hands shoulder-width.; Keep your body straight from heels to head.; Pull your chest to the table edge, then lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Hips sagging; Shrugging shoulders toward the ears
safety: Test the table first: it must not tip or slide when you pull.
notes: Bend knees to make it easier.

name: Prone Y-T-W raise
form_cues: Lie face down, forehead resting, arms out in a Y shape.; Lift arms a few centimetres, thumbs up, then lower.; Repeat with arms in a T, then elbows bent in a W.
common_mistakes: Lifting the head and arching the back; Shrugging instead of squeezing shoulder blades
safety: Keep the lift small and pain-free.
notes: Great for posture and shoulder health.

name: Scapular push-up
form_cues: Start in a high plank with straight arms.; Let your chest sink between shoulder blades, then push the floor away.; Keep elbows locked the whole time.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows; Moving the hips instead of the shoulder blades
safety: Keep the range pain-free if you have shoulder impingement.
notes: Great warm-up for push-ups and handstands.

name: Bench dips
form_cues: Hands on the edge of a bench by your hips, legs out in front.; Lower until elbows reach about 90°, staying close to the bench.; Press through your palms to straighten your arms.
common_mistakes: Dropping too deep and straining the shoulders; Letting the hips drift far from the bench
safety: Stop at 90° if you have shoulder issues; use a chair braced against a wall.
notes: Bend knees to make it easier, raise feet onto another chair to make it harder.

name: Diamond push-ups
form_cues: Form a diamond with thumbs and index fingers under your chest.; Keep elbows close to your sides as you lower.; Press up until your arms lock out fully.
common_mistakes: Elbows flaring wide; Hips sagging as the triceps fatigue
safety: Move hands slightly further apart if your wrists or elbows complain.

name: Bodyweight calf raise
form_cues: Stand tall, feet hip-width, fingertips on a wall.; Rise as high onto the balls of the feet as possible.; Pause at the top, then lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Bouncing quickly; Rolling onto the outer toes
safety: Hold a wall or rail for balance.
notes: Stand on a step edge for a bigger stretch.

name: Bodyweight squat
form_cues: Feet about shoulder-width, toes turned out slightly.; Sit hips back and down, knees tracking over toes.; Stand by driving through the whole foot.
common_mistakes: Heels lifting off the floor; Knees caving inward
regressions: Box squat to chair; Wall sit
progressions: Pistol squat; Shrimp squat; Bulgarian split squat
safety: Go only as deep as you can keep a neutral back and heels down.

name: Bulgarian split squat
form_cues: Rest your back foot laces-down on a bench behind you.; Lower straight down until the front thigh is near parallel.; Drive through the front heel to stand tall.
common_mistakes: Front foot too close to the bench; Pushing off the back leg
progressions: Shrimp squat; Dumbbell Bulgarian split squat
safety: Use a stable bench that won't slide.
notes: Hold dumbbells to add load; listed here as the bodyweight version.

name: Cossack squat
form_cues: Start in a very wide stance.; Shift into one hip and squat deep while the other leg goes straight.; Keep the bent-side heel down and chest tall.
common_mistakes: Lifting the heel of the working leg; Rounding the back to get lower
safety: Hold onto a door frame for balance if needed.

name: Forward lunge
form_cues: Step forward and lower both knees to about 90°.; Keep your torso upright and front knee over the foot.; Push hard off the front foot to return.
common_mistakes: Short step that pushes the knee far over the toes; Back knee slamming into the floor
safety: Use reverse lunges instead if forward steps bother your knees.

name: Lateral lunge
form_cues: Step wide to one side and sit hips back into that leg.; Keep the other leg straight and both feet flat.; Push off the bent leg to return to centre.
common_mistakes: Bent knee caving in; Rounding the back
safety: Keep your toes pointing forward or slightly out.

name: Nordic hamstring curl
equipment: Anchor for the heels (sofa, partner) and a mat
form_cues: Kneel with heels anchored under something solid.; Keep hips straight and lower your body forward as slowly as possible.; Catch yourself with your hands and push back up.
common_mistakes: Bending at the hips to shorten the lever; Dropping fast at the start
safety: Start with a few slow negatives; expect heavy soreness the first week.
notes: Proven to reduce hamstring strain risk in sport. Can also be done with a GHD or a band for help.

name: Reverse lunge
form_cues: Step back and lower the back knee toward the floor.; Keep most of your weight in the front heel.; Drive through the front foot to bring the leg back.
common_mistakes: Leaning far forward; Stepping back too narrow and losing balance
safety: Often the most knee-friendly lunge.

name: Reverse Nordic
form_cues: Kneel tall with knees hip-width and toes flat.; Lean your straight body back by bending only at the knees.; Squeeze your quads to pull yourself upright.
common_mistakes: Bending at the hips; Going deeper than you can control
safety: Use a thick pad under the knees and start with a small range.

name: Single-leg calf raise
form_cues: Stand on one foot on a step edge, heel hanging off.; Lower the heel below the step for a full stretch.; Rise as high as you can, pause, and repeat.
common_mistakes: Using the hand to pull yourself up; Bending the knee to cheat
safety: Keep a hand on a rail or wall for balance only.

name: Sissy squat
form_cues: Rise onto your toes and hold a support with one hand.; Push knees forward and lean back so hips stay straight.; Lower until knees are near the floor, then return.
common_mistakes: Bending at the hips like a normal squat; Dropping too fast onto the knees
safety: Use a pad under the knees and skip it if you have kneecap pain.
notes: Strong quad isolation without any machine.

name: Skater squat
form_cues: Stand on one leg with the other bent behind you.; Hinge slightly and lower until the back knee touches a pad.; Push through the front heel to stand.
common_mistakes: Back foot touching down for help; Knee caving inward
safety: Reach arms forward for balance and keep the movement slow.
notes: Similar to the shrimp squat, but the back leg is free rather than held.

name: Sliding leg curl
equipment: Towel or sliders on a smooth floor
form_cues: Lie on your back, heels on a towel, and lift hips into a bridge.; Slide heels out until legs are nearly straight.; Pull heels back under the knees, keeping hips high.
common_mistakes: Letting hips sink as the heels slide out; Moving too fast
progressions: Single-leg sliding leg curl; Nordic hamstring curl
safety: Use on a smooth floor; stop if your hamstrings cramp.
aliases: Towel hamstring curl; Slider leg curl
notes: Also done on a stability ball.

name: Split squat
form_cues: Take a long split stance, both feet facing forward.; Drop the back knee straight down toward the floor.; Push through the front foot to rise, feet staying planted.
common_mistakes: Front knee caving in; Stance too narrow, like walking a tightrope
safety: Hold a wall for balance if needed.

name: Sumo squat
form_cues: Take a wide stance with toes turned out about 45°.; Sit straight down, pushing knees out over toes.; Keep chest tall and squeeze glutes to stand.
common_mistakes: Knees collapsing inward; Leaning far forward
safety: Only go as wide as your hips comfortably allow.
notes: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell between the legs to load it.

name: Tibialis raise
form_cues: Lean your back on a wall with feet a step out in front.; Pull your toes up toward your shins as high as you can.; Lower slowly without touching down fully.
common_mistakes: Feet too close to the wall; Rushing the reps
safety: Step feet further out to make it harder.
notes: Helps balance calf work and may ease shin splints.

name: Walking lunge
form_cues: Step forward into a lunge, back knee just above the floor.; Push up and bring the back foot through into the next step.; Keep your torso tall and steps even.
common_mistakes: Steps too short; Wobbling side to side
safety: Clear a straight path free of trip hazards.

name: Wall sit
form_cues: Slide down the wall until thighs are parallel to the floor.; Keep knees over ankles and back flat on the wall.; Breathe steadily and hold.
common_mistakes: Knees drifting past the toes; Pushing on thighs with the hands
safety: Sit higher on the wall if your knees ache.

name: Bodyweight hip thrust
form_cues: Rest your upper back on a bench, feet flat and knees bent.; Drive hips up until shins are vertical and body is flat.; Tuck chin and squeeze glutes at the top.
common_mistakes: Over-arching the back at the top; Feet too far away
progressions: Single-leg hip thrust; Barbell hip thrust
safety: Make sure the bench is against a wall so it can't slide.

name: Clamshell
form_cues: Lie on your side, hips and knees bent, feet together.; Keep feet touching and lift the top knee.; Pause at the top and lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Rolling the hips backward; Lifting the feet apart
safety: A common rehab move for knee and hip pain.
notes: Add a mini band above the knees to progress.

name: Curtsy lunge
form_cues: Step one leg diagonally behind the other.; Lower until the front thigh is near parallel.; Push through the front heel to return.
common_mistakes: Front knee collapsing inward; Twisting the hips too much
safety: Shorten the step if you feel strain in the knee.

name: Donkey kick
form_cues: Start on hands and knees with a flat back.; Keep the knee bent and push one heel toward the ceiling.; Stop when the thigh is level, then lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back to lift higher; Rotating the hips open
safety: Keep the movement in the hip, not the lower back.

name: Fire hydrant
form_cues: Start on hands and knees, back flat.; Lift one bent knee out to the side to hip height.; Lower with control, keeping weight even on both hands.
common_mistakes: Shifting the whole body sideways; Rounding the back
safety: Go only as high as you can without twisting the torso.

name: Frog pump
form_cues: Lie on your back with soles of the feet together, knees out.; Pull heels close and drive hips up.; Squeeze glutes hard at the top, then lower.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back; Lifting from the lower back instead of the glutes
safety: Skip if the wide-knee position hurts your hips.
notes: Popular high-rep glute finisher.

name: Glute bridge
form_cues: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width.; Drive through the heels to lift hips until body is straight.; Squeeze glutes hard at the top, then lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back at the top; Pushing through the toes
progressions: Single-leg glute bridge; Barbell hip thrust
safety: Keep ribs down to avoid low-back strain.

name: Single-leg glute bridge
form_cues: Lie on your back with one foot planted and the other leg raised.; Push through the planted heel to lift your hips.; Keep the pelvis level, pause, and lower.
common_mistakes: Hips tilting to one side; Arching the lower back
safety: Lower the range if you feel hamstring cramping.

name: Single-leg hip thrust
form_cues: Upper back on a bench, one foot planted, other knee pulled up.; Drive through the planted heel to lift hips level.; Lower with control without touching down.
common_mistakes: Pelvis dropping on the free side; Pushing through the toes
regressions: Bodyweight hip thrust; Single-leg glute bridge
safety: Keep the bench stable and the movement slow.

name: Band chest fly
form_cues: Anchor the band behind you at chest height.; Keep a slight bend in the elbows.; Hug your arms together in front of your chest.
common_mistakes: Bending elbows into a press; Letting arms travel too far back
safety: Avoid overstretching the front of the shoulder.

name: Band chest press
form_cues: Anchor the band at chest height behind you.; Stagger your stance and brace your core.; Press straight forward until arms are long, then return slowly.
common_mistakes: Shrugging shoulders toward ears; Letting the band snap back
safety: Secure the anchor point firmly so the band can't slip free.

name: Banded push-up
form_cues: Loop a band across your upper back, ends under your hands.; Do a normal push-up against the band's pull.; Lock out hard at the top where tension is highest.
common_mistakes: Band slipping off the shoulders; Losing body line
safety: Check the band for damage before each use.

name: Dumbbell floor fly
form_cues: Lie on the floor with a soft bend in your elbows.; Open your arms wide until elbows lightly touch the floor.; Hug the weights back up over your chest.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows into a press; Going too heavy
safety: Use light weights and keep the elbow bend fixed.
notes: The floor stops the stretch, so it is safer than a bench fly for beginners.

name: Dumbbell floor press
form_cues: Lie on your back, knees bent, dumbbells over your chest.; Lower until your upper arms touch the floor, then pause.; Press straight up and squeeze your chest at the top.
common_mistakes: Bouncing the elbows off the floor; Flaring elbows out to 90°
safety: Lay the dumbbells down at your sides, don't drop them over your face.
notes: Great no-bench option; the shorter range is kind to cranky shoulders.

name: Kettlebell floor press
form_cues: Lie on the floor, upper arm resting on the ground.; Press the bell up over your shoulder.; Lower until the elbow lightly touches the floor.
common_mistakes: Bouncing the elbow off the floor; Wrist bent backward
safety: Roll the bell into position from your side rather than lifting it overhead.
notes: Can also be done with two bells.

name: Medicine ball push-up
form_cues: Place one hand on the ball, the other on the floor.; Lower with control, keeping hips square.; Press up and switch the ball to the other hand.
common_mistakes: Ball rolling away; Twisting the hips
safety: Use a non-bouncing ball and keep the wrist stacked over it.

name: Weighted vest push-up
form_cues: Tighten the vest so the load sits high on the chest.; Keep a straight line from head to heels.; Lower until the chest nearly touches, then press up.
common_mistakes: Hips sagging under the extra load; Elbows flaring wide
safety: Add load gradually; reduce it if your lower back sags.
notes: Log vest weight as added kg.

name: Band lat pulldown
form_cues: Anchor the band high and kneel facing it.; Pull elbows down toward your back pockets.; Keep chest tall and return slowly.
common_mistakes: Pulling with the arms only; Rounding forward
safety: Double-check the high anchor is secure before loading it.

name: Band seated row
form_cues: Sit tall with legs long and the band looped around your feet.; Pull handles to your lower ribs.; Squeeze shoulder blades together before releasing slowly.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back; Leaning back to cheat the pull
safety: Wrap the band securely around the feet so it can't slip off.

name: Band straight-arm pulldown
form_cues: Anchor the band high and hinge slightly.; Keep arms straight and sweep hands to your thighs.; Feel the lats squeeze, then return slowly.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows; Shrugging
safety: Secure the high anchor before loading it.

name: Bent-over dumbbell row
form_cues: Hinge forward with a flat back, weights hanging under your shoulders.; Row elbows back toward your hips.; Squeeze at the top, then lower all the way.
common_mistakes: Standing up as you row; Rounding the lower back
safety: Brace your abs; if your lower back fatigues, switch to a supported row.
aliases: Two-arm dumbbell row; DB bent-over row

name: Bent-over dumbbell trap-3 raise
form_cues: Hinge forward, one hand on a bench or thigh.; Raise a light dumbbell up and out at about 45°, thumb up.; Pull the shoulder blade down and back; lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Shrugging; Going too heavy
safety: Use 1–4 kg; it's a small muscle.
notes: Helps posture and shoulder blade control.

name: Dumbbell deadlift
form_cues: Stand with dumbbells at your sides or in front of your shins.; Push hips back and bend knees until weights reach mid-shin.; Stand up by driving through your feet and squeezing your glutes.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back; Letting the weights drift away from your legs
progressions: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift; Trap bar deadlift
safety: Keep your spine neutral and brace before every rep.

name: Dumbbell gorilla row
secondary_muscles: Rear delts; Biceps; Obliques; Lower back
form_cues: Stand wide, hinge forward, dumbbells on the floor between your feet.; Row one weight up while the other arm pushes into its dumbbell.; Lower and alternate sides.
common_mistakes: Twisting the torso; Rounding the back
safety: Keep your hips level and back flat throughout.
notes: Popular with kettlebells; dumbbells work just as well.

name: Dumbbell shrug
form_cues: Stand tall with heavy dumbbells at your sides.; Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears.; Hold one second, then lower fully.
common_mistakes: Rolling the shoulders; Bending the elbows
safety: Keep your neck neutral; don't jut your chin forward.
notes: Use straps if grip gives out before your traps.

name: Dumbbell suitcase deadlift
form_cues: Stand with one dumbbell at your side.; Hinge and bend knees to lower it beside your foot.; Stand up without leaning toward the weight.
common_mistakes: Tilting the shoulders toward the dumbbell; Rounding the back
safety: Stay square and stop if you can't keep your torso upright.
notes: Doubles as anti-lateral-flexion core training.

name: Kettlebell gorilla row
form_cues: Hinge over two bells placed between your feet.; Row one bell to your hip while pressing into the other.; Alternate sides without twisting the torso.
common_mistakes: Rotating the hips; Rounding the back
safety: Keep a flat back and hips high throughout.

name: Kettlebell high pull
form_cues: Start like a one-arm swing.; At the hip snap, pull the elbow back and high.; Let the bell return into the backswing.
common_mistakes: Pulling with the arm too early; Rounding the shoulders
safety: Keep the bell close to avoid hitting your face.
notes: A teaching step toward the snatch.

name: Kettlebell sumo deadlift high pull
form_cues: Take a wide stance, bell between your feet.; Drive up through the legs and hips.; Pull the bell to chin height, elbows high.
common_mistakes: Pulling with arms before hips extend; Rounding the back
safety: Avoid it if upright rows bother your shoulders.

name: Renegade row
form_cues: Get into a push-up position holding hex dumbbells, feet wide.; Row one dumbbell to your hip without twisting.; Set it down softly and alternate.
common_mistakes: Hips rotating; Feet too close together
safety: Use hex dumbbells so they can't roll and catch your wrists.
notes: Add a push-up between rows for a harder version.

name: Sandbag bent-over row
form_cues: Hinge forward with a flat back, holding the bag's handles.; Row the bag to your belly button.; Lower it slowly without losing your hinge.
common_mistakes: Standing up during the row; Rounding the back
safety: Keep the spine neutral and brace before each rep.

name: Sandbag clean
form_cues: Straddle the bag and grip the sides or handles.; Drive hips through to pop the bag up.; Drop under it and catch it on your forearms at the chest.
common_mistakes: Pulling with a rounded back; Curling the bag up with the arms
safety: Start light; awkward loads need a tight, neutral spine.

name: Arnold press
form_cues: Start with dumbbells at chin height, palms facing you.; Rotate palms forward as you press overhead.; Reverse the turn on the way down.
common_mistakes: Rushing the rotation; Arching the lower back
safety: Go lighter than your normal press; the rotation loads the shoulder more.
notes: Usually done seated on an upright bench; standing works too.

name: Band external rotation
form_cues: Anchor the band at elbow height.; Tuck the elbow at your side, a towel helps.; Rotate the forearm outward, keeping the elbow still.
common_mistakes: Elbow drifting away from the body; Using too strong a band
safety: Use a light band and stop if you feel pinching.

name: Band face pull
form_cues: Anchor the band at face height.; Pull the band toward your forehead, elbows high.; Finish with hands beside your ears, thumbs back.
common_mistakes: Elbows dropping below shoulders; Leaning back
safety: Keep it light and pain-free in the shoulder.

name: Band internal rotation
form_cues: Anchor the band at elbow height on your working side.; Keep the elbow tucked at 90 degrees.; Rotate the forearm in across your stomach.
common_mistakes: Twisting the torso; Letting the elbow lift
safety: Light resistance only; this is a control drill.

name: Band lateral raise
form_cues: Stand on the band with handles at your sides.; Raise arms out to shoulder height with soft elbows.; Lower slowly and keep shoulders away from ears.
common_mistakes: Shrugging the weight up; Raising above shoulder height
safety: Use a light band; the tension is highest at the top.

name: Band overhead press
form_cues: Stand on the band and hold handles at shoulder height.; Press straight up until arms are locked out.; Keep ribs down and glutes tight.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back; Pressing forward instead of up
safety: Stand squarely on the band so it can't slip out from underfoot.

name: Band pull-apart
tags: Home-friendly; Isolation; Rehab; Shoulders; Strength; Warm-up
form_cues: Hold the band at shoulder height with straight arms.; Pull the band apart until it touches your chest.; Squeeze shoulder blades together, then return slowly.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows too much; Arching the lower back
safety: Use a light band; this should never pinch the front of the shoulder.
notes: Great as a warm-up before pressing.

name: Band upright row
form_cues: Stand on the band, hands shoulder-width.; Lead with the elbows up to chest height.; Lower slowly and keep the bar path close.
common_mistakes: Pulling hands above chest; Narrow grip that pinches shoulders
safety: Stop below shoulder height if you feel a pinch.

name: Bent-over dumbbell reverse fly
form_cues: Hinge forward until your chest is nearly parallel to the floor.; With soft elbows, raise the weights out wide.; Pause, then lower without letting your torso bob.
common_mistakes: Using the back to swing the weights; Squeezing the shoulder blades instead of moving the arms
safety: Keep a flat back and brace; sit down on a bench if your lower back tires.
aliases: Bent-over rear delt raise; Rear delt fly

name: Bottoms-up kettlebell press
form_cues: Hold the bell upside down, crushing the handle.; Keep the wrist straight and bell balanced.; Press slowly straight up and lower with control.
common_mistakes: Loose grip causing the bell to tip; Pressing too fast
safety: Use a light bell; it can tip suddenly, so keep your head out of its path.

name: Dumbbell Cuban press
form_cues: Upright-row light dumbbells until elbows reach shoulder height.; Rotate forearms up so your hands are over your elbows.; Press overhead, then reverse each step.
common_mistakes: Going too heavy; Dropping elbows during the rotation
safety: Use very light weights; this is a shoulder-health drill, not a strength test.

name: Dumbbell front raise
form_cues: Hold dumbbells in front of your thighs, palms down.; Raise to eye level with straight but soft arms.; Lower slowly without swinging back.
common_mistakes: Leaning back to lift the weight; Raising far above head height
safety: Keep it light; front delts already get lots of work from pressing.
notes: Alternate arms or use a neutral grip if your shoulders feel pinchy.

name: Dumbbell lateral raise
form_cues: Stand tall with a slight bend in your elbows.; Raise the weights out to the sides to shoulder height.; Lower slowly over two to three seconds.
common_mistakes: Swinging the body for momentum; Shrugging the shoulders up
progressions: Leaning single-arm lateral raise; Cable lateral raise
safety: Stop at shoulder height if you get any pinching.

name: Dumbbell Lu raise
form_cues: Hold light dumbbells at your sides, thumbs up.; Raise straight-armed out to the side and keep going overhead.; Lower slowly along the same path.
common_mistakes: Going too heavy; Bending the elbows
safety: Only take it overhead if you can do so without pain.
notes: Named after Olympic lifter Lu Xiaojun; works the top range of the shoulder.

name: Dumbbell rear delt row
form_cues: Hinge forward with palms facing your legs or behind you.; Row with elbows flared out wide, about 70–90°.; Pull until upper arms line up with your torso.
common_mistakes: Pulling elbows to the hips like a lat row; Going too heavy
safety: Keep a neutral spine and brace your core.

name: Dumbbell scaption raise
form_cues: Stand with thumbs pointing up.; Raise arms in a Y shape, about 30° in front of your sides.; Stop at shoulder height and lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Shrugging; Lifting straight out to the side
safety: Keep it light and pain-free.
notes: Often used in shoulder rehab; the angle matches how the shoulder blade sits.

name: Dumbbell upright row
form_cues: Hold dumbbells in front of your thighs.; Lead with your elbows and lift to lower-chest height.; Lower under control.
common_mistakes: Pulling higher than shoulder height; Shrugging instead of lifting with the elbows
safety: Stop below shoulder height if you feel a pinch in the front of the shoulder.
notes: Dumbbells let your hands move freely, which is easier on the wrists than a bar.

name: Dumbbell Z press
form_cues: Sit on the floor with legs straight out in front.; Sit tall without leaning back, dumbbells at shoulders.; Press overhead and lower with control.
common_mistakes: Rounding or leaning back; Going too heavy
safety: If tight hamstrings round your back, bend your knees slightly or sit on a plate.
notes: Named after strongman Zydrunas Savickas; exposes weak core and mobility.

name: Half-kneeling single-arm dumbbell press
form_cues: Kneel with the same-side knee down as the pressing arm.; Squeeze the down-side glute and stay tall.; Press up slightly in front of your head, then lower.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back; Shifting the hips sideways
safety: Pad the down knee with a mat or folded towel.
notes: The kneeling stance stops you cheating with the lower back.

name: Kettlebell bent press
form_cues: Rack the bell and push the hip out to the side.; Lean under the bell while the arm stays vertical.; Stand up beneath the locked arm.
common_mistakes: Pressing the bell up instead of getting under it; Losing sight of the bell
safety: An advanced lift: learn it light and with coaching.
notes: Old-time strongman lift.

name: Kettlebell clean and press
form_cues: Clean the bell to the rack.; Pause, brace, and press overhead.; Lower to rack, then let it swing back for the next clean.
common_mistakes: Leaning back on the press; Banging the forearm on the clean
safety: Keep the core braced throughout.

name: Kettlebell halo
form_cues: Hold the bell upside down by the horns.; Circle it closely around your head.; Keep ribs down and hips still.
common_mistakes: Arching the back; Circling too far from the head
safety: Use a light bell and move slowly to avoid knocking your head.
notes: Great shoulder warm-up before pressing.

name: Kettlebell jerk
form_cues: Dip and drive to launch the bell.; Drop under it with a second dip to lock out.; Stand tall with the arm locked before lowering.
common_mistakes: Pressing out the lockout; Rushing the second dip
safety: Requires solid overhead mobility and wrist position.
notes: A staple of kettlebell sport.

name: Kettlebell overhead carry
form_cues: Press the bell overhead and lock the arm.; Keep the biceps by your ear while you walk.; Stay tall; don't lean away from the bell.
common_mistakes: Bent elbow; Arching the lower back
safety: Only carry overhead with full, pain-free shoulder mobility.

name: Kettlebell overhead press
form_cues: Start with the bell in the rack, forearm vertical.; Squeeze glutes and grip, then press straight up.; Finish with biceps by your ear, then lower to rack.
common_mistakes: Leaning back to finish; Flaring the elbow early
progressions: Kettlebell push press; Bottoms-up kettlebell press
safety: Brace hard and don't press through shoulder pain.
aliases: Single-arm kettlebell press; KB military press

name: Kettlebell push press
form_cues: Dip a few centimetres by bending the knees.; Drive up with the legs to launch the bell.; Finish the lockout with the arm.
common_mistakes: Dipping too deep; Pressing before the legs finish
safety: Keep heels down in the dip and control the bell back to the rack.

name: Kettlebell snatch
form_cues: Swing back and drive hips explosively.; Keep the bell close and punch through at the top.; Lock out overhead with biceps by your ear.
common_mistakes: Letting the bell flop onto the wrist; Pressing it up instead of hip drive
regressions: One-arm kettlebell swing; Kettlebell high pull
safety: Needs good overhead mobility; drop the bell safely if control is lost.

name: Kettlebell windmill
form_cues: Lock the bell overhead, feet angled away from it.; Push the hip out and slide your free hand down the leg.; Keep eyes on the bell and the arm vertical.
common_mistakes: Bending the overhead arm; Twisting the chest down to the floor
safety: Start light; stop if the shoulder feels unstable.

name: Leaning single-arm lateral raise
form_cues: Hold a post and lean away with your arm straight.; Raise the dumbbell out to the side to shoulder height.; Lower slowly and keep the lean steady.
common_mistakes: Turning it into an upright row; Swinging
safety: Hold something solid that will not move when you lean on it.
notes: The lean keeps tension on the side delt at the bottom of the rep.

name: Sandbag overhead press
form_cues: Clean the bag to your chest.; Brace and press it straight overhead.; Lower it back to the chest under control.
common_mistakes: Leaning back; Bag rolling forward overhead
safety: Use handles if available; loose sand shifts mid-rep.

name: Side-lying dumbbell external rotation
form_cues: Lie on your side, top elbow bent 90° and pinned to your ribs.; Rotate the forearm up toward the ceiling.; Lower slowly without the elbow lifting off your side.
common_mistakes: Letting the elbow leave the body; Using too heavy a weight
safety: Start with 1–3 kg; stop if you feel sharp pain.
notes: A rolled towel under the elbow helps keep good position.

name: Single-arm dumbbell overhead press
form_cues: Stand tall with one dumbbell at your shoulder.; Brace your abs and press straight up without leaning.; Lower slowly back to the shoulder.
common_mistakes: Leaning away from the weight; Flaring the ribs
safety: Keep the free hand on your belly to feel your abs stay tight.

name: Standing dumbbell shoulder press
form_cues: Stand tall, dumbbells at shoulder height, palms forward.; Squeeze glutes and abs, then press straight overhead.; Lower with control back to your shoulders.
common_mistakes: Leaning back to finish the rep; Pressing the weights forward instead of up
safety: Keep your ribs down so your lower back doesn't arch.
aliases: Standing DB overhead press; Dumbbell military press

name: Turkish get-up
form_cues: Keep eyes on the bell and arm locked the whole time.; Move step by step: roll, elbow, hand, bridge, sweep, stand.; Reverse each step slowly to return to the floor.
common_mistakes: Bending the bell arm; Rushing transitions
safety: Practise with a shoe or no weight first; never lose sight of the bell.
notes: Builds shoulder stability through the whole body.

name: Band curl
form_cues: Stand on the band with feet hip-width apart.; Keep elbows pinned to your sides as you curl.; Lower slowly against the band's pull.
common_mistakes: Swinging the torso to finish reps; Letting elbows drift forward
safety: Check the band for nicks or tears before every session.
notes: Widen your stance to make it harder.

name: Band overhead triceps extension
form_cues: Anchor the band low behind you, hands overhead.; Keep elbows pointing up and close to your head.; Straighten arms fully, then lower with control.
common_mistakes: Elbows flaring wide; Arching the back
safety: Make sure the band is secure behind you before loading it.

name: Band pushdown
form_cues: Anchor the band high, over a door or bar.; Keep elbows tucked at your sides.; Push down until arms are straight, then control the return.
common_mistakes: Elbows flaring out; Leaning over to push with body weight
safety: Make sure the door is closed and locked if using a door anchor.

name: Concentration curl
form_cues: Sit with your elbow braced on your inner thigh.; Curl the weight toward your shoulder.; Squeeze, then lower to full extension.
common_mistakes: Lifting the elbow off the thigh; Leaning back
safety: Use a stable seat; any bench or chair works.

name: Cross-body hammer curl
form_cues: Hold dumbbells with thumbs up.; Curl one weight across your body toward the opposite shoulder.; Lower slowly and alternate.
common_mistakes: Twisting the torso; Lifting the elbow forward
safety: Keep the shoulder still; only the forearm moves.

name: Dumbbell curl
form_cues: Stand tall, elbows tucked at your sides, palms forward.; Curl up and squeeze at the top.; Lower slowly until your arms are fully straight.
common_mistakes: Swinging the torso; Letting elbows drift forward
progressions: Incline dumbbell curl; Dumbbell spider curl
safety: Keep wrists neutral; drop the weight if you have to swing it.
aliases: Standing DB curl; Alternating dumbbell curl
notes: Curl both arms together or alternate them.

name: Dumbbell pinch hold
form_cues: Grab a hex dumbbell by one end with fingers and thumb only.; Stand and hold it at your side.; Squeeze hard until time is up.
common_mistakes: Letting the palm touch; Holding over your feet
safety: Hold it beside your foot, not over it, in case it slips.
aliases: Dumbbell head pinch; Hex dumbbell pinch grip
notes: Pinching two plates together is a common alternative.

name: Dumbbell pronation and supination
form_cues: Rest your forearm on your thigh, hold one end of a dumbbell.; Slowly rotate palm up, then palm down.; Keep the forearm still the whole time.
common_mistakes: Moving the elbow; Using a weight that's too heavy
safety: Holding further from the end makes it harder; start close.
notes: A hammer works if you don't have a light dumbbell.

name: Dumbbell reverse curl
form_cues: Hold dumbbells with palms facing down.; Curl up keeping wrists straight.; Lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Letting wrists drop; Swinging
safety: Go light; the overhand grip limits the load.

name: Dumbbell triceps kickback
form_cues: Hinge forward and pin upper arms by your sides.; Straighten your elbows to push the weights back.; Pause at full lockout, then lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Swinging the upper arm; Not reaching full lockout
safety: Keep your back flat; support one hand on a bench if needed.
notes: Can be done one arm at a time with a hand on a bench.

name: Dumbbell waiter curl
form_cues: Cup one end of a dumbbell in both palms, like a tray.; Curl it up keeping elbows by your sides.; Lower slowly without the dumbbell tipping.
common_mistakes: Swinging; Letting elbows flare
safety: Hold the dumbbell securely so it can't slip out.
notes: Keeps the biceps under tension at the top.

name: Finger extension with band
form_cues: Loop a band around all fingers and the thumb.; Spread fingers wide against the band.; Return slowly and repeat.
common_mistakes: Using too thick a band; Moving through a tiny range
safety: Ease off if you feel joint pain.
notes: Balances out gripper and climbing work; helps keep elbows healthy.

name: Hammer curl
form_cues: Hold dumbbells with palms facing each other.; Curl up keeping thumbs on top.; Lower under control to full extension.
common_mistakes: Swinging; Letting the wrists bend
safety: Keep elbows pinned to your sides.

name: Hand gripper squeeze
form_cues: Set the gripper deep in the palm.; Squeeze until the handles touch.; Hold the close for a second, then open slowly.
common_mistakes: Gripper set too high in the fingers; Rushing reps with no full close
safety: Build up gradually; overuse can irritate finger tendons.
aliases: Gripper close; Captains of Crush gripper
notes: Hold for time at the close for crush endurance.

name: Overhead dumbbell extension
form_cues: Hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands under the top plate.; Lower it behind your head, elbows pointing up.; Straighten your arms fully at the top.
common_mistakes: Elbows flaring wide; Arching the lower back
safety: Sit down with back support if your lower back arches.
aliases: Two-hand overhead DB extension; Seated dumbbell French press

name: Reverse wrist curl
form_cues: Rest forearms on your thighs, palms down, wrists off the edge.; Lift the backs of your hands toward the ceiling.; Lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Going too heavy; Moving the forearm
safety: Very light weights are enough; this can help with tennis elbow rehab.

name: Single-arm overhead dumbbell extension
form_cues: Hold a dumbbell overhead, arm straight.; Lower it behind your head, elbow pointing up.; Extend back up; support the elbow with your free hand if needed.
common_mistakes: Elbow drifting out; Going too heavy
safety: Lower slowly to protect the elbow.

name: Thick-grip dumbbell curl
form_cues: Fit the thick grips and hold the dumbbells hard.; Curl up with elbows pinned to your sides.; Lower slowly without losing your crush grip.
common_mistakes: Swinging; Wrists curling back
safety: Use about 20–30% less weight than your normal curl.

name: Thick-grip dumbbell hold
form_cues: Fit thick grips over the handles.; Deadlift the dumbbells and stand tall.; Crush the handles and hold for time.
common_mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders; Letting the thumb slip
safety: Set the dumbbells down before your grip fully fails.

name: Wrist curl
form_cues: Rest forearms on your thighs or a bench, palms up, wrists off the edge.; Let the dumbbells roll down toward your fingers.; Curl your wrists up as high as you can.
common_mistakes: Lifting the forearms; Bouncing
safety: Use light weights and smooth reps.
aliases: Dumbbell wrist curl; Seated wrist curl

name: Wrist roller
form_cues: Hold the roller at shoulder height with straight arms.; Roll the weight all the way up, one hand at a time.; Unroll slowly under control; don't let it drop.
common_mistakes: Letting arms drop to waist height; Spinning the weight down quickly
safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain at the elbow (tennis-elbow area).
notes: Roll overhand for extensors and underhand for flexors.

name: Zottman curl
form_cues: Curl up with palms facing up.; At the top, turn palms down.; Lower slowly with palms down, then turn back at the bottom.
common_mistakes: Rushing the lowering phase; Using a weight too heavy for the palms-down part
safety: Pick a weight you can control on the way down.
notes: Trains biceps up and forearms on the way down.

name: Band deadlift
form_cues: Stand on the band and hinge to grab the handles.; Keep a flat back and push hips back.; Stand up by driving hips forward.
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back; Squatting instead of hinging
safety: Keep the band centred under both feet.

name: Band good morning
form_cues: Stand on the band and loop it behind your neck.; Hinge forward with soft knees and a flat back.; Squeeze glutes to return upright.
common_mistakes: Rounding the spine; Bending knees too much
safety: Pad the band across the upper back, not the neck.

name: Band hamstring curl
form_cues: Lie face down with the band anchored low behind you.; Loop it around your ankles and curl heels to glutes.; Lower slowly without lifting hips.
common_mistakes: Hips lifting off the floor; Letting the band snap back
safety: Anchor the band firmly to something heavy and low.

name: Band squat
form_cues: Stand on the band, handles at shoulders.; Sit hips back and down, knees tracking toes.; Drive through the whole foot to stand tall.
common_mistakes: Knees caving in; Heels lifting
safety: Keep the band under the mid-foot so it can't fly out.

name: Box step-up
equipment: Plyo box or sturdy bench; Dumbbells (optional)
form_cues: Put your whole foot on the box.; Drive up through the front heel, not the back toe.; Step down slowly under control.
common_mistakes: Pushing off the back foot; Knee caving inward; Box too high for your hip mobility
progressions: Dumbbell step-up; Barbell step-up; Lateral step-up
safety: Use a stable box that can't slide; start with knee height or lower.
notes: Hold dumbbells at your sides to add load.

name: Double kettlebell front squat
form_cues: Clean both bells to the rack, elbows tucked.; Squat to depth keeping the chest up.; Drive up without letting the bells pull you forward.
common_mistakes: Elbows flaring and chest dropping; Knees caving
safety: Clean the bells into position carefully; set them down rather than drop them.

name: Double kettlebell Romanian deadlift
form_cues: Hold a bell in each hand at your thighs.; Push hips back with soft knees until hamstrings stretch.; Squeeze glutes to stand up.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back; Bending knees too much
safety: Keep bells close to the legs throughout.

name: Dumbbell calf raise
form_cues: Hold dumbbells at your sides, balls of feet on a step.; Lower heels for a deep stretch.; Rise as high as you can and pause.
common_mistakes: Bouncing; Bending the knees
safety: Hold a rail with one hand if balance is an issue.
notes: Works fine on flat floor if you have no step.

name: Dumbbell cossack squat
form_cues: Stand very wide holding a dumbbell at your chest.; Sit down over one leg while the other stays straight, toes up.; Push back to the middle and switch sides.
common_mistakes: Heel of the bent leg lifting; Rounding the back
safety: Only go as deep as your hips allow without pain.
notes: Great for adductor strength and hip mobility.

name: Dumbbell deficit reverse lunge
form_cues: Stand on a low step holding dumbbells.; Step back off it and sink deep.; Drive through the front foot to step back up.
common_mistakes: Using too high a step; Wobbly front knee
safety: Use a stable step no higher than about 10 cm.
notes: The extra depth stretches the glutes more than a normal lunge.

name: Dumbbell forward lunge
form_cues: Stand tall, dumbbells at your sides.; Step forward and lower until both knees bend about 90°.; Push off the front foot back to standing.
common_mistakes: Front knee caving inward; Stepping too short
safety: Step far enough that your front heel stays down.

name: Dumbbell front squat
form_cues: Rest one end of each dumbbell on your shoulders, elbows high.; Squat down keeping your torso upright.; Drive up without letting the elbows drop.
common_mistakes: Elbows dropping; Rounding the upper back
safety: Brace hard; the weight sits on your shoulders, so keep a tight upper back.

name: Dumbbell lateral lunge
form_cues: Hold a dumbbell at your chest.; Step wide to the side and sit back into that hip.; Keep the other leg straight, then push back to centre.
common_mistakes: Knee caving inward; Heel lifting
safety: Keep toes pointing forward or slightly out.

name: Dumbbell overhead walking lunge
form_cues: Press dumbbells overhead and lock your arms.; Walk forward in lunges keeping your arms vertical.; Keep ribs down and steps controlled.
common_mistakes: Arms drifting forward; Arching the back
safety: Use light weights; lower them with control if you lose position.
notes: Single-arm overhead version is a common CrossFit option.

name: Dumbbell reverse lunge
form_cues: Stand tall, dumbbells at your sides.; Step back and lower your back knee toward the floor.; Drive through the front heel to return.
common_mistakes: Leaning forward too much; Landing on the back knee
safety: Easier on the knees than forward lunges.

name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
form_cues: Stand tall, soft knees, dumbbells in front of your thighs.; Push your hips back and slide the weights down your legs.; Stop at a deep hamstring stretch, then drive hips forward.
common_mistakes: Squatting the weight down; Rounding the back to go lower
progressions: Dumbbell B-stance Romanian deadlift; Barbell Romanian deadlift
safety: Only go as low as you can with a flat back.
notes: Strict stiff-leg version: knees nearly straight and weights to the floor.

name: Dumbbell split squat
form_cues: Stand in a long split stance with dumbbells at your sides.; Lower your back knee straight down toward the floor.; Drive through the front foot to come up; finish all reps then switch.
common_mistakes: Front heel lifting; Stance too short
safety: Pad the floor under your back knee if it touches.

name: Dumbbell squat
form_cues: Hold dumbbells at your sides, feet shoulder-width.; Squat down keeping your chest up and knees over toes.; Stand by pushing the floor away.
common_mistakes: Rounding forward; Knees caving in
safety: Keep the weights hanging straight; don't let them hit your knees.
aliases: Dumbbell squat at sides; DB suitcase squat

name: Dumbbell sumo squat
form_cues: Stand wide, toes turned out, one dumbbell hanging between your legs.; Push knees out and sit straight down.; Squeeze your glutes to stand up.
common_mistakes: Knees caving in; Leaning forward
safety: Stand on two plates or steps if you want the dumbbell to go deeper.

name: Dumbbell tiptoe farmer's walk
form_cues: Pick up dumbbells and rise onto the balls of your feet.; Walk with short steps without letting heels touch.; Stay tall and set the weights down with control.
common_mistakes: Heels dropping; Leaning forward
safety: Use moderate weights; rolling an ankle is the main risk.
aliases: Farmer's walk on toes; Calf walk

name: Dumbbell walking lunge
form_cues: Hold dumbbells at your sides and step forward into a lunge.; Lower the back knee close to the floor.; Drive forward into the next step without pausing upright.
common_mistakes: Knees caving in; Steps too short
safety: Make sure you have a clear path.

name: Goblet Cossack squat
form_cues: Take a very wide stance holding the bell at your chest.; Shift and sit deep into one hip, other leg straight.; Lift the straight-leg toes up and keep the heel down.
common_mistakes: Lifting the bent-leg heel; Rounding the back
safety: Work within your hip range; go only as deep as you can control.

name: Goblet reverse lunge
form_cues: Hold the bell at your chest.; Step back and lower the back knee softly.; Push through the front foot to return.
common_mistakes: Front knee caving; Stepping too short
safety: Use a support nearby if balance is an issue.

name: Goblet squat
form_cues: Hold one dumbbell vertically against your chest.; Sit down between your knees, chest tall.; Drive up through your whole foot.
common_mistakes: Heels lifting; Knees caving in
safety: Keep your heels down; stop if your knees hurt.
aliases: Dumbbell goblet squat; Kettlebell goblet squat

name: Heels-elevated dumbbell squat
form_cues: Put your heels on a wedge or small plate, feet close.; Hold dumbbells at your sides or one at your chest.; Sink straight down letting knees travel forward.
common_mistakes: Leaning forward; Bouncing out of the bottom
safety: Make sure the heel support can't slide out.
notes: Raised heels shift work to the quads; a weight plate is a handy wedge.

name: Kettlebell deadlift
form_cues: Stand with the bell between your feet.; Push hips back and grip it with a flat back.; Stand tall by driving hips forward.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back; Squatting the weight up
safety: Keep the bell close to you and the spine neutral.
notes: Teaches the hinge before learning swings.

name: Kettlebell thruster
form_cues: Squat with the bell(s) in the rack.; Drive up out of the squat.; Use that momentum to press overhead.
common_mistakes: Pressing before standing; Chest dropping in the squat
safety: Keep heels down and lower the bells back to the rack under control.

name: Medicine ball lunge with twist
form_cues: Hold the ball at chest height, arms extended.; Lunge forward, then rotate toward the front leg.; Turn back to centre before standing up.
common_mistakes: Front knee drifting inward when you rotate; Rushing the twist
safety: Rotate through the upper back, not the knee.

name: Medicine ball overhead lunge
form_cues: Hold the ball overhead with arms locked.; Step forward and lower the back knee.; Keep ribs down; don't let the ball drift forward.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back; Elbows bending
safety: Skip the overhead hold if your shoulders lack mobility.

name: Medicine ball squat to press
form_cues: Hold the ball at your chest and squat.; Stand up and press the ball overhead.; Lower it to your chest as you sit back down.
common_mistakes: Heels lifting; Arching the back overhead
safety: Control the ball overhead; don't release or throw it.

name: Sandbag bear-hug squat
form_cues: Hug the bag tight to your chest.; Sit down between your knees.; Stand up without letting the bag pull you forward.
common_mistakes: Rounding forward; Heels lifting
safety: Keep the bag close to reduce strain on the lower back.

name: Sandbag Zercher squat
form_cues: Cradle the bag in the crooks of your elbows.; Squat deep while keeping the chest up.; Drive up through the whole foot.
common_mistakes: Upper back rounding; Bag sliding toward the wrists
safety: Keep elbows high and the load tight to your body.

name: Single-arm dumbbell overhead squat
form_cues: Press one dumbbell overhead and lock the arm.; Squat down keeping the arm vertical and eyes forward.; Stand up without the weight drifting.
common_mistakes: Bent arm; Torso twisting
safety: Practise with no weight first; it needs good shoulder mobility.

name: Single-leg dumbbell calf raise
form_cues: Stand on one foot on a step, dumbbell in the same-side hand.; Lower the heel slowly below the step.; Push up as high as possible and pause.
common_mistakes: Rushing the reps; Using the free hand to pull up
safety: Lightly hold a wall for balance only.

name: Weighted vest walking lunge
form_cues: Fit the vest snugly so it doesn't bounce.; Take a long step and lower the back knee softly.; Drive through the front heel into the next step.
common_mistakes: Front knee caving; Leaning forward under the vest
safety: Start with a light vest (around 5–10% of body weight).
notes: Log the vest weight as added kg.

name: American kettlebell swing
form_cues: Swing as normal but carry the bell to overhead.; Finish with biceps by ears, bell bottom up.; Keep ribs down; don't arch to reach overhead.
common_mistakes: Hyperextending the lower back; Pulling with the arms
safety: Skip it if you lack full overhead shoulder mobility.
notes: Common in CrossFit; the Russian swing is safer for most people.

name: Band glute kickback
form_cues: Loop the band around one ankle and anchor it low.; Kick the leg back from the hip, knee slightly bent.; Squeeze the glute without arching your back.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back; Swinging the leg
safety: Hold a support to stay balanced.

name: Banded clamshell
form_cues: Lie on your side, knees bent, band above knees.; Keep feet together and open the top knee.; Hold briefly at the top, then lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Rolling the hips backward; Rushing the reps
safety: Move only through a pain-free range.

name: Banded glute bridge
form_cues: Lie on your back with the mini band above your knees.; Press knees out against the band.; Drive hips up and squeeze glutes at the top.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back at the top; Letting knees cave
safety: Keep ribs down to protect the lower back.

name: Banded lateral walk
form_cues: Place the mini band above the knees or around the ankles.; Sit into a quarter squat with chest up.; Step sideways, keeping tension on the band.
common_mistakes: Letting knees cave inward; Standing up tall between steps
safety: Keep the band flat on the skin so it doesn't roll and pinch.
aliases: Mini-band side walk; Lateral band walk
notes: Band around ankles or feet is harder than above the knees.

name: Dumbbell B-stance Romanian deadlift
form_cues: Put most weight on the front leg, back toes lightly down beside its heel.; Hinge hips back with a flat back.; Drive through the front heel to stand tall.
common_mistakes: Pushing off the back foot; Rotating the hips open
safety: Keep the back foot as a kickstand for balance only.
notes: Bridge between two-leg and single-leg RDLs.

name: Dumbbell curtsy lunge
form_cues: Hold dumbbells at your sides or one at your chest.; Step one leg diagonally behind the other, like a curtsy.; Lower, then drive through the front heel to return.
common_mistakes: Twisting the hips too much; Front knee collapsing
safety: Stop short of any knee discomfort; it's a twisting angle.

name: Dumbbell frog pump
form_cues: Lie down, soles of the feet together, knees out wide.; Rest a dumbbell on your hips.; Drive your hips up fast and squeeze, then lower.
common_mistakes: Arching the back; Heels sliding away
safety: Keep reps smooth; stop if your hips feel pinchy.
notes: A high-rep glute burnout.

name: Dumbbell glute bridge
form_cues: Lie on your back, knees bent, dumbbell resting on your hip crease.; Drive through your heels and lift your hips.; Squeeze your glutes hard at the top, then lower.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back at the top; Pushing through the toes
safety: Hold the dumbbell with both hands and pad it with a towel.

name: Dumbbell sumo deadlift
form_cues: Stand wide, toes out, one dumbbell on end between your feet.; Sit hips back and grab the handle with a flat back.; Push the floor apart to stand up, squeezing glutes.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back; Knees caving in
safety: Stand on two plates if the dumbbell is too low to reach with a flat back.

name: Kettlebell clean
form_cues: Hike the bell back, then drive hips forward.; Keep the elbow close and zip the bell up.; Catch it softly in the rack, wrist straight.
common_mistakes: Bell flipping over and banging the forearm; Casting the bell wide
safety: Learn with a light bell; a bruised forearm means the path is too wide.

name: Kettlebell swing
tags: Compound; Endurance; Glutes; Home-friendly; Power; Strength
form_cues: Hike the bell back high between your thighs.; Snap hips forward and squeeze glutes hard.; Let the bell float to chest height; arms stay relaxed.
common_mistakes: Squatting the swing instead of hinging; Lifting with the arms; Rounding the back
safety: Clear the space around you and keep a neutral spine throughout.

name: Monster walk
form_cues: Band around ankles, sit into a quarter squat.; Step diagonally forward and out with each foot.; Keep constant tension; don't let feet come together.
common_mistakes: Knees caving in; Standing too upright
safety: Keep the band flat so it doesn't roll.

name: One-arm kettlebell swing
form_cues: Grip the handle with one hand, free arm relaxed.; Keep shoulders square; resist the twist.; Drive with hips and let the bell float.
common_mistakes: Rotating the torso; Shrugging the working shoulder
safety: Start lighter than your two-hand swing weight.

name: Seated banded hip abduction
form_cues: Sit on the edge of a bench, band above knees.; Push knees out as far as you can.; Hold a second, then return with control.
common_mistakes: Using momentum; Letting feet come off the floor
safety: Keep the band flat on the thighs.

name: Single-leg dumbbell glute bridge
form_cues: Lie down, one foot planted, other leg lifted, dumbbell on the working hip.; Push through the planted heel to raise your hips.; Keep the hips level as you lower.
common_mistakes: Hips tilting; Arching the back
safety: Hold the dumbbell steady with your hand so it can't roll.

name: Single-leg Romanian deadlift
secondary_muscles: Lower back; Adductors; Foot and ankle stabilisers
form_cues: Stand on one leg with a soft knee, weight in the opposite hand.; Hinge forward as your free leg reaches straight back.; Keep hips square and return to standing.
common_mistakes: Opening the hip toward the ceiling; Rounding the back
safety: Use a wall or rack with your free hand if balance is shaky.

name: Farmer's carry
form_cues: Pick up heavy dumbbells with a flat back.; Stand tall, shoulders down, and walk with short steps.; Set them down with control at the end.
common_mistakes: Leaning or swaying; Shrugging up
safety: Clear your path and deadlift the weights down, don't drop them.
notes: Track the weight per hand; distance or time goes in the reps.

name: Kettlebell front rack carry
form_cues: Clean two bells to the rack.; Walk tall with ribs down and short steps.; Breathe behind the brace.
common_mistakes: Leaning back; Elbows flaring
safety: Set the bells down with a controlled hinge.
notes: Track distance in metres; one-bell version trains anti-side-bend.

name: Barbell bench press
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Flat bench
form_cues: Eyes under the bar, shoulder blades pinched, feet planted; Lower the bar to your mid-chest with elbows at about 45°; Press up and slightly back over your shoulders
common_mistakes: Bouncing the bar off the chest; Flaring elbows to 90°; Lifting hips off the bench
regressions: Push-ups; Flat dumbbell press; Smith machine bench press
safety: Use a spotter or safety arms; never use a thumbless grip.

name: Barbell floor press
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Squat rack
form_cues: Lie under the bar in a rack with knees bent; Lower until your upper arms rest on the floor; Pause, then press back to lockout
common_mistakes: Slamming elbows into the floor; Bouncing out of the bottom; Flared elbows
safety: Set rack pins low enough to unrack, and use safeties.
notes: Shoulder-friendly; good lockout builder.

name: Cable crossover fly
form_cues: Set pulleys high and take a staggered stance.; Keep a soft bend in the elbows throughout.; Sweep hands down and together in a hugging arc.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows and turning it into a press.; Letting the handles yank the shoulders back at the top.
safety: Use a weight you can control at the stretch to protect the shoulder joint.
aliases: High-to-low cable fly; Standing cable fly; Cable crossover
notes: High-to-low angle biases the lower chest.

name: Decline bench press
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Decline bench
form_cues: Lock your legs under the pads; Lower the bar to your lower chest; Press straight up over your shoulders
common_mistakes: Bouncing the bar; Bar drifting toward the face; Flaring elbows
safety: Always use a spotter; it's hard to bail out of a decline press.

name: Decline cable fly
equipment: Cable machine; Decline bench; Single handles
form_cues: Set a decline bench between low pulleys.; Lock in your feet before taking the handles.; Sweep the handles together over the lower chest.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows too much.; Letting the head hang off the bench.
safety: Avoid if lying head-down makes you dizzy or you have high blood pressure.
notes: High-to-low standing fly is an easier substitute.

name: Decline dumbbell fly
form_cues: Secure your feet and lie back on a decline bench.; Open arms wide with soft elbows.; Bring the weights back together over your lower chest.
common_mistakes: Bending elbows too much; Dropping too low
safety: Sit up carefully at the end with the weights held close to your chest.

name: Decline dumbbell press
form_cues: Hook your feet under the pads and lie back.; Lower the dumbbells to your lower chest.; Press up and slightly in.
common_mistakes: Rushing the descent; Letting the weights drift over your face
safety: Have a partner hand you the dumbbells, or start with them on your thighs.
notes: Some adjustable benches decline; otherwise use a fixed decline bench.

name: Dumbbell fly
form_cues: Soft bend in the elbows, locked in.; Open wide until you feel a chest stretch.; Hug the weights back up over your chest.
common_mistakes: Bending elbows into a press; Lowering too far
safety: Go light; this is a stretch move.

name: Dumbbell pullover
form_cues: Lie on a bench holding one dumbbell over your chest with both hands.; With slightly bent elbows, lower it back behind your head.; Pull it back over your chest using chest and lats.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows like a triceps extension; Over-arching the lower back
safety: Grip the dumbbell securely and stop before your shoulders feel strained.
notes: Lying across the bench is the classic old-school version.

name: Dumbbell squeeze press
form_cues: Lie on a bench and press the dumbbells together over your chest.; Keep squeezing them together as you lower to your chest.; Press back up without letting them separate.
common_mistakes: Letting the dumbbells drift apart; Using too much weight
safety: Hex dumbbells are easiest to squeeze; keep wrists straight.

name: Flat bench cable fly
equipment: Cable machine; Flat bench; Single handles
form_cues: Lie on a bench between low pulleys.; Open the arms wide with soft elbows.; Hug the handles together over your chest.
common_mistakes: Dropping the hands too low below the bench.; Pressing instead of flying.
safety: Keep the stretch controlled to protect the shoulder.
notes: Keeps tension at the top, unlike dumbbell flies.

name: Flat bench cable press
equipment: Cable machine; Flat bench; Single handles
form_cues: Place the bench between low pulleys.; Press up and slightly together over the chest.; Lower until hands are level with your chest.
common_mistakes: Bench not centred so tension is uneven.; Bouncing at the bottom.
safety: Have handles in place before lying down so you don't twist to grab them.
aliases: Cable bench press; Lying cable press
notes: Constant tension compared to dumbbells.

name: Flat dumbbell press
form_cues: Lie back with feet flat and shoulder blades pinched together.; Lower the dumbbells to the sides of your chest, elbows about 45°.; Press up and slightly in until arms are straight.
common_mistakes: Flaring elbows to 90°; Clanking the weights at the top
progressions: Incline dumbbell press; Barbell bench press
safety: Kick the dumbbells up from your knees and lower them back to your knees when done.

name: Incline barbell press
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Incline bench
form_cues: Set the bench to 30–45°; Lower the bar to your upper chest; Press up over your shoulders, shoulder blades tucked
common_mistakes: Bench set too steep; Bar touching the neck; Hips coming off the seat
safety: Use a spotter or safeties; keep your back pinned to the pad.

name: Incline bench cable fly
equipment: Cable machine; Adjustable bench; Single handles
form_cues: Set the bench to about 30 degrees between low pulleys.; Keep a slight bend in the elbows.; Bring hands together over the upper chest.
common_mistakes: Bench too steep.; Letting elbows bend and press.
safety: Use moderate weight; deep stretch under load stresses the shoulder.

name: Incline bench cable press
equipment: Cable machine; Adjustable bench; Single handles
form_cues: Set the bench to 30–45 degrees between low pulleys.; Press up over the upper chest.; Keep shoulder blades pinned to the bench.
common_mistakes: Bench set too steep, turning it into a shoulder press.; Elbows flared to 90 degrees.
safety: Grab handles before reclining to avoid twisting under load.

name: Incline dumbbell fly
form_cues: Set the bench to 30° and hold dumbbells over your upper chest.; Open your arms wide with a fixed elbow bend.; Squeeze them back together over your chest.
common_mistakes: Turning it into a press; Going too deep
safety: Keep the weight light enough to control the stretch.

name: Incline dumbbell press
form_cues: Set the bench to about 30°, not steeper.; Lower to the upper chest with elbows slightly tucked.; Press up and slightly in, without clanking the dumbbells.
common_mistakes: Bench set too steep; Bouncing at the bottom
safety: Lower until you feel a chest stretch, never pain in the shoulder.

name: Kneeling cable crossover
form_cues: Kneel tall in the middle of the crossover.; Brace your core so the hips don't move.; Bring hands together in front of your belly button.
common_mistakes: Rocking the torso to cheat the weight.; Letting elbows drop too low.
safety: Use a mat under the knees.
notes: Kneeling removes leg drive and keeps the work strict.

name: Landmine squeeze press
form_cues: Hold the bar end with both palms pressed together; Squeeze your hands hard into the bar; Press up and out from your chest
common_mistakes: Losing the squeeze; Leaning back; Using the legs to push
safety: Keep the landmine anchored so it can't slide.

name: Low-to-high cable fly
form_cues: Set pulleys at the lowest notch.; Scoop the handles up to chin height.; Keep chest proud and elbows softly bent.
common_mistakes: Turning it into a front raise.; Arching the lower back to lift the weight.
safety: Keep the load light enough that the shoulders don't roll forward.
aliases: Low cable crossover; Upward cable fly; Incline cable fly (standing)
notes: Biases the upper (clavicular) chest.

name: Low-to-high cable press
form_cues: Set pulleys low and stand in a split stance.; Press up and out at about 30 degrees.; Finish with hands at eye level.
common_mistakes: Turning it into a shoulder press.; Arching the lower back.
safety: Keep ribs down to protect the lower back.
aliases: Incline standing cable press; Upward cable press

name: Mid-height cable fly
form_cues: Set pulleys at chest height.; Lead with the elbows, not the hands.; Squeeze the chest hard as the handles meet.
common_mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders up.; Using too much weight and losing the arc.
safety: Stop the stretch where the shoulders still feel stable.
aliases: Cable chest fly; Straight cable fly
notes: Targets the middle of the chest.

name: Multi-gym chest press
form_cues: Set the seat so handles line up with mid-chest.; Press forward smoothly until arms are nearly straight.; Control the weight back until you feel a chest stretch.
common_mistakes: Shrugging shoulders up to the ears.; Letting the stack slam between reps.
progressions: Seated chest press machine; Flat dumbbell press
safety: Adjust the seat before loading; keep the weight stack clear of hands and feet.
notes: Most home multi-gyms use a pulley-driven press arm; resistance may feel lighter than a commercial machine.

name: Multi-gym pec fly
form_cues: Keep a soft bend in the elbows throughout.; Squeeze the pads or handles together in front of your chest.; Open slowly until you feel a stretch, not a strain.
common_mistakes: Pushing with the hands instead of hugging with the arms.; Letting the arms travel too far back.
safety: Avoid overstretching the shoulders at the open position.
aliases: Home gym butterfly; Multi-gym pec deck

name: Neutral-grip dumbbell press
form_cues: Lie on a flat bench, palms facing each other.; Lower with elbows close to your sides.; Press straight up, keeping the dumbbells parallel.
common_mistakes: Letting elbows flare; Bouncing at the bottom
safety: A shoulder-friendly option if regular pressing aches.
notes: More triceps than the standard grip.

name: Pin press
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Squat rack; Flat bench
form_cues: Set pins just above your chest or at a sticking point; Get tight under the bar before every rep; Press explosively off the pins
common_mistakes: Losing tightness between reps; Bouncing off pins; Bench not centred in the rack
safety: Make sure the pins are level and the bench is centred.
aliases: Dead bench; Bench press from pins
notes: Builds strength from a dead stop.

name: Reverse-grip bench press
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Flat bench
form_cues: Take an underhand grip just outside shoulder-width; Lower the bar to your lower chest, elbows tucked; Press back toward your face in an arc
common_mistakes: Losing grip on the unrack; Too heavy too soon; Wrists bent back
safety: Always use a spotter for the hand-off; the grip is easy to lose.

name: Single-arm cable chest press
tags: Chest; Compound; Core; Hypertrophy; Strength; Unilateral
form_cues: Stand facing away with the handle at chest height.; Press forward without letting the torso twist.; Use the opposite leg forward for a stable base.
common_mistakes: Rotating the hips to push the weight.; Shrugging the pressing shoulder.
safety: Start light; the anti-rotation demand is bigger than it looks.
aliases: One-arm cable press; Unilateral cable press

name: Single-arm cable fly
form_cues: Stand side-on with the handle at shoulder height.; Sweep the arm across past the midline.; Keep hips and shoulders square.
common_mistakes: Rotating the torso to finish the rep.; Bending the elbow too much.
safety: Control the return so the shoulder isn't pulled into a deep stretch.
aliases: One-arm cable crossover; Unilateral cable fly
notes: Crossing past the midline gives a stronger peak contraction.

name: Single-arm dumbbell bench press
form_cues: Lie on a bench with one dumbbell, other hand on your belly.; Lower it to your chest without twisting.; Press up while keeping your hips and shoulders flat.
common_mistakes: Rolling toward the weight; Lifting the hips
safety: Start light; the unevenness takes getting used to.
notes: Doubles as anti-rotation core work.

name: Smith machine bench press
form_cues: Line the bar up with your mid-chest; Lower under control; Press up and lock out
common_mistakes: Bench misaligned; Bouncing; Flaring elbows
safety: Set safety stops above your chest.

name: Smith machine incline bench press
form_cues: Set the bench at 30–45°; Lower to your upper chest; Press straight up
common_mistakes: Bar touching the neck; Bench too steep; Bouncing
safety: Set safety stops.

name: Standing cable chest press
form_cues: Set pulleys at chest height and step forward.; Press the handles straight out and slightly together.; Brace your core so you don't lean.
common_mistakes: Leaning too far forward.; Flaring elbows straight out to the sides.
safety: Use a staggered stance for balance.
aliases: Cable chest press; Standing cable press

name: Suspension chest fly
form_cues: Lean forward, arms out front with soft elbows.; Open arms wide as you lower your chest.; Hug back together using your chest.
common_mistakes: Bending elbows into a press; Going too low and straining shoulders
safety: Start upright and only lean further once you control the bottom.

name: Suspension chest press
form_cues: Face away from the anchor, arms out in front.; Lower your chest between your hands in a plank.; Press back up without letting hips sag.
common_mistakes: Straps rubbing the arms; Hips sagging
safety: Lower your body angle gradually; the straps can swing if you lose control.

name: Wide-grip bench press
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Flat bench
form_cues: Grip about one-and-a-half times shoulder-width; Lower under control to mid-chest; Press up without letting shoulders roll forward
common_mistakes: Going wider than the rings allow; Bouncing the bar; Shoulders lifting off the bench
safety: Avoid if you have shoulder pain; stay within competition grip width (index finger on the rings).
notes: Shorter range and more chest emphasis than a standard grip.

name: Barbell bent-over row
form_cues: Hinge until your torso is about 45° or lower; Pull the bar to your lower ribs; Lower under control without standing up
common_mistakes: Standing up more each rep; Jerking with the hips; Rounding the back
safety: Keep your back flat; stop if your lower back fatigues first.

name: Barbell pullover
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Flat bench
form_cues: Lie on a bench holding the bar over your chest, elbows soft; Lower it back over your head in an arc; Pull it back over your chest using lats and chest
common_mistakes: Bending elbows too much; Arching the lower back; Going too heavy
safety: Use a light load and stop if your shoulders pinch overhead.

name: Barbell shrug
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Squat rack
form_cues: Hold the bar at your thighs, arms straight; Lift your shoulders straight up to your ears; Pause, then lower slowly
common_mistakes: Rolling the shoulders; Bending the elbows; Bouncing the weight
safety: Use straps for heavy sets to spare your grip.

name: Behind-the-back barbell shrug
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Squat rack
form_cues: Hold the bar behind your thighs; Shrug up and slightly back; Hold the top for a second
common_mistakes: Bar dragging on the legs; Using momentum; Short reps
safety: Unrack from mid-thigh height in a rack.

name: Behind-the-neck lat pulldown
equipment: Lat pulldown machine; Long lat bar
form_cues: Lean your head slightly forward under the bar.; Pull only to the base of your skull.; Keep the movement slow and controlled.
common_mistakes: Jutting the head forward to clear the bar.; Using heavy weight with poor shoulder mobility.
safety: Only use if you have good shoulder external rotation; skip it if it pinches.
notes: Front pulldowns train the same muscles with less shoulder stress.

name: Bent-over cable row
form_cues: Hinge forward with a flat back, knees soft.; Row the bar to your belly button.; Keep the torso angle fixed.
common_mistakes: Standing up during each rep.; Rounding the lower back.
safety: Keep the spine neutral; skip if your lower back is irritated.
aliases: Cable bent-over row; Low-pulley bent row

name: Cable high row
equipment: Cable machine; Rope or two handles
form_cues: Set the pulley high and kneel or sit facing it.; Pull handles toward your upper chest, elbows wide.; Squeeze shoulder blades down and together.
common_mistakes: Leaning back to pull.; Shrugging toward the ears.
safety: Use a mat if kneeling.
aliases: Kneeling high row; High cable row

name: Cable shrug
form_cues: Stand close to a low pulley holding the bar.; Shrug the shoulders straight up to the ears.; Pause, then lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Rolling the shoulders in circles.; Bending the elbows.
safety: Keep the neck relaxed and chin neutral.

name: Chest-supported dumbbell row
form_cues: Lie face down on a bench set to 30–45°.; Let the dumbbells hang, then row elbows toward your hips.; Squeeze your shoulder blades and lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Lifting your chest off the pad; Shrugging
safety: A great option when your lower back is tired.
aliases: Incline dumbbell row; Prone incline row

name: Close-grip lat pulldown
form_cues: Attach a V-handle and sit tall.; Lean back slightly and pull to the upper chest.; Squeeze the shoulder blades down and back.
common_mistakes: Rounding forward on the way up.; Yanking with momentum.
safety: Keep the movement smooth; don't let the stack slam.
aliases: V-bar pulldown; Neutral close-grip pulldown; V-handle lat pulldown

name: Cross-body cable lat pulldown
form_cues: Set the pulley high and reach across to the opposite handle.; Pull the elbow down and in toward your side.; Feel a big stretch at the top.
common_mistakes: Turning it into a straight-arm pulldown.; Rotating the whole torso.
safety: Use a weight you can control through the full arc.
notes: Works well in a cable crossover with the far pulley.

name: Deadlift
form_cues: Bar over mid-foot, shins close, hands just outside legs; Pull the slack out, brace, then push the floor away; Lock out by squeezing glutes, not leaning back
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back; Bar drifting away from the legs; Jerking the bar off the floor
regressions: Trap bar deadlift; Kettlebell deadlift; Rack pull
safety: Keep a neutral spine; use bumper plates or pads if you might drop it.
notes: Reset each rep for cleaner technique.

name: Deficit deadlift
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Low platform
form_cues: Stand on a 2–5 cm platform or plate; Set your hips a little lower than a normal deadlift; Push the floor away and keep the bar close
common_mistakes: Platform too high; Rounding the back to reach the bar; Hips shooting up
safety: Use a stable platform; reduce weight by about 10–20% versus your regular pull.
notes: Builds speed and strength off the floor.

name: Incline dumbbell shrug
form_cues: Lie face down on an incline bench, arms hanging.; Shrug your shoulders up and back toward each other.; Hold briefly, then lower.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows; Rolling the shoulders
safety: Keep your chest on the pad.
notes: Targets the middle traps more than standing shrugs.

name: Kayak row
equipment: Lat pulldown machine; Long lat bar
form_cues: Hold the bar wide and pull one end down to the hip.; Rotate slightly toward the working side.; Alternate sides like paddling a kayak.
common_mistakes: Using too much weight and losing control of the bar.; Not returning to full stretch between sides.
safety: Keep the movement controlled; the bar can swing.
aliases: Lat pulldown kayak row; Paddle pulldown

name: Kneeling single-arm cable pulldown
