form_cues: Set the pulley high and kneel in front of it.; Drive the elbow down toward your hip.; Keep ribs down and hips square.
common_mistakes: Leaning sideways to finish the rep.; Pulling the hand past the shoulder line.
safety: Use a mat under the knee.
aliases: Half-kneeling one-arm pulldown; Single-arm high cable pulldown

name: Kroc row
form_cues: Brace one hand on a bench, feet staggered.; Row a heavy dumbbell for high reps with a little body English.; Lower to a full stretch each rep.
common_mistakes: Turning it into a full-body jerk; Losing the flat back
safety: Use straps if needed and keep the lower back neutral.
notes: Named after powerlifter Matt Kroczaleski.

name: Lying cable pullover
equipment: Cable machine; Flat bench; Straight bar or rope
form_cues: Lie on a bench with head toward a low pulley.; Arms long, pull the bar over to your thighs.; Keep your lower back flat on the bench.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows a lot.; Arching the back at the stretch.
safety: Keep the stretch overhead within a pain-free range.

name: Meadows row
form_cues: Stand side-on to the bar end and stagger your stance; Grip the thick end overhand; Pull your elbow up and back
common_mistakes: Twisting the torso; Shrugging; Too heavy
safety: Rest your free forearm on your knee for support.

name: Neutral-grip lat pulldown
form_cues: Hold the parallel handles palms facing each other.; Pull the elbows straight down to your ribs.; Pause briefly with the chest up.
common_mistakes: Shrugging at the top.; Partial reps without a full stretch.
safety: Shoulder-friendly grip; good if wide grip bothers your shoulders.

name: One-arm dumbbell row
form_cues: Knee and hand on the bench, back flat.; Pull the dumbbell toward your hip, not your armpit.; Lower until your arm is fully straight.
common_mistakes: Twisting the torso to lift; Shrugging the weight up
safety: Keep your neck neutral and your back flat.
aliases: Single-arm DB row; Bench dumbbell row

name: Pendlay row
form_cues: Start each rep with the bar on the floor, back flat; Torso near parallel to the floor; Pull explosively to your lower chest, then set it down
common_mistakes: Hips rising to help; Back rounding; Not resting the bar each rep
safety: Needs good hamstring mobility to keep a flat back.

name: Rack pull
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Squat rack
form_cues: Set the bar on pins just below or above the knee; Wedge into the bar and brace before pulling; Finish tall with glutes squeezed and shoulders back
common_mistakes: Hyperextending at the top; Starting loose; Using it as an ego lift with poor form
safety: Lower the bar under control so it doesn't bounce on the pins.
notes: Can also be done off blocks.

name: Reverse-grip lat pulldown
form_cues: Grip the bar palms-up at shoulder width.; Drive the elbows down to your sides.; Touch the bar to your upper chest.
common_mistakes: Curling the bar down with the biceps.; Leaning back too far.
safety: Avoid a very narrow grip if your wrists or elbows complain.

name: Reverse-grip seated cable row
form_cues: Grip a straight bar palms-up at shoulder width.; Drive elbows back close to your sides.; Pull to the belly button.
common_mistakes: Curling with the biceps.; Leaning back excessively.
safety: Use a grip width that's comfortable for your wrists.
aliases: Underhand cable row; Supinated cable row

name: Ring row
form_cues: Hang under the rings, body straight.; Pull the rings to your ribs, turning palms in.; Lower to straight arms with control.
common_mistakes: Hips sagging; Short range of motion
safety: Check ring straps and anchor before use.
notes: Raise the feet on a box to make it harder.

name: Rope straight-arm pulldown
form_cues: Hinge forward with arms long.; Pull the rope to your hips and flare the ends apart.; Return slowly until you feel the lats stretch.
common_mistakes: Bending at the elbows.; Shrugging toward the ears.
safety: Keep the spine neutral as you hinge.
notes: The rope allows a slightly longer range than the bar.

name: Seal row
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; High flat bench
form_cues: Lie chest-down on a raised bench; Pull the bar to the underside of the bench; Lower to full stretch
common_mistakes: Lifting the chest off the bench; Short range; Kicking legs
safety: Bench must be stable and raised on blocks or a frame.
notes: Removes the lower back from rowing. Needs a raised bench (no specific gear id).

name: Seated cable row
form_cues: Sit tall with a slight bend in the knees.; Pull the handle to your lower ribs.; Squeeze shoulder blades together, then reach forward.
common_mistakes: Rocking back and forth with the torso.; Rounding the back on the return.
safety: Keep a neutral spine; don't let the stack pull you into a rounded back.
aliases: Seated row; V-handle cable row; Low row

name: Seated good morning
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Squat rack; Flat bench
form_cues: Sit astride a bench with the bar on your upper back; Lean forward from the hips with a flat back; Rise back up by squeezing glutes and back
common_mistakes: Rounding to get lower; Using heavy loads too soon; Bouncing at the bottom
safety: Light loads only; skip if you have lower-back problems.

name: Single-arm cable shrug
form_cues: Stand side-on to a low pulley holding one handle.; Shrug up and slightly back.; Lower slowly to a full stretch.
common_mistakes: Leaning away from the cable.; Jerking the weight.
safety: Keep the neck neutral and avoid tilting the head.
aliases: One-arm cable shrug; Side cable shrug
notes: The angled pull lines up well with the upper trap fibres.

name: Single-arm high cable row
form_cues: Set the pulley high and stand in a split stance.; Row the elbow down and back toward the hip.; Reach up fully between reps.
common_mistakes: Twisting the torso.; Using short partial reps.
safety: Keep the shoulder down away from the ear.

name: Single-arm lat pulldown
form_cues: Use a single D-handle and sit tall.; Pull the elbow down to your hip.; Let the arm reach high for a full stretch.
common_mistakes: Twisting the torso to cheat.; Shrugging the working shoulder.
safety: Keep the free hand on the thigh pad for stability.
notes: Great for fixing side-to-side imbalances.

name: Single-arm seated cable row
form_cues: Sit tall holding one D-handle.; Pull the elbow back past your ribs.; Allow a little reach forward for a stretch.
common_mistakes: Twisting a lot to move the weight.; Shrugging the shoulder up.
safety: Brace the free hand on the platform or thigh.
aliases: One-arm cable row; Unilateral seated row

name: Single-arm standing cable row
tags: Back; Compound; Core; Hypertrophy; Strength; Unilateral
form_cues: Stand in a split stance, opposite leg forward.; Row the handle to your hip.; Keep the hips facing the machine.
common_mistakes: Over-rotating the torso.; Rushing the lowering phase.
safety: Start light to learn the anti-rotation control.
aliases: One-arm standing cable row; Split-stance cable row

name: Single-arm suspension row
form_cues: Hold both handles in one hand, body in a plank.; Row up without twisting toward the strap.; Lower slowly and keep hips square.
common_mistakes: Rotating the torso to cheat; Hips dropping
safety: Lock the handles together so they can't slip.

name: Smith machine bent-over row
form_cues: Hinge to about 45°; Pull the bar to your lower ribs; Lower slowly
common_mistakes: Rounding the back; Jerking; Standing up
safety: Keep a flat back.

name: Smith machine shrug
form_cues: Stand tall with arms straight; Shrug straight up; Pause and lower
common_mistakes: Rolling shoulders; Bending elbows; Bouncing
safety: Use straps if needed.

name: Snatch-grip deadlift
form_cues: Take a wide snatch grip with hips set lower than usual; Keep your chest up and the bar close; Push through the floor, squeezing the upper back
common_mistakes: Rounding the upper back; Grip too narrow; Hips rising first
safety: Use straps if grip fails before the back; start lighter than your deadlift.

name: Standing cable row
form_cues: Set the pulley at chest height.; Stand in a quarter squat with chest up.; Row to the lower ribs, then reach long.
common_mistakes: Leaning back to use body weight.; Letting knees lock out.
safety: Hold a stable athletic stance so you don't get pulled forward.
aliases: Standing two-arm cable row; Mid cable row

name: Straight-arm pulldown
form_cues: Hinge slightly with arms long and soft elbows.; Sweep the bar down to your thighs.; Keep the chest up and ribs down.
common_mistakes: Bending elbows into a tricep pushdown.; Using the hips to swing the weight.
safety: Keep the weight moderate; it's a feel exercise.
notes: Great lat warm-up before pull-ups or pulldowns.

name: Suspension row
form_cues: Lean back with arms straight and body in a plank.; Pull your chest to your hands, elbows at your sides.; Lower slowly, keeping hips up.
common_mistakes: Hips sagging; Shrugging shoulders
safety: Check the anchor point and straps before every set.
notes: Walk feet forward to make it harder.

name: T-bar row
equipment: Landmine or T-bar row; Olympic barbell; Weight plates
form_cues: Straddle the bar and hinge to about 45°; Pull the handle to your chest; Lower slowly to full stretch
common_mistakes: Rounding the back; Standing up too much; Using momentum
safety: Keep your back flat; use a V-handle under the bar.
notes: The machine version needs only the tbar gear.

name: Trap bar deadlift
form_cues: Stand in the centre of the bar, handles in line with your ankles; Sit hips down and grip the handles; Push the floor away and stand tall
common_mistakes: Rounding the back; Hips too high; Leaning back at lockout
safety: Easier on the lower back than a straight bar; still keep a neutral spine.
notes: Use the high handles to shorten the range for beginners.

name: Trap bar shrug
form_cues: Stand in the bar with arms straight; Shrug straight up to your ears; Pause and lower slowly
common_mistakes: Rolling the shoulders; Bending the elbows; Bouncing
safety: Use straps for heavy sets.
notes: Neutral grip keeps the load at your sides like dumbbells.

name: Underhand barbell row
form_cues: Underhand grip, shoulder-width; Lean over to about 70°; Pull the bar to your belly button
common_mistakes: Standing too upright; Curling with the arms; Jerking the weight
safety: Avoid if supinated grip bothers your elbows.

name: Wide-grip lat pulldown
equipment: Lat pulldown machine; Long lat bar
form_cues: Grip the bar just outside shoulder width.; Pull your elbows down toward your back pockets.; Bring the bar to the top of your chest.
common_mistakes: Leaning way back and turning it into a row.; Pulling with the arms only and shrugging.
safety: Lock thighs under the pad and control the bar on the way up.

name: Wide-grip seated cable row
form_cues: Hold a lat bar wide, palms down.; Pull the bar to your lower chest, elbows out.; Pinch the shoulder blades together.
common_mistakes: Shrugging up.; Leaning back to finish the rep.
safety: Keep the torso steady; don't swing.
aliases: Wide-grip cable row; Lat bar seated row
notes: Elbows-out pulling biases the upper back and rear delts.

name: Barbell front raise
form_cues: Hold the bar at your thighs, shoulder-width grip; Raise it to eye level with soft elbows; Lower slowly, no swinging
common_mistakes: Swinging with the hips; Raising too high; Shrugging
safety: Keep it light; the long lever stresses the shoulders.

name: Barbell upright row
form_cues: Grip slightly wider than shoulders; Lead with your elbows up to chest height; Lower slowly
common_mistakes: Narrow grip pinching the shoulders; Pulling above chest height; Swinging the body
safety: Stop at chest height and skip it if you feel shoulder pinching.

name: Behind-the-back cable lateral raise
equipment: Cable machine; Single handle or ankle strap
form_cues: Stand side-on with the cable running behind your back.; Raise the arm out to the side.; Keep the torso still and upright.
common_mistakes: Turning the hips.; Using too much weight.
safety: Keep it light; the start position stretches the shoulder.
notes: An ankle strap around the wrist removes grip from the movement.

name: Behind-the-neck press
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Squat rack
form_cues: Take a wider grip with the bar on your traps; Press straight up with head neutral; Lower only as far as shoulders comfortably allow
common_mistakes: Forcing range you don't have; Craning the head forward; Going heavy
safety: Only for people with good shoulder mobility and no shoulder pain.
notes: Also useful as a jerk accessory for weightlifters.

name: Bent-over cable rear delt raise
form_cues: Hinge forward with crossed low cables.; Raise arms out to the sides.; Hold the hinge without bouncing.
common_mistakes: Standing up as you lift.; Rounding the lower back.
safety: Keep a neutral spine; use a bench for chest support if needed.
aliases: Bent-over cable reverse fly; Low cable rear delt raise

name: Cable external rotation
tags: Hypertrophy; Isolation; Rehab; Shoulders; Strength; Unilateral; Warm-up
form_cues: Set the pulley at elbow height, stand side-on.; Keep elbow tucked, rotate the forearm outward.; Return slowly.
common_mistakes: Letting the elbow drift away from the side.; Using too much weight.
safety: Use very light weight; stop if you feel sharp pain.
aliases: Cable shoulder external rotation; Cable ER
notes: Place a rolled towel between elbow and side.

name: Cable front raise
equipment: Cable machine; Rope or straight bar
form_cues: Stand facing away from a low pulley.; Raise the attachment to eye level with straight arms.; Lower slowly without swinging.
common_mistakes: Leaning back to lift.; Raising too high and shrugging.
safety: Keep the core tight to protect the lower back.
aliases: Rope front raise; Bar cable front raise

name: Cable internal rotation
tags: Hypertrophy; Isolation; Rehab; Shoulders; Strength; Unilateral; Warm-up
form_cues: Stand side-on with the pulley at elbow height.; Keep the elbow at your side.; Rotate the forearm across your stomach.
common_mistakes: Twisting the torso.; Lifting the elbow.
safety: Light weight only; this is a rehab and prehab move.

name: Cable lateral raise
form_cues: Stand side-on to a low pulley, handle in the far hand.; Raise the arm out to shoulder height.; Lead with the elbow and lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Swinging the body.; Raising above shoulder height with shrugged traps.
safety: Keep the weight light enough for strict reps.
aliases: Single-arm cable lateral raise; One-arm cable side raise
notes: Constant tension at the bottom, where dumbbells go slack.

name: Cable lean-away lateral raise
form_cues: Hold the machine and lean away from a low pulley.; Raise the arm out to the side.; Keep a slight bend in the elbow.
common_mistakes: Changing the lean during the set.; Letting the wrist lead above the elbow.
safety: Keep a firm grip on the machine with the free hand.
notes: Leaning away increases tension at the bottom of the range.

name: Cable rear delt row
form_cues: Set the pulley at chest height.; Row with elbows high and wide.; Pull to the upper chest, not the face.
common_mistakes: Dropping the elbows.; Leaning back to cheat.
safety: Keep shoulders down and away from ears.
aliases: Rope rear delt row; Wide cable row to face

name: Cable shoulder press
form_cues: Set pulleys low and stand or sit between them.; Press the handles overhead.; Keep ribs down and avoid arching.
common_mistakes: Leaning back.; Letting elbows drift behind the body.
safety: Brace your core so the lower back doesn't arch.
aliases: Standing cable overhead press; Seated cable shoulder press
notes: Single-arm half-kneeling version adds core work.

name: Cable upright row
equipment: Cable machine; Straight or EZ bar
form_cues: Hold the bar shoulder-width at a low pulley.; Lead with the elbows up to chest height.; Keep the bar close to your body.
common_mistakes: Pulling the hands higher than the elbows.; Using a very narrow grip.
safety: Stop at chest height if you feel shoulder pinching.

name: Cable Y-raise
form_cues: Hold opposite low handles crossed in front of you.; Raise the arms up and out into a Y.; Stop when arms are just above head height.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back.; Shrugging the traps.
safety: Keep it light; stop if you feel pinching overhead.
aliases: Cable Y raise; Low cable Y-raise
notes: Good for upper-back and shoulder balance.

name: Chest-supported dumbbell reverse fly
form_cues: Lie face down on an incline bench.; With soft elbows, raise the dumbbells out wide.; Pause at the top, then lower under control.
common_mistakes: Swinging; Squeezing shoulder blades instead of moving the arms
safety: Use light weights; rear delts are small.

name: Incline dumbbell Y raise
form_cues: Lie face down on a 30–45° incline, thumbs up.; Raise the dumbbells in a Y shape in line with your ears.; Lower slowly without shrugging.
common_mistakes: Shrugging; Using momentum
safety: Use very light dumbbells (1–5 kg).
notes: Good for posture and shoulder blade control.

name: Landmine lateral raise
form_cues: Stand side-on, holding the bar end low across your body; Raise it out to shoulder height; Lower slowly
common_mistakes: Shrugging; Swinging; Too heavy
safety: Light loads.

name: Landmine press
form_cues: Hold the bar end at your shoulder; Press up and forward; Lower slowly back to the shoulder
common_mistakes: Leaning back; Shrugging; Twisting
safety: Shoulder-friendly; keep your ribs down.
aliases: Single-arm landmine press; Half-kneeling landmine press
notes: Do it half-kneeling or standing.

name: Landmine thruster
form_cues: Squat with the bar end at your chest; Drive up and press in one motion; Lower back to the chest
common_mistakes: Pressing before standing; Leaning back; Losing balance
safety: Moderate loads; keep your core braced.

name: Lying side lateral raise
form_cues: Lie on your side on an incline bench.; Raise the top arm out until it points up.; Lower slowly to below the bench line.
common_mistakes: Going too heavy; Rotating the torso
safety: Use a light weight; keep it pain-free.
aliases: Side-lying lateral raise; Incline side raise
notes: Loads the bottom of the lateral raise that standing raises miss.

name: Reverse cable fly
equipment: Cable machine; No attachment or single handles
form_cues: Set pulleys at shoulder height and cross the cables.; Pull arms out wide with soft elbows.; Keep the chest tall and don't shrug.
common_mistakes: Squeezing shoulder blades too hard and using traps.; Bending the elbows into a row.
safety: Use light weight; rear delts are small muscles.
aliases: Cable rear delt fly; Standing reverse crossover
notes: Hold the cable ends directly or use handles.

name: Rope cable upright row
form_cues: Hold the rope ends at a low pulley.; Pull up and apart, elbows leading.; Stop at chest height.
common_mistakes: Raising elbows above shoulders.; Leaning back.
safety: The rope lets wrists move freely; stop if shoulders pinch.

name: Rope face pull
tags: Hypertrophy; Isolation; Rehab; Shoulders; Strength; Warm-up
form_cues: Set the rope at forehead height.; Pull toward your face, splitting the rope.; Finish with hands beside your ears, thumbs back.
common_mistakes: Pulling to the chest instead of the face.; Using heavy weight and leaning back.
safety: Keep it light and smooth; it's a shoulder-health move.
notes: Great for posture and shoulder health; kneeling version reduces cheating.

name: Seated barbell overhead press
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Squat rack; Adjustable bench
form_cues: Set the bench upright, back against the pad; Lower the bar to your upper chest; Press straight up past your face
common_mistakes: Arching hard off the pad; Bar drifting forward; Half reps
regressions: Seated dumbbell shoulder press; Smith machine shoulder press
safety: Use a rack or spotter for unracking.

name: Seated dumbbell shoulder press
form_cues: Set the bench upright and sit with your back flat on the pad.; Start with dumbbells at ear height, elbows slightly forward.; Press up until arms are straight, then lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Arching off the backrest; Cutting the range short at the bottom
progressions: Standing dumbbell shoulder press; Arnold press
safety: Kick the dumbbells up off your knees one at a time to get into position.
notes: A flat bench works too; sitting without back support adds core work.

name: Single-arm cable front raise
form_cues: Stand facing away with the cable between your legs.; Raise the arm straight to eye level.; Keep the torso square.
common_mistakes: Rotating the torso.; Locking the elbow hard.
safety: Keep the weight light; front delts already get lots of pressing work.

name: Single-arm cable reverse fly
form_cues: Stand side-on with the pulley at shoulder height.; Reach across and pull the arm out wide.; Stop when the arm is in line with your body.
common_mistakes: Rotating the torso.; Overextending behind the body.
safety: Keep the movement smooth and light.

name: Smith machine shoulder press
form_cues: Sit upright with the bar just in front of your face; Lower to chin level; Press up to lockout
common_mistakes: Arching off the pad; Lowering behind the neck; Half reps
safety: Set the bench so the bar clears your face.

name: Standing barbell overhead press
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Squat rack
form_cues: Bar on front delts, hands just outside shoulders; Squeeze glutes, move your head back and press straight up; Push your head through at the top
common_mistakes: Leaning back and turning it into an incline press; Pressing the bar around the face; Soft knees adding leg drive
regressions: Seated dumbbell shoulder press; Landmine press
safety: Keep ribs down to protect your lower back.
aliases: Overhead press; Military press; Strict press

name: Suspension face pull
form_cues: Lean back, palms down, arms straight.; Pull elbows high and wide, hands beside your ears.; Finish in a W shape, then lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Elbows dropping; Leaning too far back
safety: Keep it pain-free in the shoulder.
aliases: TRX W raise; TRX face pull

name: Suspension reverse fly
form_cues: Lean back, arms straight in front.; Open arms wide into a T.; Squeeze shoulder blades, then return slowly.
common_mistakes: Bending elbows into a row; Hips sagging
safety: Keep the lean modest at first.

name: Suspension Y raise
form_cues: Lean back with straight arms.; Raise arms up and out into a Y shape.; Keep shoulders down, away from ears.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows; Arching the back
safety: Use a small lean; this targets small muscles.
notes: Pair with T and W raises as a shoulder-health circuit.

name: Two-arm cable lateral raise
form_cues: Stand in the middle of a crossover with low pulleys.; Hold opposite handles crossed in front.; Raise both arms out to shoulder height.
common_mistakes: Shrugging up.; Letting the handles cross unevenly.
safety: Use light weights and focus on smooth tempo.
aliases: Crossover lateral raise; Cable Y-cross lateral raise

name: Z press
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Squat rack
form_cues: Sit on the floor with legs straight out in front; Brace hard and press the bar straight up; Keep your torso tall without leaning back
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back; Leaning back to finish; Too much weight
safety: Set the rack low so you can unrack seated; use light weights.
notes: Removes the legs and lower back from the press, exposing weak spots.

name: Barbell curl
form_cues: Hands shoulder-width, elbows tucked; Curl without swinging; Lower slowly to full extension
common_mistakes: Swinging the hips; Elbows drifting forward; Half reps
safety: Stop if your wrists hurt; switch to an EZ bar.

name: Barbell reverse wrist curl
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Flat bench
form_cues: Rest forearms on a bench, palms down; Lift the back of your hands up; Lower slowly
common_mistakes: Heavy weight; Moving the forearms; Short range
safety: Light loads; good for elbow health.

name: Bayesian cable curl
form_cues: Stand facing away from a low pulley.; Let the arm hang slightly behind you.; Curl without letting the elbow drift forward.
common_mistakes: Bringing the elbow forward to finish.; Leaning to shorten the stretch.
safety: Ease into the stretch if your front shoulder feels tight.
aliases: Behind-the-body cable curl; Face-away cable curl
notes: Trains the biceps in a lengthened position.

name: Behind-the-back barbell wrist curl
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Squat rack
form_cues: Hold the bar behind your thighs; Curl your wrists up; Lower to fingertips
common_mistakes: Bending elbows; Jerking; Too heavy
safety: Unrack from a rack at hip height.

name: Cable bar curl
equipment: Cable machine; Straight or EZ bar
form_cues: Stand close to a low pulley.; Keep elbows pinned to your sides.; Curl to shoulder height and lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Swinging the hips.; Letting elbows drift forward.
safety: Use a weight you can lower under control.
aliases: Straight-bar cable curl; Cable curl; EZ-bar cable curl
notes: An EZ bar is easier on the wrists.

name: Cable concentration curl
form_cues: Kneel or sit with the elbow braced on the thigh.; Curl the handle up slowly.; Squeeze hard at the top.
common_mistakes: Lifting the elbow off the thigh.; Short range.
safety: Choose a weight you can control.
aliases: Kneeling cable concentration curl; Seated cable concentration curl

name: Cable drag curl
form_cues: Stand close to a low pulley.; Drag the bar up your body, elbows going back.; Keep the bar touching your torso.
common_mistakes: Letting elbows come forward.; Shrugging.
safety: Stand close so the cable runs vertically.

name: Cable preacher curl
equipment: Cable machine; Preacher bench; Straight or EZ bar
form_cues: Set a preacher bench in front of a low pulley.; Rest the upper arms flat on the pad.; Curl up and lower to nearly straight.
common_mistakes: Lifting the elbows off the pad.; Dropping fast at the bottom.
safety: Don't snap the elbows straight at the bottom.
notes: Single-handle version works one arm at a time.

name: Cable reverse curl
equipment: Cable machine; Straight or EZ bar
form_cues: Grip the bar palms down.; Curl up with wrists straight.; Lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Letting wrists bend back.; Too heavy a weight.
safety: Use an EZ bar if straight-bar wrists ache.
aliases: Reverse-grip cable curl; Overhand cable curl

name: Cable tricep kickback
equipment: Cable machine; Single handle or no attachment
form_cues: Hinge forward holding a low cable.; Keep upper arm parallel to the floor.; Straighten the arm back and squeeze.
common_mistakes: Swinging the upper arm.; Rounding the back.
safety: Keep a flat back in the hinge.

name: Cable wrist curl
form_cues: Kneel or sit with forearms on a bench, palms up.; Let the bar roll to your fingers.; Curl the wrists up and squeeze.
common_mistakes: Lifting forearms off the bench.; Bouncing the weight.
safety: Use light weight; wrist tendons get sore easily.
notes: Flip palms down for a reverse wrist curl.

name: Close-grip bench press
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Flat bench
form_cues: Grip about shoulder-width, not much closer; Keep elbows tucked near your sides; Touch the lower chest and press to lockout
common_mistakes: Hands so close it hurts the wrists; Elbows flaring out; Bouncing off the chest
safety: Use a spotter; wrists should stay stacked over elbows.

name: Close-grip dumbbell press
form_cues: Lie on a bench, dumbbells touching, palms facing each other.; Lower them to your lower chest with elbows tucked.; Press straight up with the weights still touching.
common_mistakes: Elbows flaring; Bouncing off the chest
safety: Keep the weights over your chest, not your face.
aliases: Dumbbell crush press for triceps; Neutral close-grip DB press

name: Cross-body cable hammer curl
equipment: Cable machine; Rope or single handle
form_cues: Stand side-on to a low pulley.; Curl the handle across toward the opposite shoulder.; Keep the elbow tight to the side.
common_mistakes: Swinging the arm.; Twisting the torso.
safety: Keep wrist neutral.

name: Cross-body cable tricep extension
equipment: Cable machine; No attachment or single handles
form_cues: Hold opposite high cables crossed in front of your face.; Extend arms out and down to the sides.; Keep elbows at shoulder height.
common_mistakes: Dropping elbows.; Turning it into a fly.
safety: Use light weight; focus on squeezing the triceps.
aliases: Cross cable tricep extension; Cable X tricep extension
notes: Can be done one arm at a time.

name: Drag curl
form_cues: Pull your elbows back as you curl; Drag the bar up your torso; Lower the same path
common_mistakes: Elbows drifting forward; Using momentum; Shrugging
safety: Use moderate weights.

name: Dumbbell preacher curl
equipment: Dumbbell; Preacher bench or incline bench
form_cues: Rest the back of your upper arm on the pad.; Curl the dumbbell up and squeeze.; Lower slowly but stop just short of locking out hard.
common_mistakes: Dropping fast at the bottom; Lifting the elbow off the pad
safety: Control the bottom to protect the elbow.
notes: No preacher bench? Lean over the back of an incline bench.

name: Dumbbell skull crusher
form_cues: Lie on a bench, dumbbells over your shoulders, palms facing each other.; Bend the elbows to lower the weights beside your head.; Straighten your arms, keeping upper arms still.
common_mistakes: Elbows flaring; Moving the upper arms
safety: Lower slowly; the weights end up near your head.
aliases: Lying dumbbell triceps extension; DB lying extension

name: Dumbbell spider curl
form_cues: Lie chest-down on an incline bench, arms hanging.; Curl up and squeeze hard at the top.; Lower slowly without swinging.
common_mistakes: Moving the upper arm; Lifting the chest off the pad
safety: Keep your chin over the top of the bench, not resting on it.

name: EZ-bar curl
form_cues: Grip the angled handles; Keep elbows by your sides; Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly
common_mistakes: Using momentum; Lifting elbows; Partial reps
safety: Wrist-friendlier than a straight bar.

name: EZ-bar overhead triceps extension
form_cues: Hold the bar overhead, elbows pointed forward; Lower behind your head; Extend back up
common_mistakes: Elbows flaring; Arching back; Heavy loads
safety: Sit on a bench for support if needed.

name: EZ-bar skull crusher
equipment: EZ curl bar; Weight plates; Flat bench
form_cues: Lie on a bench, bar over your eyes; Lower the bar to your forehead by bending elbows; Extend back without moving upper arms
common_mistakes: Elbows flaring; Moving shoulders; Too heavy
safety: Control the bar; use a spotter if heavy.
notes: Can be done with a straight bar too.

name: EZ-bar spider curl
equipment: EZ curl bar; Weight plates; Incline bench
form_cues: Lie chest-down on an incline bench; Let arms hang straight down; Curl up and squeeze hard
common_mistakes: Swinging; Elbows moving forward; Heavy loads
safety: Use light weight; can also use dumbbells.

name: High cable curl
form_cues: Stand between high pulleys, arms out to the sides.; Curl the handles toward your ears.; Keep upper arms level with the shoulders.
common_mistakes: Dropping the elbows.; Using too much weight.
safety: Use light weight; shoulders are in an exposed position.
aliases: Overhead cable curl; Double-biceps cable curl; Cable crossover curl
notes: Hits the biceps in a shortened, peak-contraction position.

name: Incline dumbbell curl
form_cues: Sit back on a 45–60° bench, arms hanging straight down.; Curl up without moving your elbows forward.; Lower all the way to a full stretch.
common_mistakes: Bringing elbows forward; Lifting the head and shoulders off the pad
safety: Go lighter than normal curls; the stretch is demanding.

name: Incline hammer curl
form_cues: Sit back on an incline bench, palms facing in.; Curl up with thumbs leading.; Lower slowly to full stretch.
common_mistakes: Swinging; Elbows drifting forward
safety: Keep shoulders back on the pad.

name: JM press
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Flat bench
form_cues: Grip close and tuck elbows; Lower bar toward your chin; Press back up
common_mistakes: Bar hitting the face; Elbows flaring; Too heavy
safety: Learn with an empty bar and a spotter.
notes: A hybrid between a close-grip bench and a skull crusher.

name: Lying cable curl
equipment: Cable machine; Straight bar; Floor or bench
form_cues: Lie on your back with feet toward a low pulley.; Keep upper arms on the floor.; Curl the bar toward your forehead.
common_mistakes: Lifting elbows off the floor.; Using momentum.
safety: Use a mat for comfort.
notes: Locks out body swing for very strict reps.

name: Lying cable tricep extension
equipment: Cable machine; Flat bench; Straight or EZ bar
form_cues: Lie on a bench, head toward a low pulley.; Upper arms angled slightly back.; Extend the bar up, bend back toward your forehead.
common_mistakes: Elbows flaring.; Moving the upper arms.
safety: Control the bar near the head.
notes: Constant tension version of a skull crusher.

name: Lying cross-body triceps extension
form_cues: Lie on a bench with one dumbbell straight up.; Bend the elbow so the weight lowers toward the opposite shoulder.; Extend back up.
common_mistakes: Moving the upper arm; Going too heavy
safety: Lower slowly so the dumbbell doesn't hit your chest.

name: Overhead rope extension
form_cues: Face away from the pulley, rope behind your head.; Keep elbows pointing forward.; Extend until arms are straight.
common_mistakes: Elbows flaring wide.; Arching the lower back.
safety: Use a split stance and brace to protect the lower back.
aliases: Overhead cable tricep extension; Rope overhead extension
notes: A straight bar works too; stretches the long head.

name: Plate pinch hold
form_cues: Pinch two smooth plates together, smooth sides out.; Keep fingers straight and thumb pressed hard.; Stand tall and hold for time.
common_mistakes: Curling fingers around the edge; Holding plates against the leg
safety: Hold over a clear floor and keep your feet out of the drop zone.
notes: Walk with the plates for a pinch carry.

name: Preacher curl
equipment: EZ curl bar; Weight plates; Preacher bench
form_cues: Armpits snug on the pad; Curl up without lifting elbows; Lower to nearly straight arms
common_mistakes: Bouncing at the bottom; Lifting off the pad; Dropping fast
safety: Don't lock out hard at the bottom under heavy loads.

name: Preacher hammer curl
form_cues: Hold the dumbbell with thumb up throughout.; Keep the elbow pinned to the pad as you curl.; Lower slowly to a full stretch.
common_mistakes: Turning the palm up mid-rep.; Rushing the lowering phase.
safety: Keep the wrist straight and neutral.
notes: Builds arm thickness and elbow-flexor strength.

name: Reverse barbell curl
form_cues: Overhand grip, shoulder-width; Curl while keeping wrists straight; Lower slowly
common_mistakes: Wrists flexing; Swinging; Heavy weight
safety: Use an EZ bar if the straight bar hurts the wrists.

name: Reverse-grip preacher curl
equipment: Preacher curl bench; EZ curl bar
form_cues: Grip the bar palms down, hands shoulder-width.; Curl up while keeping wrists straight.; Lower with control; don't let the bar drop.
common_mistakes: Letting the wrists bend back.; Using too much weight for the grip.
safety: Go lighter than a regular preacher curl; forearms tire fast.
aliases: Reverse preacher curl; Overhand preacher curl
notes: Great for forearm and elbow health in pulling athletes.

name: Reverse-grip tricep pushdown
equipment: Cable machine; Straight or EZ bar
form_cues: Grip the bar palms up.; Keep elbows locked in place at your sides.; Push down until arms are straight.
common_mistakes: Bending the wrists.; Going too heavy.
safety: Keep it light; wrists are in a weaker position.

name: Ring bicep curl
form_cues: Lean back with palms up and arms straight.; Curl hands toward your forehead, elbows high.; Lower slowly without dropping elbows.
common_mistakes: Turning it into a row; Hips sagging
safety: Rings rotate freely, so start with a small lean.

name: Rope hammer curl
form_cues: Hold the rope with palms facing each other.; Curl up keeping elbows still.; Lower all the way down.
common_mistakes: Rocking the torso.; Half reps at the top.
safety: Keep wrists straight, not bent back.
aliases: Cable rope hammer curl; Cable hammer curl

name: Rope pushdown
form_cues: Set the rope high and pin elbows to your sides.; Push down and spread the rope at the bottom.; Let forearms rise only to parallel.
common_mistakes: Elbows drifting forward.; Leaning over to use body weight.
safety: Keep wrists neutral and shoulders down.
aliases: Rope tricep pushdown; Cable rope pushdown

name: Single-arm cable curl
form_cues: Hold a D-handle at a low pulley.; Curl with the palm turning up.; Squeeze at the top, lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Leaning away to help.; Elbow moving forward.
safety: Keep the shoulder still.
aliases: One-arm cable curl; D-handle cable curl

name: Single-arm cable pushdown
form_cues: Hold a D-handle from a high pulley.; Pin the elbow and press down to straight.; Control the return.
common_mistakes: Twisting the torso.; Elbow drifting out.
safety: Keep the shoulder down and still.
notes: Underhand or overhand grip both work.

name: Single-arm overhead cable extension
form_cues: Face away from a low pulley, handle behind the head.; Keep the upper arm by your ear.; Extend up until straight.
common_mistakes: Upper arm moving.; Leaning sideways.
safety: Ease into the bottom stretch.

name: Smith machine close-grip bench press
form_cues: Shoulder-width grip; Tuck elbows; Press to lockout
common_mistakes: Hands too close; Elbows flaring; Bouncing
safety: Set safety stops.

name: Straight-bar pushdown
form_cues: Grip the bar palms down, shoulder width.; Elbows tight, push until arms are straight.; Control the bar back up.
common_mistakes: Flaring elbows.; Using shoulders to push.
safety: Avoid locking out hard if elbows ache.

name: Suspension bicep curl
form_cues: Face the anchor, palms up, leaning back.; Keep elbows high and still.; Curl hands toward your forehead.
common_mistakes: Dropping elbows into a row; Hips sagging
safety: Walk feet forward slowly to add load.

name: Suspension triceps extension
form_cues: Face away, arms straight overhead holding handles.; Bend only at the elbows, hands toward your forehead.; Straighten arms to push back to the start.
common_mistakes: Elbows flaring; Hips piking
safety: Begin fairly upright; the movement gets hard quickly as you lean.

name: Tate press
form_cues: Lie on a bench, dumbbells over your chest, palms toward your feet.; Bend the elbows out to lower the dumbbell ends to your chest.; Extend back up by squeezing your triceps.
common_mistakes: Going too heavy; Letting the elbows drop toward your sides
safety: Use light weights and lower with control.

name: V-bar pushdown
form_cues: Hold the V-handle with thumbs up top.; Keep elbows at your sides.; Press down to full extension.
common_mistakes: Rocking the body.; Short range at the top.
safety: Use a weight you can lower slowly.
notes: Usually allows the heaviest loads of the pushdown variations.

name: Anderson squat
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Squat rack
form_cues: Set the pins at your sticking point and start under the bar; Get tight and brace before you push; Drive the bar off the pins without bouncing
common_mistakes: Loose start position; Bouncing the bar off the pins; Hips shooting up first
safety: Pins must be secure and level; lower each rep back to the pins with control.
notes: Starts from a dead stop to build strength out of the bottom.

name: Barbell back squat
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Squat rack
form_cues: Bar sits on your upper traps, hands just outside shoulders; Brace hard, then sit down between your heels; Drive up through mid-foot, chest and hips rising together
common_mistakes: Knees caving inward; Heels lifting off the floor; Cutting depth short as the weight climbs
regressions: Goblet squat; Box squat; Smith machine squat
progressions: Pause squat; Front squat; Low-bar back squat
safety: Squat inside a rack with safety pins set just below your bottom position.
notes: Add a 2–3 sec pause at the bottom for a tougher, technique-focused variation.

name: Barbell box squat
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Squat rack; Box or bench
form_cues: Set a box at or just below parallel; Sit back until you lightly touch the box, staying tight; Drive up hard without rocking off the box
common_mistakes: Crashing down onto the box; Relaxing completely on the box; Rocking forward to get up
safety: Never drop onto the box under load; sit with control.
notes: Great for teaching depth and hip drive, and easier on the knees.

name: Barbell Bulgarian split squat
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Squat rack; Flat bench
form_cues: Rest the back foot laces-down on a bench; Lower straight down until the back knee nearly touches; Drive up through the front heel
common_mistakes: Front foot too close to the bench; Bouncing off the back leg; Losing balance under the bar
regressions: Bulgarian split squat; Barbell split squat
safety: Master the dumbbell version first; balance is the limiter with a bar on your back.

name: Barbell forward lunge
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Squat rack
form_cues: Step forward and land heel first; Drop the back knee straight down; Push firmly back to the start
common_mistakes: Knee shooting far past toes with heel lifting; Stepping too narrow; Slamming the knee down
safety: Requires good balance and deceleration; start with an empty bar.

name: Barbell hack squat
form_cues: Hold the bar behind your legs, arms straight; Squat down keeping your chest up and the bar close; Stand tall by pushing through the whole foot
common_mistakes: Bar scraping the calves; Leaning too far forward; Rounding the back at the bottom
safety: Raise the plates on small blocks if the bar hits your heels.
notes: Different from the machine hack squat; great quad builder with just a barbell.

name: Barbell lateral lunge
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Squat rack
form_cues: Step wide to the side and sit back into that hip; Keep the trailing leg straight and both feet flat; Push off the bent leg to return
common_mistakes: Knee caving in on the working leg; Rounding the back; Heel lifting
regressions: Bodyweight lateral lunge; Goblet lateral lunge
safety: Go light; the side-to-side load is harder to control under a bar.

name: Barbell reverse lunge
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Squat rack
form_cues: Step back far enough that the front shin stays fairly upright; Lower the back knee under control; Push off the front foot to return to standing
common_mistakes: Short step putting pressure on the front knee; Torso folding forward; Wobbly side-to-side steps
progressions: Barbell walking lunge; Deficit reverse lunge
safety: Use a lighter load than your squat and keep the area around you clear.
notes: Usually kinder on the knees than forward lunges.

name: Barbell Romanian deadlift
form_cues: Start standing and soften the knees slightly; Push your hips back, sliding the bar down your thighs; Stop when hamstrings are stretched, then drive hips forward
common_mistakes: Rounding the back to reach lower; Bending the knees into a squat; Bar drifting away from the legs
safety: Only go as low as you can keep a flat back.

name: Barbell split squat
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Squat rack
form_cues: Take a long split stance with feet hip-width apart; Drop the back knee straight down toward the floor; Push through the front foot to rise
common_mistakes: Feet in a straight line, causing wobble; Front heel lifting; Leaning far forward
regressions: Bodyweight split squat; Dumbbell split squat
progressions: Barbell Bulgarian split squat; Barbell walking lunge
safety: Start light to find balance; unrack and rerack with both feet together.

name: Barbell standing calf raise
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Squat rack
form_cues: Stand tall with the bar on your back; Rise as high as you can onto the balls of your feet; Lower slowly to a full stretch
common_mistakes: Bouncing reps; Bending the knees; Short range of motion
safety: Stand on a plate edge for more range only once balance is solid.

name: Barbell step-up
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Squat rack; Box
form_cues: Plant your whole foot on a knee-height box; Drive up through the top heel, not the back toe; Lower slowly to the floor
common_mistakes: Pushing off with the bottom leg; Box too high; Knee caving in
safety: Use a sturdy, non-slip box and keep the height modest when loaded.

name: Barbell walking lunge
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Squat rack
form_cues: Take long, steady steps with feet hip-width apart; Lightly kiss the back knee to the floor; Drive through the front foot into the next step
common_mistakes: Rushing the steps; Narrow tightrope stance; Leaning forward under the bar
safety: Need a clear path; set the bar down if you lose balance rather than fighting it.

name: Cable lateral lunge
form_cues: Stand side-on holding a handle at the chest.; Step out wide and sit back into the hip.; Push back to the start.
common_mistakes: Knee travelling past the toes inward.; Rounding the back.
safety: Keep the trailing leg straight and the heel down.

name: Cable reverse lunge
form_cues: Face the pulley holding a handle at the chest.; Step back and lower the back knee.; Drive through the front foot to return.
common_mistakes: Short steps.; Leaning forward too much.
safety: Move slowly and keep balance.

name: Cable Romanian deadlift
equipment: Cable machine; Straight bar or rope
form_cues: Stand close to a low pulley holding the bar.; Push the hips back, bar sliding down the thighs.; Stand up by squeezing the glutes.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back.; Bending knees into a squat.
safety: Stop at mid-shin or when your back starts to round.

name: Cable split squat
equipment: Cable machine; Single handles or rope
form_cues: Stand in a long split stance holding low cables.; Drop the back knee straight down.; Push through the front heel.
common_mistakes: Front knee caving in.; Stance too short.
safety: Keep the back knee off the floor.

name: Cable squat
equipment: Cable machine; Rope or straight bar
form_cues: Hold the attachment at chest, lean back slightly.; Sit down between your heels.; Drive up through the whole foot.
common_mistakes: Knees caving in.; Heels lifting.
safety: Keep the cable taut and stand far enough back.
aliases: Cable goblet squat; Rope cable squat
notes: The counterbalance helps beginners squat deeper.

name: Cable sumo squat
equipment: Cable machine; Rope or straight bar
form_cues: Stand wide over a low pulley, toes out.; Squat straight down with the chest up.; Push knees out over toes.
common_mistakes: Knees collapsing in.; Leaning forward.
safety: Stand on boxes for a deeper range if the stack hits the floor.

name: Clean deadlift
form_cues: Set up exactly like your clean; Lift slowly with the chest up and the bar close; Keep shoulders over the bar past the knees
common_mistakes: Hips shooting up; Bar drifting away; Rounding
safety: Keep a flat back.
notes: Strength exercise that grooves the first pull of the clean.

name: Dumbbell box step-over
form_cues: Hold dumbbells at your sides facing a box.; Step up, stand tall on top, and step down the other side.; Turn and repeat, alternating legs.
common_mistakes: Jumping down; Rounding the back
safety: Step, don't jump, down from the box with weights in hand.
notes: Common in CrossFit workouts; count total reps.

name: Dumbbell lateral step-up
form_cues: Stand side-on to a box with dumbbells at your sides.; Step the near foot up and stand tall.; Lower slowly back down on the same side.
common_mistakes: Knee caving in; Hopping off the floor foot
safety: Use a lower box to start.

name: Dumbbell lying leg curl
form_cues: Lie face down with knees just off the bench end.; Squeeze a dumbbell between your feet.; Curl heels toward your glutes and lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Dropping the dumbbell; Lifting the hips
safety: Have a partner place the dumbbell, and keep it light.
notes: A home substitute for the leg curl machine.

name: Dumbbell step-up
form_cues: Place your whole foot on a knee-height box or bench.; Drive through that heel to stand up tall.; Step down slowly with the same leg leading back.
common_mistakes: Pushing off the bottom foot; Box too high
safety: Make sure the bench or box is solid and won't tip.

name: Front squat
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Squat rack
form_cues: Rest the bar on your front delts with elbows high; Keep your torso upright as you sit straight down; Lead with the elbows as you drive up
common_mistakes: Elbows dropping and bar rolling forward; Rounding the upper back; Rising onto the toes
safety: Use safety pins; if the bar slips forward, push it away and step back.
aliases: Barbell front squat; Clean-grip front squat
notes: Use a cross-arm grip or straps if wrist mobility limits the clean grip.

name: Front-foot elevated split squat
form_cues: Put your front foot on a low step, back foot on the floor.; Sink until the back knee nearly touches the floor.; Drive up through the front foot.
common_mistakes: Front heel lifting; Leaning sideways
safety: Use a stable step about 5–10 cm high.
notes: Gives more depth than a regular split squat.

name: Good morning
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Squat rack
form_cues: Bar on upper traps, knees softly bent; Push hips back and bow forward with a flat back; Stop at about parallel and drive hips forward
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back; Going too heavy; Turning it into a squat
regressions: Band good morning; Barbell Romanian deadlift
safety: Start very light; stop the descent the moment your back starts to round.

name: Landmine reverse lunge
form_cues: Hold the bar end at your chest; Step back and lower the knee; Drive through the front foot to stand
common_mistakes: Short step; Torso collapsing; Wobbly knees
safety: Stable loading for beginners.

name: Landmine squat
form_cues: Hold the bar end at your chest; Sit down between your heels; Drive up through mid-foot
common_mistakes: Knees caving; Leaning onto the bar; Heels lifting
safety: Good beginner squat; the arc supports the torso.

name: Low-bar back squat
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Squat rack
form_cues: Rest the bar on the shelf of your rear delts, below the traps; Push hips back and lean your chest forward more than high-bar; Keep wrists straight and elbows driving up out of the hole
common_mistakes: Bar rolling down the back; Wrists bent back taking the load; Turning the lift into a good morning
safety: Use safety pins and warm your shoulders up first; stop if elbows or wrists ache.
notes: Common in powerlifting because the shorter lever lets you move more weight.

name: Multi-gym leg curl
form_cues: Set the pad just above your heels.; Curl the pad towards your glutes without lifting your hips.; Return slowly to almost straight legs.
common_mistakes: Hips popping up off the bench.; Cutting the range short at the bottom.
progressions: Lying leg curl; Seated leg curl
safety: Keep your hips pressed down to protect the lower back.
notes: Depending on the model this is done seated, standing or lying on the leg-extension attachment.

name: Multi-gym leg extension
form_cues: Line your knee up with the machine's pivot point.; Kick up until legs are straight and squeeze the quads.; Lower slowly over two to three seconds.
common_mistakes: Swinging the weight up with momentum.; Lifting hips off the seat.
safety: Start light if you have knee pain and stop if it sharpens.
notes: Usually shares a station with the multi-gym leg curl.

name: Overhead squat
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Squat rack
form_cues: Lock the bar overhead with a wide snatch grip; Push up into the bar and keep it over mid-foot; Sit straight down with your chest tall
common_mistakes: Bar drifting forward; Soft elbows; Heels lifting
safety: Practise with an empty bar; learn to dump the bar forward or back safely.
notes: A key snatch accessory that builds overhead stability and mobility.

name: Safety squat bar squat
equipment: Safety squat bar; Weight plates; Squat rack
form_cues: Hold the handles lightly and keep elbows down; Brace and fight to keep your chest up; Sit down between your heels and drive straight up
common_mistakes: Letting the bar tip you forward; Pulling the handles too hard; Cutting depth
safety: Use safety pins; the bar's camber pushes you forward, so start lighter than your back squat.
notes: Needs a safety squat bar (no app gear id; nearest is barbell). Shoulder-friendly squat option.

name: Seated dumbbell calf raise
form_cues: Sit with balls of the feet on a plate or step.; Rest dumbbells on your knees.; Lower heels, then press up as high as possible.
common_mistakes: Bouncing; Too short a range
safety: Pad the dumbbells on your knees with a towel.

name: Smith machine Bulgarian split squat
form_cues: Rear foot on a bench; Lower straight down; Drive up through the front heel
common_mistakes: Foot too close; Bouncing; Leaning
safety: Set safety stops.

name: Smith machine calf raise
form_cues: Stand on a plate; Rise high on your toes; Lower to a full stretch
common_mistakes: Bouncing; Bent knees; Short reps
safety: Use a stable step.

name: Smith machine reverse lunge
form_cues: Step back under the bar; Lower the back knee; Drive back to standing
common_mistakes: Short step; Leaning; Knee crashing
safety: Stable option for beginners.

name: Smith machine Romanian deadlift
form_cues: Stand close with feet under the bar; Push hips back keeping the bar close; Stand up by driving hips forward
common_mistakes: Rounding the back; Bending knees too much; Bar too far forward
safety: Only go as low as your back stays flat.

name: Smith machine split squat
form_cues: Long split stance under the bar; Lower the back knee; Push up through the front foot
common_mistakes: Short stance; Front heel lifting; Leaning
safety: Set safety stops.

name: Smith machine squat
form_cues: Feet slightly in front of the bar; Sit down under control; Drive up through mid-foot
common_mistakes: Feet too far back; Knees caving; Half reps
safety: Set the safety stops just below your bottom position.

name: Standing cable hamstring curl
form_cues: Face the pulley with the strap on the ankle.; Curl the heel toward the glute.; Keep the thigh still.
common_mistakes: Moving the thigh forward and back.; Arching the back.
safety: Hold the frame and keep hips steady.
aliases: Cable leg curl; Standing cable leg curl
notes: Home-gym substitute for a leg curl machine.

name: Standing cable hip adduction
form_cues: Stand side-on with the strap on the near ankle.; Pull the leg across your body.; Return slowly to the start.
common_mistakes: Twisting the hips.; Too big a stretch out to the side.
safety: Ease into the outward stretch to avoid groin strains.
aliases: Cable hip adduction; Cable inner thigh

name: Standing cable hip flexion
tags: Hypertrophy; Isolation; Legs; Rehab; Strength; Unilateral
form_cues: Face away from a low pulley, strap on the ankle.; Drive the knee up to hip height.; Keep standing tall.
common_mistakes: Leaning back.; Swinging the leg.
safety: Hold the frame for balance.
aliases: Cable knee drive; Cable hip flexor raise
notes: Useful for runners and kicking sports.

name: Stiff-leg deadlift
form_cues: Start from the floor with knees nearly straight; Hinge at the hips with a long, flat back; Pull the bar up close to your legs
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back; Bending the knees too much; Yanking from the floor
safety: Use a weight you can control with a flat back; skip if you have a lower-back injury.
notes: Unlike the RDL, each rep starts from the floor.

name: Suspension hamstring curl
form_cues: Lie on your back with heels in the cradles.; Lift hips into a bridge.; Curl heels to your glutes, keeping hips high.
common_mistakes: Hips dropping during the curl; Rushing the return
safety: Set the straps about 20–30 cm off the floor.

name: Suspension lunge
form_cues: Place the back foot in the foot cradle.; Lower the back knee toward the floor.; Drive through the front heel to stand.
common_mistakes: Front knee caving; Leaning too far forward
safety: Lower the straps to mid-calf height for good balance.
aliases: TRX suspended lunge; TRX split squat

name: Suspension-assisted pistol squat
form_cues: Hold the handles and stand on one leg.; Sit down slowly with the free leg out front.; Use the straps only as much as needed to rise.
common_mistakes: Knee caving inward; Pulling hard with the arms
safety: Stop above the depth where your knee or hip hurts.
notes: Reduce the arm assist over time.

name: Trap bar Romanian deadlift
form_cues: Start standing, knees soft; Push your hips back as the bar slides down; Stop at a hamstring stretch and stand back up
common_mistakes: Rounding the back; Squatting the weight; Bar drifting forward
safety: Only go as low as you can keep a flat back.

name: Zercher squat
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Squat rack
form_cues: Cradle the bar in the crooks of your elbows, hands together; Stay tall and brace as you squat between your knees; Keep elbows up so the bar doesn't drag you forward
common_mistakes: Rounding the upper back; Letting the elbows drop; Going too heavy before the arms adapt
safety: Pad the bar or wear long sleeves; set the rack hooks at mid-chest height.
notes: Builds a strong upper back and brace; a favourite of strongmen.

name: Barbell glute bridge
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Bar pad
form_cues: Lie on your back, bar padded across your hips; Plant feet close and drive hips up; Pause and squeeze at the top
common_mistakes: Overarching the lower back; Pushing through the toes; Rushing the reps
safety: Pad the bar; use bumper plates so the bar can roll over your legs.
notes: Shorter range than the hip thrust but easier to set up.

name: Barbell hip thrust
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Flat bench; Bar pad
form_cues: Upper back on the bench edge, bar padded over your hips; Tuck your chin and drive through your heels; Squeeze glutes hard at the top with shins vertical
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back at the top; Feet too far away or too close; Pushing through the toes
progressions: Pause hip thrust; Single-leg hip thrust
safety: Always use a pad or folded mat under the bar.

name: Cable donkey kickback
form_cues: Get on all fours facing a low pulley.; Drive the heel up toward the ceiling.; Keep the hips square and back flat.
common_mistakes: Rotating the hips.; Arching the lower back.
safety: Use a mat for your knees.

name: Cable fire hydrant
form_cues: On all fours, side-on to a low pulley.; Lift the bent knee out to the side.; Keep the torso still.
common_mistakes: Leaning the body away.; Rushing the reps.
safety: Light weight; slow control matters more.

name: Cable glute kickback
form_cues: Attach the strap and hold the frame.; Kick the leg back with a slight knee bend.; Squeeze the glute without arching your back.
common_mistakes: Swinging the leg.; Arching the lower back.
safety: Keep core braced to protect the lower back.

name: Cable pull-through
form_cues: Face away from a low pulley, rope between legs.; Push hips back with a flat back.; Drive hips forward and squeeze the glutes.
common_mistakes: Squatting instead of hinging.; Pulling with the arms.
safety: Walk far enough out that the stack doesn't touch at the top.
notes: Good way to learn the hip hinge.

name: Dumbbell hip thrust
form_cues: Upper back on a bench edge, dumbbell on your hips.; Drive through your heels and raise hips to a straight line.; Tuck your chin and squeeze glutes hard at the top.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back; Feet too far forward
safety: Pad the dumbbell and hold it in place with both hands.

name: Single-leg cable Romanian deadlift
tags: Balance; Compound; Glutes; Hypertrophy; Strength; Unilateral
form_cues: Hold the handle in the hand opposite the standing leg.; Hinge forward as the free leg goes back.; Keep hips level.
common_mistakes: Opening the hips.; Rounding the spine.
safety: Touch the frame with the free hand for balance if needed.

name: Single-leg dumbbell hip thrust
form_cues: Upper back on a bench, dumbbell on the working hip.; Lift one foot and drive through the other heel.; Keep hips level and lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Hips dropping to one side; Overarching
safety: Start with bodyweight to master the balance.

name: Single-leg landmine Romanian deadlift
form_cues: Hold the bar end in the opposite hand; Hinge on one leg, reaching the other leg back; Return by driving hips forward
common_mistakes: Rounding the back; Opening the hips; Knee locked
safety: The landmine offers extra stability.

name: Smith machine hip thrust
equipment: Smith machine; Flat bench; Bar pad
form_cues: Upper back on the bench; Bar over the hips, padded; Drive hips up and squeeze
common_mistakes: Overarching; Pushing through toes; Rushing
safety: Pad the bar.

name: Standing cable hip abduction
form_cues: Stand side-on with the strap on the far ankle.; Lift the leg out to the side.; Keep the toes pointing forward.
common_mistakes: Leaning the torso sideways.; Swinging the leg.
safety: Hold the frame for balance.
aliases: Cable hip abduction; Ankle-strap leg raise

name: Straight-leg cable hip extension
form_cues: Face the pulley with the strap on one ankle.; Keep the leg straight and push it back.; Stop before your lower back arches.
common_mistakes: Leaning forward a lot.; Using momentum.
safety: Hold the frame for balance.

name: Sumo deadlift
form_cues: Take a wide stance with toes turned out, hands inside the knees; Push knees out over the toes and keep chest up; Spread the floor with your feet and stand tall
common_mistakes: Knees caving in; Hips rising before the bar moves; Stance so wide you can't push
regressions: Sumo kettlebell deadlift; Trap bar deadlift
progressions: Deficit sumo deadlift; Pause sumo deadlift
safety: Warm up hips and adductors well before heavy sets.

name: Suspension hip press
form_cues: Lie on your back, heels in the cradles.; Press heels down and lift hips high.; Pause at the top, then lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back; Legs swinging
safety: Keep the straps still before lifting.

name: Assisted dip
form_cues: Kneel or stand on the pad and grip the dip handles.; Lower until upper arms are about parallel to the floor.; Press back up, leaning slightly forward for chest.
common_mistakes: Going too deep and straining the shoulders.; Shrugging at the bottom.
safety: More counterweight makes it easier; stop short of any shoulder pinch.
notes: Reduce the assistance over time as you get stronger.

name: Decline chest press machine
form_cues: Set the seat so handles start at lower chest.; Press down and forward until arms are nearly straight.; Return slowly and keep the chest proud.
common_mistakes: Letting shoulders roll forward.; Rushing the lowering phase.
progressions: Decline bench press; Iso-lateral decline press
safety: Use the foot lever or a partner to get into position if the start is deep.
notes: Nearest app gear id is the seated chest press machine.

name: Incline press machine
form_cues: Set the seat so handles start at upper chest.; Press up and slightly in, keeping shoulders down.; Lower slowly until hands are level with the chest.
common_mistakes: Seat too low, turning it into a shoulder press.; Shrugging at the top.
progressions: Iso-lateral incline press; Incline dumbbell press
safety: Keep shoulder blades back to protect the front of the shoulder.
aliases: Incline chest press machine; Machine incline press

name: Iso-lateral chest press
equipment: Plate-loaded chest press machine; Weight plates
form_cues: Load both sides evenly and set handles at mid-chest.; Drive the arms forward along their curved path together.; Lower slowly to a deep chest stretch.
common_mistakes: One arm doing more of the work.; Bouncing out of the bottom.
progressions: Single-arm machine chest press; Barbell bench press
safety: Make sure the arms are both on their stops before you load or unload plates.
aliases: Hammer Strength chest press; Plate-loaded chest press
notes: Independent arms help fix left-right imbalances.

name: Iso-lateral decline press
equipment: Plate-loaded decline press machine; Weight plates
form_cues: Load both sides evenly before sitting down.; Press down and out along the arc together.; Lower with control to a full stretch.
common_mistakes: Pushing with one side more than the other.; Losing upper-back tightness.
safety: Make sure both arms are resting on their stops before loading.

name: Iso-lateral incline press
equipment: Plate-loaded incline press machine; Weight plates
form_cues: Set the seat so handles sit at upper-chest level.; Drive both arms up evenly.; Lower under control to a deep upper-chest stretch.
common_mistakes: Uneven loading or pressing.; Bouncing at the bottom.
safety: Rack both arms before getting up or changing plates.
aliases: Hammer Strength incline press; Plate-loaded incline press
notes: Arms can be pressed one at a time for unilateral work.

name: Lying chest press machine
form_cues: Lie with handles in line with your mid-chest.; Keep feet flat and upper back tight on the pad.; Press up, then lower slowly to a stretch.
common_mistakes: Arching hard off the bench.; Locking out aggressively.
safety: Make sure the starting position is safe before unracking.
aliases: Lying machine bench press; Supine chest press
notes: Mimics the bench press with no need for a spotter.

name: Pec deck fly
form_cues: Set the seat so handles are at chest height.; Keep a slight bend in the elbows and hug the handles together.; Open slowly until you feel a stretch, then squeeze back.
common_mistakes: Letting the arms travel far behind the body.; Pressing with the hands instead of moving at the shoulder.
progressions: Single-arm pec deck fly; Cable crossover fly
safety: Limit the backward stretch if you have shoulder pain.
aliases: Pec deck; Butterfly machine; Machine fly
notes: Pause one second at the squeeze for more chest work.

name: Seated chest press machine
form_cues: Set the seat so handles are level with mid-chest.; Keep shoulder blades back and down against the pad.; Press out, then return slowly until you feel a stretch.
common_mistakes: Seat set too low or high.; Elbows flaring straight out to the sides.
progressions: Iso-lateral chest press; Barbell bench press
safety: Set the seat height before loading, and keep wrists stacked over elbows.
aliases: Machine chest press; Vertical chest press
notes: A safe way to train chest to failure without a spotter.

name: Single-arm machine chest press
form_cues: Brace your free hand on the seat or your hip.; Press one handle forward without twisting your torso.; Lower slowly and keep the shoulder blade pinned.
common_mistakes: Rotating the body to finish the rep.; Using momentum from the hips.
safety: Keep the torso square to stop the lower back twisting.
notes: Best on machines with independent arms.

name: Single-arm pec deck fly
form_cues: Sit side-on or square and hold the frame with your free hand.; Sweep one handle across your body past midline.; Return slowly to a controlled stretch.
common_mistakes: Twisting the torso to move the weight.; Using too much load to cross midline.
safety: Keep the shoulder down and back throughout.
notes: Crossing past midline gives a stronger peak contraction than two-arm flies.

name: Wide chest press machine
equipment: Plate-loaded wide chest press machine; Weight plates
form_cues: Grip the wide handles with elbows slightly below shoulders.; Press forward and in, squeezing the chest.; Return slowly to a full stretch across the chest.
common_mistakes: Shoulders rolling forward at the top.; Short, choppy reps.
safety: Avoid an aggressive stretch if your shoulders are sensitive.
aliases: Hammer Strength wide chest; Plate-loaded wide chest press
notes: The wider path puts more emphasis on the outer chest stretch than a standard chest press.

name: Assisted chin-up
form_cues: Grip shoulder-width with palms facing you.; Drive elbows down and bring chin over the bar.; Lower all the way to straight arms.
common_mistakes: Craning the neck to reach the bar.; Dropping fast on the way down.
safety: Keep the shoulders active at the bottom rather than hanging loose.
notes: Biceps help more here, so most people find it easier than the pull-up.

name: Assisted pull-up
form_cues: Grip just outside shoulder width, palms forward.; Pull your chest towards the bar, elbows down to your ribs.; Lower slowly to fully straight arms.
common_mistakes: Half reps that skip the bottom stretch.; Swinging or kicking.
safety: Step on and off the pad carefully; more counterweight means more help.
notes: Cut the assistance by one plate when you can do 3 x 10.

name: Back extension
form_cues: Set the pad just below your hip bones.; Hinge down with a flat back, then rise until body is straight.; Squeeze glutes at the top without over-arching.
common_mistakes: Hyperextending past straight at the top.; Jerking up fast.
progressions: Weighted back extension; GHD back extension
safety: Don't arch past a straight line; stop if you feel sharp back pain.
aliases: 45-degree back extension; Hyperextension; Roman chair back extension
notes: Hold a plate to your chest to add load.

name: Chest-supported row machine
form_cues: Set the chest pad so you can just reach the handles.; Pull elbows back and squeeze shoulder blades together.; Let the arms straighten slowly and the shoulders reach forward.
common_mistakes: Lifting the chest off the pad.; Shrugging instead of pulling back.
safety: Chest support takes load off the lower back.
notes: Neutral grip hits lats more; wide overhand hits upper back more.

name: Chest-supported T-bar row
equipment: Chest-supported T-bar row machine; Weight plates
form_cues: Lie chest-down on the pad with feet on the platform.; Row the handles up until elbows pass your torso.; Lower all the way to straight arms.
common_mistakes: Lifting the chest off the pad.; Jerking the first part of the rep.
safety: Step on the platform carefully and keep your chin neutral.
aliases: Incline T-bar row; Lying T-bar row
notes: Easier on the lower back than the standing T-bar row.

name: GHD back extension
form_cues: Set the pad at your hips with feet locked under the rollers.; Lower your torso towards the floor with a flat back.; Rise until your body is horizontal, not higher.
common_mistakes: Swinging up past horizontal.; Rounding fast at the bottom.
safety: Lift no higher than straight; this horizontal version is harder than 45 degrees.
aliases: 90-degree back extension; GHD hyperextension; Horizontal back extension

name: Iso-lateral D.Y. row
equipment: Plate-loaded D.Y. row machine; Weight plates
form_cues: Set the chest pad so you reach the handles with straight arms.; Pull with an underhand or neutral grip towards your waist.; Lower under control for a full stretch.
common_mistakes: Using the legs to drive the weight.; Cutting the stretch short.
safety: Keep the chest supported to protect the lower back.
aliases: Hammer Strength DY row; Dorian Yates row machine
notes: Mimics the underhand barbell row made popular by Dorian Yates.

name: Iso-lateral front lat pulldown
form_cues: Lock your thighs under the pads.; Pull the handles down towards your shoulders, elbows to ribs.; Let the arms rise slowly to a full stretch.
common_mistakes: Leaning back a lot to cheat.; Not letting the arms straighten.
safety: Control the return so the plates don't yank your shoulders.
notes: No exact app gear id; nearest is the lat pulldown machine.

name: Iso-lateral high row
equipment: Plate-loaded high row machine; Weight plates
form_cues: Secure your thighs under the pads.; Pull the handles down and back towards your lower chest.; Return slowly with a full stretch overhead.
common_mistakes: Leaning way back to cheat.; Pulling with the hands rather than driving elbows.
safety: Keep the chest up and avoid jerky reps.
aliases: Hammer Strength high row; Machine high row
notes: Sits between a pulldown and a row; great for lat width. App gear id is the nearest match.

name: Iso-lateral low row
equipment: Plate-loaded low row machine; Weight plates
form_cues: Sit with chest on the pad and grab the low handles.; Row elbows back past your torso towards your hips.; Reach forward slowly for a full lat stretch.
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back.; Flaring elbows wide.
safety: Keep your chest on the pad the whole time.
aliases: Hammer Strength low row; Machine low row
notes: The low-to-high path biases the lower lats.

name: Iso-lateral row
form_cues: Keep your chest on the pad and feet planted.; Row the handles back towards your hips.; Reach forward fully on the way back for a lat stretch.
common_mistakes: Jerking the weight with the torso.; Short range at the front.
safety: Load both sides evenly before starting.
notes: Arms can be worked one at a time.

name: Machine shrug
form_cues: Stand tall with arms straight holding the handles.; Lift shoulders straight up towards the ears.; Pause, then lower slowly to a full stretch.
common_mistakes: Rolling the shoulders in circles.; Bending the elbows to pull.
safety: Keep the neck neutral; don't jut your chin forward.

name: Pullover machine
form_cues: Set the seat so your shoulders line up with the pivot.; Drive the elbows down in an arc to your stomach.; Return slowly to a deep overhead stretch.
common_mistakes: Pulling with the hands instead of the elbows.; Arching the lower back at the top.
safety: Limit the top stretch if overhead positions hurt your shoulders.
notes: No exact app gear id; nearest is the lat pulldown machine. Trains lats without the biceps tiring first.

name: Seated back extension machine
form_cues: Sit with the pad across your upper back and feet secure.; Push back slowly until your torso is upright or slightly past.; Return to the start with control.
common_mistakes: Jerking back with momentum.; Using too much weight.
safety: Use a light load and slow reps; skip if it aggravates back pain.
aliases: Lower back machine; Lumbar extension machine
notes: No exact app gear id; nearest is the Roman chair.

name: Wide-grip machine row
primary_muscles: Upper back; Rear delts; Mid traps
form_cues: Grip the wide handles with palms facing down.; Pull elbows out and back to shoulder height.; Squeeze shoulder blades, then return slowly.
common_mistakes: Shrugging up towards the ears.; Pulling to the belly instead of the chest.
safety: Keep the neck relaxed and chin tucked.
aliases: Upper back machine row; Wide machine row
notes: Targets the upper back more than the lats.

name: Iso-lateral shoulder press
equipment: Plate-loaded shoulder press machine; Weight plates
form_cues: Load both sides evenly and sit tall.; Press both handles overhead along their arc.; Lower slowly to shoulder height.
common_mistakes: One side drifting ahead.; Shrugging at the top.
safety: Rack both arms before standing up.
aliases: Hammer Strength shoulder press; Plate-loaded shoulder press
notes: Press one arm at a time to even out imbalances.

name: Lateral raise machine
form_cues: Line your shoulders up with the machine's pivot.; Raise the arms out to shoulder height, leading with the elbows.; Lower slowly without letting the stack rest.
common_mistakes: Shrugging the weight up with traps.; Swinging the torso.
progressions: Single-arm machine lateral raise; Cable lateral raise
safety: Stop at shoulder height if raising higher pinches.
aliases: Machine lateral raise; Side raise machine
notes: Keeps constant tension through the whole range.

name: Machine rear delt row
form_cues: Use a wide overhand grip and set your chest on the pad.; Row with elbows flared out to shoulder level.; Squeeze the back of the shoulders, then lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Turning it into a regular row with elbows in.; Using too much weight.
safety: Keep it light and controlled; the rear delts are small.

name: Machine upright row
form_cues: Grip slightly wider than shoulders.; Lead with the elbows up to about shoulder height.; Lower slowly to straight arms.
common_mistakes: Pulling elbows above shoulder level.; Narrow grip causing shoulder pinch.
safety: Stop at shoulder height and skip it if you feel a pinch.

name: Rear delt machine
form_cues: Face the pad with handles at shoulder height.; Sweep arms back in a wide arc, slight bend in elbows.; Return slowly without letting the stack touch.
common_mistakes: Squeezing shoulder blades so traps take over.; Using momentum.
progressions: Single-arm reverse pec deck; Reverse cable fly
safety: Use moderate weight; the rear delts are small.
aliases: Reverse pec deck; Reverse fly machine; Rear delt fly
notes: Most pec decks double as a rear delt machine with the handles reversed.

name: Seated shoulder press machine
form_cues: Set the seat so handles start just above shoulder level.; Press up without locking out hard.; Lower slowly until hands are near the shoulders.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back off the pad.; Seat too high so the range is short.
progressions: Iso-lateral shoulder press; Seated dumbbell shoulder press
safety: Keep the back flat on the pad.
aliases: Machine shoulder press; Machine overhead press

name: Single-arm machine lateral raise
form_cues: Sit tall and work one arm at a time.; Raise the elbow out to shoulder height.; Lower slowly and keep the shoulder down.
common_mistakes: Leaning away to cheat.; Rushing reps.
safety: Keep the weight modest and the shoulder relaxed.

name: Single-arm reverse pec deck
form_cues: Sit side-on or square and grip the opposite handle.; Sweep the arm back across your body to shoulder line.; Return slowly to the start.
common_mistakes: Twisting the torso.; Pulling past the line of the body.
safety: Keep the shoulder down and the movement smooth.
notes: Reaching across the body gives a longer range than the two-arm version.

name: Bicep curl machine
form_cues: Line your elbows up with the machine's pivot.; Curl up and squeeze the biceps at the top.; Lower slowly until arms are nearly straight.
common_mistakes: Lifting elbows off the pad.; Half reps at the top.
safety: Don't let the weight drop at the bottom.

name: Overhead triceps extension machine
form_cues: Sit with elbows pointing up and resting on the pad.; Extend the arms until straight overhead.; Lower slowly to a deep triceps stretch.
common_mistakes: Elbows drifting wide.; Arching the lower back.
safety: Limit the stretch if the elbows or shoulders feel irritated.
notes: Overhead position stretches the long head of the triceps.

name: Seated dip machine
form_cues: Sit tall with your back on the pad and grip the handles.; Press down until arms are straight, elbows close to sides.; Let the handles rise slowly to about 90 degrees.
common_mistakes: Elbows flaring wide.; Leaning forward and pushing with shoulders.
safety: Don't let the handles rise so high that your shoulders roll forward.
aliases: Triceps dip machine; Seated triceps press
notes: No exact app gear id; nearest is the tricep extension machine.

name: Single-arm machine curl
form_cues: Work one arm at a time with the elbow on the pad.; Curl up fully and squeeze.; Lower slowly to a full stretch.
common_mistakes: Shifting the body to help.; Rushing the lowering.
safety: Keep the wrist straight.
notes: Best on machines with independent handles.

name: Tricep extension machine
form_cues: Line your elbows up with the machine's pivot.; Push the handles down until arms are straight.; Return slowly without letting elbows lift off the pad.
common_mistakes: Shoulders rolling forward.; Bouncing at the top.
