progressions: Overhead triceps extension machine; Rope pushdown
safety: Keep the elbows fixed on the pad.
aliases: Machine triceps extension; Seated triceps extension machine

name: Belt squat
form_cues: Attach the belt low around your hips and stand tall.; Squat down keeping torso upright.; Drive up through mid-foot.
common_mistakes: Leaning forward.; Belt riding up onto the lower back.
safety: Great option when the spine needs a break; unhook the belt only when the lever is racked.
aliases: Belt squat machine; Hip belt squat
notes: Loads the legs without compressing the spine.

name: Belt squat march
form_cues: Stand tall with the belt loaded and knees soft.; March in place, lifting knees to hip height.; Keep hips level and steady.
common_mistakes: Shuffling feet instead of driving knees.; Leaning back.
safety: Keep the load moderate and stop if form breaks.
notes: A conditioning and hip-stability finisher.

name: Donkey calf raise
form_cues: Hinge forward with hips under the pad and back flat.; Rise high on your toes.; Lower to a deep stretch.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back.; Short reps.
safety: Keep the spine neutral.
notes: No exact app gear id; nearest is the standing calf machine.

name: Glute-ham raise
form_cues: Lock feet in with knees just behind the pad.; Start upright, then lower forward with a straight line hips to head.; Pull yourself back up by digging toes into the plate.
common_mistakes: Bending at the hips to cheat.; Dropping uncontrolled on the way down.
safety: Build up slowly; push off a box or use a band if you can't control the lowering.
notes: One of the best hamstring builders for knee flexion and hip extension together.

name: Hack squat
form_cues: Set shoulders under the pads and feet shoulder-width.; Lower until thighs are at least parallel, back flat.; Drive up through mid-foot without locking out.
common_mistakes: Heels lifting.; Hips sliding off the back pad.
safety: Engage the safety catches before you start.
aliases: Machine hack squat; Plate-loaded hack squat

name: Hack squat calf raise
form_cues: Stand with balls of feet on the platform edge.; Rise high and pause.; Lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Bending the knees.; Bouncing.
safety: Watch foot placement on the edge.

name: Hip adduction machine
form_cues: Sit tall with pads on the inside of your knees.; Squeeze the legs together.; Open slowly to a comfortable stretch.
common_mistakes: Letting the weight snap open.; Leaning forward.
safety: Don't force a stretch past what's comfortable.

name: Kneeling leg curl
form_cues: Kneel with forearms on the pads and heel under the roller.; Curl the heel up towards your glute.; Lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back.; Using momentum.
safety: Keep the hips steady.
notes: No exact app gear id; nearest is the lying leg curl machine.

name: Leg extension
form_cues: Line your knee up with the pivot and set the pad on your lower shins.; Extend fully and squeeze the quads.; Lower slowly over two to three seconds.
common_mistakes: Swinging the weight up.; Hips lifting off the seat.
safety: Use moderate loads if you have knee pain.

name: Leg press
form_cues: Place feet shoulder-width in the middle of the platform.; Lower until knees reach about 90 degrees, hips stay down.; Press through the whole foot without locking the knees.
common_mistakes: Lower back peeling off the pad at the bottom.; Knees caving in.
safety: Never lock out hard, and keep the safety handles in reach.

name: Leg press calf raise
form_cues: Place the balls of your feet on the bottom edge of the platform.; Keep knees soft and press through the toes.; Lower heels slowly for a deep stretch.
common_mistakes: Bending the knees to move the weight.; Bouncing reps.
safety: Keep the safety handles locked; feet can slip off the edge.
aliases: Calf press; Leg press calf press

name: Lying leg curl
form_cues: Lie face down with knees just off the pad's edge.; Curl heels towards your glutes, hips pressed down.; Lower slowly until legs are almost straight.
common_mistakes: Hips lifting off the pad.; Dropping the weight.
progressions: Single-leg lying leg curl; Nordic hamstring curl
safety: Keep the hips down to protect the lower back.
aliases: Prone leg curl; Lying hamstring curl

name: Narrow-stance leg press
form_cues: Place feet hip-width or closer, low on the platform.; Lower slowly, letting knees travel forward.; Press up through the whole foot.
common_mistakes: Heels lifting off the platform.; Going so deep the lower back rounds.
safety: Skip low foot placement if it bothers your knees.
aliases: Close-stance leg press; Quad-focus leg press

name: Pendulum squat
form_cues: Set shoulders under the pads with feet forward on the platform.; Sink deep with the arc, knees travelling forward.; Drive back up without locking out.
common_mistakes: Shallow reps.; Feet set too far back so heels lift.
safety: Use the safety lock; depth is deep, so build up gradually.
notes: Very quad-dominant with little load on the spine.

name: Seated calf raise
form_cues: Set the pad snug on your lower thighs.; Rise high onto the balls of your feet.; Lower slowly to a deep stretch.
common_mistakes: Bouncing reps.; Partial range.
safety: Release the safety lever only once the pad is set.
notes: Bent knees bias the soleus.

name: Seated leg curl
form_cues: Lock the thigh pad down firmly.; Curl the heels down and back as far as you can.; Return slowly to almost straight legs.
common_mistakes: Thigh pad set too loose.; Leaning back to cheat.
safety: Lean forward slightly for more hamstring stretch.
notes: The seated position stretches the hamstrings more than lying.

name: Seated leg press machine
form_cues: Set the seat so knees start at about 90 degrees.; Push through mid-foot until legs are nearly straight.; Return slowly without letting the stack slam.
common_mistakes: Seat too close so the hips round.; Locking the knees.
safety: Keep the lower back on the pad.
aliases: Horizontal leg press; Selectorized leg press
notes: A gentle starting point for beginners.

name: Single-leg calf raise machine
form_cues: Stand on one foot on the edge.; Rise high and pause at the top.; Lower slowly to a full stretch.
common_mistakes: Bending the knee.; Short range.
safety: Keep a light grip on the handles for balance.

name: Single-leg leg extension
form_cues: Work one leg at a time with the other relaxed.; Extend fully and pause.; Lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Twisting the hips.; Rushing the lowering.
safety: Go lighter than half your two-leg weight to start.

name: Single-leg leg press
form_cues: Place one foot in the middle of the platform.; Lower slowly, keeping the knee in line with the toes.; Press up without locking out.
common_mistakes: Hips twisting.; Knee caving inward.
safety: Use much lighter weight than two-leg pressing.
notes: Great for spotting and fixing side-to-side differences.

name: Single-leg lying leg curl
form_cues: Work one leg at a time with hips square.; Curl the heel up fully.; Lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Hip on the working side lifting.; Jerky reps.
safety: Start light; it's easy to strain a hamstring with jerky reps.

name: Single-leg seated calf raise
form_cues: Place one foot on the platform under the pad.; Rise as high as possible.; Lower slowly to a deep stretch.
common_mistakes: Bouncing.; Leaning onto the pad.
safety: Keep the pad secure.

name: Single-leg seated leg curl
form_cues: Lock the thigh pad down and work one leg.; Curl the heel back fully.; Return slowly.
common_mistakes: Twisting in the seat.; Partial reps.
safety: Keep the pad tight on the thighs.

name: Standing calf raise
form_cues: Stand with balls of feet on the edge and shoulders under the pads.; Rise as high as you can and pause.; Lower slowly to a deep heel stretch.
common_mistakes: Bouncing at the bottom.; Bending the knees.
progressions: Single-leg calf raise machine; Donkey calf raise
safety: Pause at the bottom to avoid Achilles strain.
aliases: Standing calf raise machine; Machine calf raise

name: Standing leg curl
form_cues: Stand tall with the pad behind your ankle.; Curl the heel up towards your glute.; Lower slowly without swinging.
common_mistakes: Hip flexing forward.; Leaning the torso.
safety: Hold the handles and keep the hips square.
aliases: Standing single-leg curl; Standing hamstring curl
notes: No exact app gear id; nearest is the lying leg curl machine.

name: V-squat
form_cues: Stand on the platform with shoulders under the pads.; Squat down with a slight lean following the machine's arc.; Press up through the whole foot.
common_mistakes: Heels lifting.; Short range.
safety: Use the safety catches.
notes: No exact app gear id; nearest is the hack squat machine.

name: Vertical leg press
form_cues: Lie flat with hips directly under the platform.; Unlock and lower the platform towards your chest.; Press straight up without locking the knees.
common_mistakes: Lifting the hips off the floor pad.; Going too deep and rounding.
safety: Always use the safety stops; this machine loads straight down onto you.

name: GHD hip extension
form_cues: Set the pad so your hips hang just off the front.; Hinge down from the hips, keeping the spine neutral.; Squeeze glutes to bring your body back to straight.
common_mistakes: Rounding and un-rounding the spine.; Overextending at the top.
safety: Keep the motion at the hips; stop if the lower back takes over.
aliases: GHD hip raise; Hip extension on GHD

name: Glute kickback machine
form_cues: Set the pad behind your knee or foot.; Drive the leg back and up.; Return slowly.
common_mistakes: Arching the back.; Swinging.
safety: Brace the core to protect the lower back.

name: Glute-focused back extension
form_cues: Turn feet out and keep chin tucked, upper back slightly rounded.; Lower by hinging at the hips.; Drive hips into the pad by squeezing the glutes.
common_mistakes: Using the lower back to lift.; Setting the pad too high so you can't hinge.
safety: Keep the movement at the hips, not the lower back.
notes: Setting the pad lower on the thighs lets the hips move more.

name: High-foot leg press
form_cues: Place feet high on the platform, hip-width.; Lower until hips are deeply flexed but still on the pad.; Push through the heels to the top.
common_mistakes: Tailbone lifting off the seat.; Heels lifting.
safety: Stop the descent before your lower back rounds.
notes: Moving feet higher shifts work from quads to glutes and hamstrings.

name: Hip abduction machine
form_cues: Sit tall with pads on the outside of your knees.; Push the legs apart.; Return slowly.
common_mistakes: Using momentum.; Bouncing reps.
safety: Keep the movement smooth.

name: Hip thrust machine
form_cues: Set the belt across your hips and feet flat.; Drive hips up until body is straight.; Lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Overarching the lower back.; Feet set too far forward.
safety: Tuck the chin and keep ribs down.
aliases: Glute drive machine; Machine hip thrust

name: Leaning hip abduction
form_cues: Sit and lean forward from the hips, holding the frame.; Push the knees out.; Return slowly.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back.; Using momentum.
safety: Keep the back flat.
notes: Leaning forward shifts work towards the upper glute max.

name: Multi-hip abduction
form_cues: Stand tall with the pad on the outside of your thigh.; Lift the leg sideways.; Lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Leaning the torso.; Swinging.
safety: Hold the handles for balance.
notes: No exact app gear id; nearest is the abductor machine.

name: Multi-hip glute extension
form_cues: Stand tall with the pad behind your thigh.; Drive the leg back.; Return slowly.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back.; Swinging.
safety: Brace the core.
notes: No exact app gear id; nearest is the glute kickback machine.

name: Reverse hack squat
form_cues: Face the back pad with chest on it and shoulders under the pads.; Sit hips back and down, keeping chest on the pad.; Drive up through the heels.
common_mistakes: Chest coming off the pad.; Cutting depth short.
safety: Use the safety stops and start light.
notes: More hip hinge than the regular hack squat, so the glutes work harder.

name: Reverse hyper
form_cues: Lie chest-down with hips at the pad's edge and grip the handles.; Swing legs up until in line with the body, squeezing glutes.; Lower under control; don't let the pendulum yank you.
common_mistakes: Letting momentum drive the swing.; Overarching at the top.
safety: Start light; the strap and pendulum can whip the spine if you go too heavy.
notes: Popular as a lower-back rehab and strength accessory.

name: Single-leg back extension
form_cues: Hook one foot under the roller, other leg free.; Hinge down slowly with hips square.; Rise by driving the working hip into the pad.
common_mistakes: Hips twisting open.; Bouncing at the bottom.
safety: Go slowly; the single leg makes balance harder.

name: Single-leg hip thrust machine
form_cues: Set up as normal and lift one foot off.; Drive the hips up through the planted heel.; Lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Hips tilting.; Arching.
safety: Use much lighter load than two-leg.

name: Wide-stance leg press
form_cues: Place feet wide with toes turned out slightly.; Lower with knees tracking over the toes.; Drive through the heels to press up.
common_mistakes: Knees collapsing inward.; Hips lifting off the seat.
safety: Only go as deep as your hips allow without rounding.

name: Archer push-up
form_cues: Set hands very wide with fingers turned slightly out.; Shift down toward one hand while the other arm stays straight.; Press back up through the bent arm, then switch sides.
common_mistakes: Bending the 'straight' arm to help; Twisting the hips toward the floor
safety: Warm up wrists and shoulders well before loading one side.
notes: A key step toward the one-arm push-up.

name: Hindu push-up
form_cues: Start in a downward-dog shape with hips high.; Swoop your chest low and forward between your hands.; Finish in an upward arch, then push hips back up to start.
common_mistakes: Collapsing into the lower back at the top; Bending the arms only, without the swoop
safety: Skip the arched finish if you have lower back pain.
notes: Traditional Indian wrestling exercise; pairs well with Hindu squats.

name: One-arm push-up
form_cues: Spread feet wide and place one hand under your chest.; Put the free hand behind your back and brace hard.; Lower with control, keeping hips square, then press up.
common_mistakes: Rotating the torso to cheat the rep; Feet too close together
safety: Build up slowly with incline versions to protect the shoulder.
notes: Elevate the hand on a bench to regress.

name: Spiderman push-up
form_cues: Start in a strong push-up position.; As you lower, bring one knee toward the same-side elbow.; Return the leg as you press up; alternate sides.
common_mistakes: Letting the hips rotate or sag; Rushing so the chest doesn't reach the bottom
safety: Keep the movement slow if your hips are tight.

name: Typewriter push-up
form_cues: Set hands very wide and lower to the bottom of a push-up.; Slide your chest across to one hand, then the other, staying low.; Return to centre and press up.
common_mistakes: Rising up while shifting sideways; Hips sagging during the slide
safety: Stop if you feel pinching in the shoulder at the bottom.

name: Advanced tuck planche
form_cues: Start from a tuck planche.; Open the hips so the back is flat and level.; Keep arms locked and hips at shoulder height.
common_mistakes: Back rounding up like a regular tuck; Hips dropping
safety: Build up over months; stop with any elbow pain.

name: Dive bomber push-up
form_cues: Start with hips high and arms straight, like a downward dog.; Dive your chest close to the floor, sweeping forward.; Reverse the path back to the start instead of pushing straight up.
common_mistakes: Dropping straight down without the sweep; Letting elbows flare wide
safety: Move slowly at first; it is tough on stiff shoulders.
notes: Unlike the Hindu push-up, the bomber returns along the same path.

name: Elevated pike push-up
form_cues: Put feet on a box and walk hands back until hips are over shoulders.; Lower your head in front of your hands, forming a tripod.; Press up to straight arms, keeping hips stacked.
common_mistakes: Hips drifting back behind the hands; Head lowering directly between hands
safety: Use a box that cannot slide; keep the neck neutral.
aliases: Feet-elevated pike push-up; Box pike push-up

name: Freestanding handstand
form_cues: Kick up softly with straight arms.; Balance using your fingertips and heels of the hands.; Squeeze legs together and keep a straight body line.
common_mistakes: Over-arching the back; Bent elbows
progressions: Freestanding handstand push-up; Press to handstand
safety: Practise bailing out (cartwheel or roll) before kicking up away from a wall.

name: Freestanding handstand push-up
form_cues: Hold a steady freestanding handstand first.; Lower in control, keeping balance over your hands.; Press up while staying stacked.
common_mistakes: Losing balance at the bottom; Arching the back to press
safety: Elite skill: use a soft floor and know how to bail.

name: Frog stand
form_cues: Squat down and place hands flat, shoulder-width.; Rest knees on the backs of your bent elbows.; Lean forward until feet float, eyes slightly ahead.
common_mistakes: Looking straight down and tipping over; Not leaning enough
safety: Put a pillow in front of your face while learning.
notes: Gateway to arm balances; yoga calls a similar pose crow.

name: Full planche
form_cues: Lean far forward with locked arms.; Hold legs together and straight behind you.; Keep the whole body level just above the floor.
common_mistakes: Arched lower back; Bent arms
safety: One of the hardest bodyweight skills; train years, not weeks.

name: Handstand push-up
form_cues: Kick up into a handstand with your back to the wall.; Lower your head to the floor with elbows angled forward.; Press back up to straight arms.
common_mistakes: Crashing the head into the floor; Elbows flaring out wide
regressions: Elevated pike push-up; Wall handstand hold
progressions: Deficit handstand push-up; Freestanding handstand push-up
safety: Place a folded mat under your head; build up with negatives first.

name: Pike push-up
form_cues: Walk feet in so hips are high and you form an upside-down V.; Lower the top of your head toward a spot ahead of your hands.; Press back up, keeping hips high.
common_mistakes: Letting hips drop into a push-up shape; Elbows flaring straight out
safety: Lower slowly so you don't bump your head.

name: Planche lean
form_cues: From a push-up, turn fingers out and lean shoulders past your hands.; Keep arms locked and shoulder blades pushed apart.; Hold the lean without letting hips sag.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows; Leaning only a little
safety: Warm wrists well and build lean distance slowly.

name: Planche push-up
form_cues: Hold a tuck or straddle planche with arms straight.; Bend elbows to lower your chest while staying parallel.; Press back up without losing the lean.
common_mistakes: Feet touching down during the rep; Shoulders not leaning past the hands
safety: Elite skill: build up over months and stop at any wrist or elbow pain.
notes: Parallettes ease the wrists; the tuck version is the usual first step.

name: Press to handstand
form_cues: Start with hands down, hips high, legs straight or straddled.; Lean shoulders forward until your feet lift without jumping.; Raise legs slowly into a straight handstand.
common_mistakes: Jumping into it; Bending the arms
safety: Requires good hamstring flexibility; warm up wrists and hips.

name: Pseudo planche push-up
form_cues: Turn fingers out and place hands beside your waist.; Lean shoulders forward past your hands and keep that lean.; Lower and press while keeping arms locked in line at the top.
common_mistakes: Losing the forward lean as you push; Bending at the hips
safety: Warm up wrists thoroughly; the lean puts big stress on them.
notes: Main pushing drill for planche training.

name: Straddle planche
form_cues: Lean forward and lift legs straight and wide.; Keep the body parallel to the floor.; Lock arms and push the floor away.
common_mistakes: Hips piking up; Bent knees
safety: Elite skill; protect elbows and wrists with gradual volume.

name: Tuck planche
form_cues: Hands under shoulders, knees tucked tight to the chest.; Lean forward until feet lift, arms locked.; Round the upper back and push the floor away.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows; Resting knees on the arms (that is a frog stand)
safety: Parallettes are kinder on the wrists.

name: Wall handstand hold
form_cues: Walk up into a handstand facing the wall.; Push the floor away, ears covered by your arms.; Squeeze legs and glutes into a straight line.
common_mistakes: Banana-shaped back; Bent arms or sunken shoulders
regressions: Wall walk; Pike hold on box
safety: Practise on a soft floor; learn to roll or cartwheel out.
notes: Chest-to-wall teaches better alignment than back-to-wall.

name: Wall walk
form_cues: Start in a push-up with feet at the wall.; Walk feet up the wall and hands back toward it.; Stop with chest near the wall, then walk back down slowly.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back; Rushing the descent
safety: Clear the area and keep a soft surface around you.

name: Sphinx push-up
form_cues: Start on forearms in a plank, hands slightly ahead of elbows.; Press through palms to straighten your arms.; Lower back onto the forearms slowly.
common_mistakes: Pushing with the hips instead of the arms; Hands placed too far forward
safety: Start from the knees if your elbows feel strained.

name: Tiger bend push-up
form_cues: Start in a handstand against a wall.; Lower onto your forearms with control.; Press back up to straight arms.
common_mistakes: Collapsing onto the head; Lowering too fast
safety: Only attempt with a solid wall handstand and a soft surface.
notes: Classic old-school strength feat.

name: Box pistol squat
form_cues: Stand on one leg in front of a box, other leg reaching forward.; Sit back slowly until you lightly touch the box.; Stand up without rocking or using momentum.
common_mistakes: Dropping onto the box; Knee caving inward
safety: Lower the box height gradually as you get stronger.
aliases: Single-leg box squat; Pistol to box

name: Hindu squat
form_cues: Swing arms back as you squat and let heels rise.; Touch fingers near your heels at the bottom.; Drive up, swinging arms forward, in a smooth rhythm.
common_mistakes: Bouncing hard at the bottom; Holding your breath
safety: Stay on the balls of the feet only if your knees are pain-free.
notes: Traditional high-rep conditioning squat from Indian wrestling.

name: Pistol squat
form_cues: Stand on one leg with the other straight out in front.; Reach arms forward and sink all the way down.; Drive up through the whole foot, keeping the free leg off the floor.
common_mistakes: Heel lifting at the bottom; Knee collapsing inward
safety: Raise the heel on a small plate if ankle mobility limits depth.
notes: Holding a light weight in front can actually help balance.

name: Shrimp squat
form_cues: Stand on one leg and hold the other foot behind you.; Lower until the back knee touches the floor softly.; Drive up through the front foot, staying tall.
common_mistakes: Crashing the knee into the floor; Leaning far forward
safety: Put a cushion under the back knee while learning.

name: Elbow lever
form_cues: Tuck elbows into your belly near the hips.; Lean forward until the legs lift.; Hold the body straight and level.
common_mistakes: Elbows sliding apart; Looking down and tipping
safety: Put a cushion in front of your face while learning.

name: L-sit
form_cues: Press hands down beside hips and lift your body.; Hold legs straight and level with the floor.; Keep shoulders pushed down away from the ears.
common_mistakes: Shrugging shoulders; Bent knees
safety: Parallettes or dip bars make it easier than the floor.

name: V-sit
form_cues: From an L-sit, lean shoulders back.; Raise straight legs higher toward your face.; Push hard through the hands to keep hips high.
common_mistakes: Bending the knees; Collapsing the shoulders
safety: Needs strong hamstring flexibility; progress slowly.

name: Chest dips
form_cues: Support on the bars and lean your torso forward.; Lower until shoulders are just below elbows.; Press up, squeezing the chest.
common_mistakes: Going too deep and straining the shoulders; Flaring elbows
safety: Skip or shorten the range if you have shoulder pain.

name: Parallette push-up
form_cues: Grip parallettes under your shoulders in a push-up.; Lower your chest below hand height for extra range.; Press back up to straight arms.
common_mistakes: Going deeper than shoulders tolerate; Sagging hips
safety: Make sure the parallettes are on a non-slip surface.
notes: Neutral grip is easy on the wrists.

name: Straight bar dip
form_cues: Support yourself on top of a straight bar with straight arms.; Lean forward and lower until the bar touches your upper belly.; Press back up to straight arms.
common_mistakes: Staying too upright and falling off; Shallow reps
safety: Needs a solid bar at around hip height.
notes: Essential for the muscle-up transition.

name: Advanced tuck front lever
form_cues: From a tuck lever, open your hips so thighs are vertical.; Keep the back flat and level.; Press the bar down with straight arms.
common_mistakes: Back rounding; Hips sagging
safety: Progress slowly to protect elbows and shoulders.

name: Archer pull-up
form_cues: Use a very wide grip.; Pull up toward one hand while the other arm stays nearly straight.; Lower and switch sides.
common_mistakes: Bending the straight arm; Swinging to the side
safety: Warm up elbows; the straight arm is under a lot of stress.

name: Back lever
secondary_muscles: Abs; Glutes; Lower back; Rear delts
form_cues: Enter from skin the cat and extend legs behind.; Hold your straight body horizontal, face down.; Squeeze glutes and keep arms locked.
common_mistakes: Piked hips; Elbows bending
safety: Build up through tuck and straddle versions to protect the biceps tendon.

name: Band-assisted pull-up
form_cues: Loop a band on the bar and put a foot or knee in it.; Pull until your chin passes the bar.; Lower slowly to a full hang.
common_mistakes: Bouncing off the band at the bottom; Half reps
safety: Check the band for nicks and step out carefully.
notes: Use thinner bands as you get stronger.

name: Bar muscle-up
form_cues: Pull explosively, aiming the bar to your lower chest.; Lean over the bar and turn the wrists quickly.; Press out to a straight-arm support on top.
common_mistakes: Chicken-winging one arm over; Using a false grip on a bar (not needed)
safety: Needs a high, solid bar with clearance above it.

name: Chest-to-bar pull-up
form_cues: Start from a full hang.; Pull explosively until your chest touches the bar.; Lower with control.
common_mistakes: Stopping at chin height; Over-arching the lower back
safety: Build up from strict pull-ups first.
notes: Key strength step toward the muscle-up.

name: Chin-ups
form_cues: Grip the bar palms facing you, shoulder-width.; Pull your chest toward the bar, elbows down and in.; Lower slowly to straight arms.
common_mistakes: Shrugging at the top; Half reps
safety: Ease off if your elbows or wrists get sore.
notes: Usually easier than pull-ups because the biceps help more.

name: Commando pull-up
form_cues: Stand under the bar and grip it with hands close, one in front of the other.; Pull up, moving your head to one side of the bar.; Lower and alternate sides each rep.
common_mistakes: Swinging the hips; Hitting the head on the bar
safety: Move your head clear of the bar on every rep.

name: Dead hang
form_cues: Grip the bar shoulder-width and hang with straight arms.; Relax your shoulders while keeping a firm grip.; Breathe steadily and let your spine lengthen.
common_mistakes: Swinging; Holding your breath
safety: Step down instead of dropping; skip if you have a shoulder dislocation history.
notes: Builds grip and decompresses the spine.

name: Flexed-arm hang
form_cues: Jump or step up so your chin is over the bar.; Hold, keeping shoulders down and chest up.; Lower slowly when you can't hold any longer.
common_mistakes: Chin resting on the bar; Shoulders creeping up
safety: Use a sturdy box to get into position.

name: Front lever
form_cues: Hang and raise your straight body until horizontal, face up.; Keep legs together and glutes squeezed.; Pull the bar toward your hips with straight arms.
common_mistakes: Hips sagging; Bent arms
safety: Very demanding on elbows and shoulders; warm up well.

name: Kipping pull-up
form_cues: Swing between an arch and a hollow position under the bar.; Drive hips up at the end of the hollow and pull.; Push away from the bar to re-enter the swing.
common_mistakes: Kipping before you can do strict pull-ups; Loose shoulders at the bottom
safety: Only kip once you have 5+ strict pull-ups; it is hard on the shoulders.
notes: Common in CrossFit for high-rep sets.

name: L-sit pull-up
form_cues: Hang and lift your legs straight out level with the floor.; Pull up while keeping the L shape.; Lower slowly without dropping the legs.
common_mistakes: Legs dropping during the pull; Bent knees
safety: Tuck the knees if the full L is too hard.

name: Negative pull-up
form_cues: Step up so your chin is above the bar.; Lower yourself as slowly as possible, 3–5 seconds.; Reach a full hang, then step back up.
common_mistakes: Dropping fast at the bottom; Kicking the legs
safety: Use a stable box to step up; expect soreness at first.

name: Neutral-grip pull-up
form_cues: Grip the parallel handles, palms facing each other.; Pull your chest up between the handles.; Lower to a full hang.
common_mistakes: Swinging; Neck craning to reach the bar
safety: Often the most shoulder-friendly grip.

name: One-arm chin-up
form_cues: Grip the bar with one hand, other arm by your side.; Brace your body and pull until your chin clears the bar.; Lower slowly to a full hang.
common_mistakes: Spinning around the bar; Jerking up from a swing
safety: Train elbows with lots of submaximal volume first; high tendon stress.
notes: Assist with a towel held lower by the free hand.

name: Pull-ups
secondary_muscles: Biceps; Rear delts; Rhomboids; Forearms; Core
form_cues: Hang with an overhand grip just wider than shoulders.; Pull elbows down toward your ribs until your chin clears the bar.; Lower to a full hang with control.
common_mistakes: Kipping or swinging; Not reaching a full hang
safety: Avoid if you have a shoulder injury flaring up.
notes: Add weight with a dip belt or vest once you can do 12+.

name: Scapular pull-up
form_cues: Hang with straight arms.; Pull shoulder blades down and back to lift yourself slightly.; Lower back to a full hang with control.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows; Swinging
safety: Keep arms straight the whole time.
notes: Teaches the first part of every pull-up.

name: Straddle front lever
form_cues: Hang and lift your body level with legs straight and wide.; Keep hips in line with your shoulders.; Press down hard through straight arms.
common_mistakes: Pike at the hips; Bent elbows
safety: Elite skill; build up over months.

name: Towel pull-up
form_cues: Drape two strong towels over the bar.; Grip a towel in each hand and hang.; Pull up as high as you can, then lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Loose towels sliding; Swinging
safety: Use thick, strong towels and check they won't slip off.
notes: Brutal grip builder for climbers and grapplers.

name: Tuck back lever
form_cues: Enter through skin the cat with knees tucked.; Stop when your back is level, face down.; Keep arms straight and squeeze the chest down.
common_mistakes: Bent arms; Hips too high or low
safety: Avoid if you have biceps tendon pain; straight-arm stress is high.

name: Tuck front lever
form_cues: Hang with straight arms and pull knees to your chest.; Press the bar down to lift hips to shoulder height.; Hold with your back horizontal.
common_mistakes: Bending the arms; Hips below shoulders
safety: Warm up shoulders and elbows; stop if elbows hurt.

name: Typewriter pull-up
form_cues: Pull up with a wide grip until the chin clears the bar.; Slide across to one hand, then the other, staying high.; Return to centre and lower.
common_mistakes: Dropping down while moving across; Kicking the legs
safety: Make sure your bar is solidly fixed; side-to-side force is high.

name: Wide-grip pull-up
form_cues: Grip the bar about one and a half shoulder-widths apart.; Pull your chest up toward the bar, elbows out and down.; Lower to straight arms.
common_mistakes: Going so wide that range is tiny; Kipping
safety: Don't go wider than is comfortable for your shoulders.

name: German hang
form_cues: From a skin the cat, lower into the back position.; Let shoulders open gently with straight arms.; Keep breathing and come out slowly.
common_mistakes: Dropping in fast; Holding too long at first
safety: Start with a few seconds; it heavily stretches the shoulder capsule.
notes: Prepares the shoulders for back lever.

name: Human flag
form_cues: Grip a vertical pole with hands wide, top arm pulling, bottom arm pushing.; Lock both arms and lift your body sideways.; Hold your legs level with the floor.
common_mistakes: Bending the bottom arm; Hips sagging
safety: Use a fixed pole that cannot rotate; warm up shoulders well.
notes: No exact gear id for a vertical pole; pullupbar used as nearest.

name: Korean dip
form_cues: Stand with the bar behind you, gripping it overhand.; Jump to a support and lower as your hands go behind the body.; Push back up to the top.
common_mistakes: Rushing into the deep stretch; Letting shoulders roll forward
safety: Needs good shoulder mobility; progress very gradually.

name: Skin the cat
form_cues: Hang and tuck your knees up through your arms.; Rotate backwards until feet point to the floor (German hang).; Return slowly the same way.
common_mistakes: Dropping into the bottom position; Bent arms twisted on a bar
safety: Go only as deep as your shoulders allow; easier on rings than a bar.

name: Dip support hold
form_cues: Jump up to support on the bars with straight arms.; Push shoulders down away from your ears.; Keep the body still and legs together.
common_mistakes: Shrugging; Bent elbows
safety: Start with short holds if your wrists are new to it.
aliases: Parallel bar support; Top dip hold

name: Triceps dip
form_cues: Support on the bars with your body upright.; Lower with elbows pointing straight back.; Press up until arms are locked.
common_mistakes: Leaning forward (turns it into a chest dip); Partial reps
safety: Stop at 90° elbow bend if your shoulders are sensitive.

name: Ring dip
form_cues: Start in a stable ring support.; Lower until shoulders are below elbows, rings close to the body.; Press back up and turn rings out at the top.
common_mistakes: Rings flaring wide; Too deep too soon
safety: Master ring support holds first; instability is high.

name: Ring fly
form_cues: Lean on the rings with arms nearly straight.; Open arms wide as you lower your chest.; Squeeze the rings back together.
common_mistakes: Bending the arms into a push-up; Going wider than you can control
safety: Start with rings higher and a steep body angle.

name: Ring push-ups
form_cues: Set rings a few centimetres off the floor and grip them.; Lower with rings close to your sides.; Press up and turn rings out slightly at the top.
common_mistakes: Rings drifting apart; Sagging hips
safety: Start with rings higher to reduce the instability.

name: Archer row
form_cues: Grip wide under a low bar.; Row toward one hand while the other arm stays straight.; Lower and switch sides.
common_mistakes: Rotating the hips; Bending the straight arm
progressions: One-arm inverted row; Front lever row
safety: Secure the bar before loading one side.

name: Inverted row
form_cues: Hang under a bar at waist height, body straight.; Pull your chest to the bar, squeezing shoulder blades.; Lower to straight arms with control.
common_mistakes: Hips sagging; Shrugging shoulders
safety: Make sure the bar is locked into the rack safety pins or Smith hooks.
notes: Lower the bar or raise the feet to make it harder.

name: Iron cross
form_cues: Start from ring support and spread arms out to the sides.; Keep arms straight and press rings down.; Hold the T shape with body upright.
common_mistakes: Bending elbows; Dropping below horizontal
safety: Elite gymnastics skill; high tendon load, train with bands and spotting.

name: Ring muscle-up
form_cues: Hang using a false grip.; Pull rings to the chest and lean the shoulders forward over them.; Transition into a dip and press to support.
common_mistakes: Losing the false grip; Pulling too far away from the rings
safety: Build strong ring dips and false-grip pull-ups first.

name: Ring support hold
form_cues: Jump up to support on the rings with straight arms.; Keep rings close to your hips.; Turn the rings out so palms face forward if you can.
common_mistakes: Rings swaying out; Shrugging
safety: Use a box to get in and out.

name: Ring triceps extension
form_cues: Lean forward holding the rings at forehead height.; Bend only the elbows to bring hands beside your head.; Straighten the arms to push back up.
common_mistakes: Moving at the shoulders; Hips sagging
safety: Steeper body angle = harder; start nearly upright.

name: Superman hold
form_cues: Lie face down, arms stretched overhead.; Lift arms, chest and legs a few centimetres together.; Keep your neck long and look at the floor.
common_mistakes: Cranking the neck up; Lifting too high and pinching the lower back
safety: Keep the lift small; stop if you feel lower-back pain.

name: Bear plank hold
form_cues: On hands and knees, hands under shoulders, knees under hips; Lift knees about 3 cm off the floor; Keep your back flat like a table
common_mistakes: Hips rising high; Rounding or arching the back
progressions: Bear plank shoulder taps; Bear crawl
safety: Keep breathing; go to fists if wrists hurt.
aliases: Bear hold; Hover plank; Quadruped hover

name: Bicycle crunch
form_cues: Hands lightly behind the head, shoulders off the floor; Rotate one shoulder toward the opposite knee as the other leg extends; Slow down and pause on each twist
common_mistakes: Flapping elbows instead of rotating the ribs; Racing through reps; Lower back peeling up
safety: Keep the extended leg higher if your back arches.
aliases: Bicycle kick crunch; Bicycles; Elbow-to-knee crunch

name: Bird dog
form_cues: Hands under shoulders, knees under hips, back flat; Reach the opposite arm and leg out long; Pause for 2 seconds without the hips tilting, then switch
common_mistakes: Arching the back as the leg lifts; Hips rotating open
regressions: Bird dog arm or leg only
progressions: Bird dog elbow-to-knee crunch; Banded bird dog
safety: Keep it small and controlled if you have back pain.
aliases: Quadruped arm and leg raise; Pointer
notes: One of McGill's 'Big 3' back-health moves.

name: Body saw
form_cues: Forearm plank with feet on sliders or a towel; Push your body back so elbows go in front of your face; Pull back to the start without letting hips sag
common_mistakes: Lower back arching as you push back; Sliding too far too soon
progressions: Ab wheel rollout; Stability ball rollout
safety: Only go as far as you can keep the ribs down.
aliases: Plank body saw; Slider body saw
notes: A towel on a hard floor or socks on wood work as sliders.

name: Butterfly sit-up
form_cues: Soles of feet together, knees out wide; Reach arms overhead and swing up to touch your feet; Roll back down and touch the floor behind you
common_mistakes: Using only arm swing; Slamming back onto the floor
safety: Use a rolled towel under the lower back if it feels uncomfortable.
notes: Common in CrossFit; the knees-out position limits hip flexor pull.

name: Copenhagen plank
form_cues: Top leg rests on a bench or chair, bottom leg hangs free; Lift hips into a straight side plank line; Squeeze the top leg down into the bench the whole time
common_mistakes: Hips sagging; Too much leg on the bench too soon
regressions: Short-lever Copenhagen (knee on bench); Side plank
safety: Start with the knee on the bench to protect the groin; stop with sharp adductor pain.
aliases: Copenhagen side plank; Copenhagen adductor plank
notes: Great for groin injury prevention in field sports. A chair works if you have no bench.

name: Cross-body mountain climber
form_cues: Start in a strong high plank; Drive each knee toward the opposite elbow; Keep the hips low and shoulders still
common_mistakes: Hips piking up; Rushing and losing the twist
safety: Keep the pace controlled if your back sags.
aliases: Cross-body climbers; Twisting mountain climbers; Oblique mountain climbers

name: Crunch
form_cues: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat; Curl your ribs toward your hips until shoulder blades lift; Lower slowly and keep a fist-sized gap under the chin
common_mistakes: Yanking on the neck; Swinging up with momentum; Lifting the whole back off the floor (that's a sit-up)
progressions: Weighted crunch; Stability ball crunch; Decline crunch
safety: Support the head lightly with fingertips; don't pull.
aliases: Basic crunch; Floor crunch; Abdominal crunch
notes: Hold a plate on the chest to add load.

name: Dead bug
form_cues: Lie on your back, arms to ceiling, knees at 90°; Lower the opposite arm and leg toward the floor; Keep the lower back flat and breathe out as you reach
common_mistakes: Lower back arching; Moving too fast
progressions: Weighted dead bug; Band dead bug; Hollow body hold
safety: A good choice for sensitive backs; shorten the range if the back lifts.
notes: Hold a dumbbell or press into a band to progress.

name: Flutter kicks
form_cues: Lie down, hands under hips, lower back pressed down; Lift legs a few centimetres off the floor; Kick small, quick up-and-down alternations
common_mistakes: Lower back arching; Kicks too big and sloppy
safety: Raise the legs higher if your back arches.
notes: Can also be tracked as time (30–45 sec).

name: Heel touches
form_cues: Lie with knees bent, feet a bit wider than hips; Lift shoulders and reach one hand to the same-side heel; Stay curled up as you tap side to side
common_mistakes: Dropping the head between reps; Pulling the chin into the chest
safety: Fine for most people; rest the head between sets if the neck tires.
aliases: Alternating heel touches; Heel taps; Side-to-side oblique reach

name: High plank
form_cues: Hands under shoulders, arms straight but not locked; Spread your fingers and push the floor away; Tuck pelvis slightly and keep a straight line
common_mistakes: Shoulders sinking toward the floor; Hips sagging
regressions: Kneeling high plank; Incline plank on a bench
safety: Go to fists or forearms if your wrists hurt.
aliases: Straight-arm plank; Push-up plank; Full plank

name: Hollow body hold
form_cues: Press your lower back into the floor; Lift shoulders and legs, arms reaching past your ears; Hold the banana shape and keep breathing
common_mistakes: Lower back lifting off the floor; Holding the breath
safety: Tuck the knees or bring arms forward if your back lifts.
aliases: Hollow hold; Hollow position; Dish hold
notes: A foundation for gymnastics and calisthenics skills.

name: Hollow body rock
form_cues: Get into a tight hollow hold; Rock from shoulders to hips without changing shape; Keep arms by the ears and legs together
common_mistakes: Bending at the hips to make the rock; Losing the low-back contact
safety: Only rock if you can hold the hollow position for 30 sec first.

name: Jackknife sit-up
form_cues: Lie flat, arms overhead; Raise one straight leg as you reach both hands to that foot; Lower back down and alternate legs
common_mistakes: Pulling with the neck; Bending the reaching leg a lot
safety: Keep the non-working leg on the floor for support.

name: Lying leg raise
form_cues: Lie flat, hands under hips or by your sides; Press the lower back into the floor and raise straight legs to vertical; Lower slowly until just before the back lifts
common_mistakes: Lower back arching off the floor; Dropping the legs fast
progressions: Bench leg raise; Hanging leg raise
safety: Bend the knees or shorten the range if your lower back lifts.
aliases: Leg raise; Floor leg raise; Straight-leg raise

name: Lying windshield wipers
form_cues: Lie on your back with arms out in a T, legs up at 90°; Lower your legs to one side while shoulders stay down; Pull them back to centre and go to the other side
common_mistakes: Shoulders lifting off the floor; Dropping the legs too fast
safety: Bend the knees to shorten the lever if your back aches.
aliases: Floor windshield wipers; Lying leg rotations

name: Mountain climbers
form_cues: Start in a high plank, hands under shoulders; Drive one knee toward your chest, then switch quickly; Keep the hips level and shoulders over the hands
common_mistakes: Hips bouncing high; Shoulders drifting behind the hands
regressions: Slow mountain climbers; Incline mountain climbers on a bench
progressions: Cross-body mountain climber; Suspension mountain climbers
safety: Slow down if your wrists or lower back complain.
notes: Track as time (30–45 sec) for conditioning work.

name: Oblique crunch
form_cues: Lie on your back with one ankle on the other knee; Curl and rotate the opposite shoulder toward the raised knee; Lower slowly and finish all reps before switching
common_mistakes: Pulling on the neck; Only moving the elbow
safety: Keep the movement small and controlled.

name: Plank
form_cues: Stack elbows under shoulders and push the floor away; Squeeze glutes and brace like you're about to be poked; Keep one straight line from head to heels
common_mistakes: Hips sagging toward the floor; Hips piked high to make it easier; Holding the breath
progressions: Plank shoulder taps; Body saw; Weighted plank
safety: Stop if you feel it in your lower back rather than your abs.
aliases: Forearm plank; Front plank; Elbow plank
notes: Quality beats time: end the set when your hips start to drop.

name: Plank shoulder taps
form_cues: Start in a high plank with feet a bit wider than hips; Tap the opposite shoulder with one hand at a time; Keep the hips still, like a glass of water is on your back
common_mistakes: Hips swaying side to side; Rushing the taps
safety: Widen your feet if you can't stop the hips rocking.
aliases: Shoulder tap plank; High plank shoulder taps

name: Plank up-down
form_cues: Start on forearms in a plank; Press up to hands one arm at a time, then lower back down; Alternate the leading arm and keep the hips level
common_mistakes: Hips rocking side to side; Hips piking up
safety: Widen the feet for stability; skip if you have wrist pain.
aliases: Up-down plank; Plank walk-ups; Commando plank

name: Reverse crunch
form_cues: Lie down, knees bent at 90°, hands by your sides; Curl your hips off the floor toward your ribs; Lower slowly without the feet crashing down
common_mistakes: Swinging the legs for momentum; Only moving the legs, not the pelvis
progressions: Bench leg raise; Hanging knee raise; Decline reverse crunch
safety: Keep it slow to protect the lower back.
aliases: Lying reverse crunch; Floor reverse crunch

name: Reverse plank
form_cues: Sit with legs long, hands behind hips, fingers toward feet; Drive hips up until your body is one straight line; Squeeze glutes and keep the chin neutral
common_mistakes: Hips sagging; Dropping the head back
safety: Do it on forearms if your wrists or shoulders object.

name: Russian twist
equipment: Optional plate, dumbbell or medicine ball
form_cues: Sit leaning back about 45° with a tall chest; Turn your shoulders, not just your arms, side to side; Lift the feet for a harder version
common_mistakes: Swinging the arms while the torso stays still; Rounding the back
safety: Skip with disc problems that dislike loaded twisting.
aliases: Seated twist; Medicine ball Russian twist; Weighted Russian twist
notes: Add a medicine ball, plate or dumbbell for load.

name: Scissor kicks
form_cues: Lie down, lower back pressed into the floor; Hold legs just off the floor; Cross one leg over the other, then switch, keeping legs straight
common_mistakes: Arching the back; Legs dropping onto the floor
safety: Keep the legs higher to make it easier on the back.

name: Seated knee tuck
form_cues: Sit leaning back on your hands, feet off the floor; Pull your knees toward your chest as your chest moves toward them; Extend the legs out long without touching the floor
common_mistakes: Rounding the shoulders forward; Letting the feet drop
safety: Lean back on forearms if you feel it in your lower back.
aliases: Seated in-and-outs; Knee tucks; Seated crunch
notes: Can also be done on a bench edge.

name: Side plank
form_cues: Elbow directly under shoulder, feet stacked or staggered; Lift hips so ankles, hips and shoulders line up; Push the floor away and don't let the top hip roll back
common_mistakes: Hips sagging down; Rolling forward or back; Shoulder shrugged up to the ear
progressions: Side plank hip dips; Side plank with rotation; Copenhagen plank
safety: Bend the bottom knee to shorten the lever if your shoulder complains.
notes: Stagger the feet for more stability; stack them for more challenge.

name: Side plank hip dips
form_cues: Start in a strong side plank on your forearm; Lower the hip a few centimetres toward the floor; Drive it back up past level and pause
common_mistakes: Rushing and bouncing the hip off the floor; Twisting the torso instead of moving sideways
progressions: Side plank with rotation; Copenhagen plank
safety: Keep the shoulder packed down; stop if it pinches.
aliases: Side plank dips; Oblique hip dips

name: Side plank with rotation
form_cues: Hold a tall side plank with the top arm reaching to the ceiling; Rotate and thread the top arm under your body; Return slowly without letting the hips drop
common_mistakes: Hips sinking as you rotate; Moving fast and losing control
progressions: Side plank with a light dumbbell reach-through
safety: Keep the supporting shoulder stacked over the elbow.
aliases: Side plank thread the needle; Side plank reach-through

name: Sit-up
form_cues: Knees bent, feet flat, arms crossed on chest; Curl up one vertebra at a time until you're upright; Lower with control rather than flopping back
common_mistakes: Jerking up with the arms or neck; Feet flying up
progressions: Butterfly sit-up; Decline sit-up; Weighted sit-up
safety: Skip or swap for crunches if sit-ups aggravate a disc problem.
aliases: Full sit-up; Floor sit-up; Bent-knee sit-up
notes: Anchor the feet under a sofa if needed.

name: Spiderman plank
form_cues: Start in a forearm or high plank; Bring one knee out to the same-side elbow; Return the leg with control and switch sides
common_mistakes: Hips hiking up to reach; Lower back sagging
safety: Move slowly; it is a strength drill, not cardio.

name: Stomach vacuum
form_cues: Breathe out fully through your mouth; Pull your belly button in toward your spine; Hold while taking small, shallow breaths
common_mistakes: Holding the breath until dizzy; Sucking in the chest instead of the belly
safety: Avoid if you are pregnant or have high blood pressure.
aliases: Abdominal vacuum; Ab vacuum; Drawing-in manoeuvre
notes: Popular in physique and rehab circles for deep-core awareness.

name: Toe touch crunch
form_cues: Lie down with legs pointing to the ceiling; Reach your hands toward your toes, lifting shoulder blades; Lower slowly and keep the legs still
common_mistakes: Throwing the arms instead of curling the trunk; Letting the legs drift down
safety: Bend the knees slightly if your hamstrings are tight.
aliases: Vertical toe touches; Toe reaches; Leg-up crunch

name: Tuck-up
form_cues: Lie flat with arms overhead; Sit up as you pull your knees to your chest; Hug the shins briefly, then lower with control
common_mistakes: Swinging with momentum; Crashing back down
safety: Keep the motion controlled to protect the lower back.
aliases: V-sit tuck; Crunchy frog; Seated knee tuck-up

name: V-up
form_cues: Lie flat with arms overhead and legs straight; Lift arms and legs together to meet over your hips; Lower slowly back to a hovering hollow position
common_mistakes: Bending the knees a lot; Flopping back down
safety: Build up through tuck-ups if your back arches.

name: Ab wheel rollout
form_cues: Kneel and hold the wheel under your shoulders; Roll forward with ribs down and glutes squeezed; Pull back with your abs, not by sitting the hips back
common_mistakes: Lower back sagging at the bottom; Going further than you can control
progressions: Standing ab wheel rollout; Barbell rollout
safety: Use a short range to start; stop if you feel your lower back.
aliases: Kneeling ab wheel rollout; Ab roller; Rollout
notes: Roll toward a wall to cap the range while learning.

name: Band Pallof press
form_cues: Anchor a band at chest height and stand side-on; Press the band straight out from your chest; Resist the twist, pause, then bring it back
common_mistakes: Letting the torso rotate; Standing too close (no tension)
progressions: Cable Pallof press; Half-kneeling Pallof press
safety: Check the anchor is secure before loading the band.
aliases: Resistance band Pallof press; Band anti-rotation press
notes: Kneeling or split stance versions shift the challenge.

name: Band woodchop
form_cues: Anchor the band high and stand side-on; Pull diagonally across your body to the opposite hip; Pivot the back foot and rotate through the trunk
common_mistakes: Pulling only with the arms; Rounding the back
safety: Use a band you can control on the way back.

name: BOSU crunch
form_cues: Sit with the dome under your lower back; Lean back into the stretch, then curl up; Lower slowly and keep feet planted
common_mistakes: Yanking the neck; Bouncing off the dome
safety: Keep feet wide to stay stable.
aliases: Crunch on BOSU; BOSU ball sit-up

name: BOSU plank
form_cues: Forearms on the dome, legs straight behind you; Brace and squeeze glutes to hold a straight line; Keep the platform still and breathe
common_mistakes: Hips sagging; Shoulders shrugged
progressions: BOSU plank with feet on dome; Stability ball plank
safety: Hold the edges if forearms slip.
aliases: Plank on BOSU; Forearm BOSU plank

name: Dumbbell side bend
form_cues: Stand tall with one dumbbell at your side; Bend sideways toward the weight, keeping hips still; Pull back up with the opposite obliques
common_mistakes: Twisting or leaning forward; Holding weights in both hands (they cancel out)
safety: Move slowly; avoid with lower back pain on side bending.
aliases: Side bend; Standing oblique bend; Weighted side bend

name: Hanging knee raise
form_cues: Hang from the bar with shoulders engaged; Bring knees up toward the chest, curling the hips; Lower under control and stop the swing
common_mistakes: Kipping and swinging; Dropping the legs fast
regressions: Captain's chair knee raise; Reverse crunch
safety: Use ab straps if your grip fails before your abs.

name: Hanging leg raise
form_cues: Hang with active shoulders and legs together; Raise straight legs to hip height or higher by curling the pelvis; Lower slowly without swinging
common_mistakes: Swinging for momentum; Only lifting with hip flexors, no pelvic curl
regressions: Hanging knee raise; Captain's chair knee raise
safety: Use ab straps if grip or shoulders give out first.
aliases: Straight-leg hanging raise; Hanging straight leg raise

name: Hanging windshield wipers
form_cues: Hang and raise straight legs up to the bar; Rotate the legs side to side like a wiper; Keep the upper body still and controlled
common_mistakes: Bending the knees; Swinging the whole body
regressions: Lying windshield wipers; Hanging leg raise
safety: Only attempt once strict toes-to-bar feel easy.

name: Medicine ball woodchop
form_cues: Hold the ball high over one shoulder; Chop down diagonally to the outside of the opposite knee; Squat a little and pivot the back foot as you rotate
common_mistakes: Arms-only movement; Releasing the ball (this is not a throw)
safety: Keep the back long as you squat down.
aliases: Med ball chop; Medicine ball wood chop
notes: A dumbbell held by the ends works too.

name: Plank pull-through
form_cues: High plank with a weight beside your ribs; Reach under with the opposite hand and drag it across; Keep the hips square and still
common_mistakes: Hips twisting; Feet too close together
safety: Use a light weight first; widen the feet for stability.

name: Stability ball crunch
form_cues: Sit then walk out until the ball is under your mid-back; Let the back stretch over the ball, then curl up; Lower slowly back into the stretch
common_mistakes: Rolling the ball rather than curling; Pulling the neck
progressions: Weighted stability ball crunch; Cable rope crunch
safety: Keep feet wide for stability.
aliases: Swiss ball crunch; Exercise ball crunch
notes: The ball allows a bigger range than a floor crunch.

name: Stability ball knee tuck
form_cues: Start in a push-up position with shins on the ball; Pull your knees toward your chest, rolling the ball in; Push it back to a straight plank without sagging
common_mistakes: Hips dropping at the start; Shoulders drifting behind hands
progressions: Stability ball pike; Suspension knee tuck
safety: Keep the ball close to start; further out is harder.
aliases: Swiss ball jackknife; Ball knee tuck; Stability ball jackknife

name: Stability ball pass
form_cues: Lie flat holding the ball overhead; Lift arms and legs to pass the ball to your feet; Lower both, then bring it back to your hands
common_mistakes: Lower back arching when lowering; Dropping the ball
safety: Don't lower your legs further than you can keep the back flat.
aliases: Swiss ball V-up pass; Ball pass; Ball exchange

name: Stability ball pike
form_cues: Start in a push-up position with shins on the ball; Lift your hips high, rolling the ball to your toes; Lower with control back to a flat plank
common_mistakes: Bending the knees; Sagging hips at the bottom
safety: Keep shoulders over hands; strong wrists required.

name: Stability ball plank
form_cues: Place forearms on the ball, legs straight behind; Brace hard so the ball doesn't wobble; Keep a straight line from head to heels
common_mistakes: Hips sagging; Ball rolling side to side
safety: Put the ball against a wall the first few times.
aliases: Swiss ball plank; Forearm plank on ball

name: Stability ball rollout
form_cues: Kneel with forearms on the ball; Roll it forward as your body straightens; Pull it back with your abs, keeping ribs down
common_mistakes: Lower back sagging; Hips staying back
progressions: Stir the pot; Ab wheel rollout
safety: Stop the roll before your back starts to arch.

name: Standing ab wheel rollout
form_cues: From standing, fold and place the wheel on the floor; Roll out to full extension with a hollow body; Pull back up to a pike without the back arching
common_mistakes: Lower back collapsing; Bending the knees to cheat back up
safety: Master 15+ kneeling rollouts first; very demanding on the lower back.
aliases: Standing rollout; Full ab wheel rollout

name: Stir the pot
form_cues: Hold a forearm plank on the ball; Draw small circles with your elbows; Keep the hips and lower back totally still
common_mistakes: Hips swaying with the ball; Circles too big
progressions: Stir the pot with feet together
safety: Keep circles small; stop if the lower back sags.
aliases: Stability ball stir the pot; Ball circles plank
notes: Popularised by Dr. Stuart McGill for spine-friendly core work.

name: Toes-to-bar
form_cues: Hang with a shoulder-width grip and press the bar down; Lift straight legs until your toes touch the bar; Lower with control between reps (or kip if training CrossFit style)
common_mistakes: Bending the knees a lot; Uncontrolled swing
regressions: Hanging leg raise; Hanging knee raise
safety: Warm up the shoulders and hamstrings first.
notes: Strict and kipping versions exist; kipping is for conditioning.

name: Waiter's carry
form_cues: Press a weight overhead and lock the arm by your ear; Brace and walk tall with ribs down; Keep the bicep near the ear the whole walk
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back; Arm drifting forward
safety: Only go overhead if your shoulder has pain-free mobility.

name: Barbell rollout
form_cues: Load small round plates and kneel behind the bar; Roll forward with ribs down and glutes tight; Pull back with your abs
common_mistakes: Arching the back; Hips staying behind
safety: Use plates with round edges so the bar rolls smoothly.
aliases: Barbell ab rollout; Kneeling barbell rollout
notes: Wider grip than an ab wheel; good gym substitute.

name: Bench leg raise
form_cues: Lie on a bench gripping it behind your head; Raise your legs and curl the hips off the bench; Lower slowly past bench level without arching
common_mistakes: Swinging the legs; Lower back lifting
safety: Bend the knees if your lower back arches.
aliases: Flat bench leg raise; Bench lying leg raise

name: Cable rope crunch
form_cues: Kneel facing the stack, rope beside your head; Curl your ribs toward your hips, rounding the spine; Keep the hips still and return slowly
common_mistakes: Sitting back with the hips instead of crunching; Pulling with the arms
safety: Keep the weight moderate so you can feel the abs, not the hips.
aliases: Kneeling cable crunch; Cable crunch; Rope crunch
notes: One of the best ways to load the abs progressively.

name: Cable woodchop
form_cues: Set the pulley high and stand side-on; Pull diagonally down across your body to the opposite hip; Rotate through the torso and pivot the back foot
common_mistakes: Arms doing all the work; Rounding the lower back
safety: Use a load you can control on the way back up.

name: Decline crunch
form_cues: Secure your feet and lie back on the decline bench; Curl your shoulders up without sitting all the way; Lower with control, keeping tension
common_mistakes: Pulling the head forward; Using momentum
safety: Start at a shallow angle.

name: Decline sit-up
form_cues: Hook feet under the pads, arms crossed on chest; Curl up until your torso is near vertical; Lower slowly to just above the bench
common_mistakes: Yanking up with the neck; Dropping back fast
safety: Lower the bench angle to make it easier.
aliases: Decline bench sit-up; Weighted decline sit-up
notes: Hold a plate on your chest to add load.

name: Dragon flag
form_cues: Lie on a bench and grip it behind your head; Lift your body to vertical, resting on the upper back; Lower as one straight line, then raise back up
common_mistakes: Bending at the hips; Lower back arching on the way down
regressions: Tuck dragon flag; Dragon flag negatives; Bench leg raise
safety: Very demanding; build up with negatives and stop if your neck takes the load.

name: Landmine rotation
form_cues: Hold the bar end at arm's length above your head; Rotate it down in an arc to one hip, pivoting the feet; Bring it back over the top and go to the other side
common_mistakes: Bending the arms; Twisting from the lower back with locked hips
safety: Start with the empty bar; use a corner if you have no landmine.

name: Low-to-high cable woodchop
form_cues: Set the pulley low and stand side-on; Pull up diagonally across your body to above the opposite shoulder; Drive from the hips and keep arms long
common_mistakes: Lifting with the arms only; Leaning back
safety: Keep the spine long; don't round to grab the handle.
aliases: Reverse woodchop; Cable lift; Low-to-high chop

name: Pallof press
form_cues: Stand side-on with the handle at chest; Press it straight out and resist the pull; Hold 2 seconds, then bring it back slowly
common_mistakes: Torso twisting toward the stack; Feet too narrow
progressions: Half-kneeling Pallof press; Pallof press with overhead reach
safety: Start light; it's harder than it looks.
aliases: Cable Pallof press; Cable anti-rotation press

name: Standing cable rotation
form_cues: Set the pulley at chest height, stand side-on; Rotate away from the stack with arms straight; Return slowly without letting it yank you back
common_mistakes: Bending the arms; Hips locked so the lower back twists
safety: Let the hips turn a little to spare the lower back.
aliases: Horizontal cable woodchop; Cable trunk rotation; Cable twist

name: Suspension fallout
form_cues: Hold handles facing away from the anchor, body leaning forward; Let arms rise overhead as you fall forward; Pull back up with your abs, not the arms
common_mistakes: Lower back arching; Bending the elbows
safety: A steeper body angle is harder; start more upright.
aliases: TRX fallout; TRX rollout; Suspension body saw

name: Suspension knee tuck
form_cues: Feet in the straps, high plank position; Pull knees in toward your chest; Extend back to a straight plank
common_mistakes: Hips sagging; Shoulders drifting back
safety: Keep the straps at mid-calf height.
aliases: TRX knee tuck; Suspension crunch; TRX crunch

name: Suspension pike
form_cues: Feet in the straps, start in a high plank; Lift hips high keeping legs straight; Lower slowly back to a flat plank
common_mistakes: Bending the knees; Sagging hips at the bottom
safety: Keep shoulders stacked over hands.

name: 45-degree side bend
form_cues: Lie sideways on the bench, hip on the pad, feet locked; Lower your torso sideways toward the floor; Raise back up past level using the top-side obliques
common_mistakes: Rotating forward or back; Bouncing at the bottom
safety: Use a short range first; stop with sharp back pain.
aliases: Roman chair side bend; Hyperextension side bend; Lateral back extension

name: Ab crunch machine
form_cues: Set the seat so the pads sit on your chest or shoulders; Curl down by bringing ribs to hips; Return slowly without letting the stack slam
common_mistakes: Pulling with the arms; Using too much weight and hip-flexing
safety: Start light and keep the motion in the abs.

name: Captain's chair knee raise
form_cues: Back against the pad, forearms on the rests; Lift knees to chest by curling the hips up; Lower with control without swinging
common_mistakes: Swinging the legs; Only lifting to 90° without curling the pelvis
progressions: Hanging knee raise; Hanging leg raise
safety: Keep shoulders down, not shrugged.
aliases: Vertical knee raise; Roman chair knee raise; Captain's chair leg raise
notes: Straighten the legs for a harder leg raise version.

name: GHD sit-up
form_cues: Sit on the pad with feet locked, hips just past it; Lower back to parallel, then reach behind if trained; Kick the knees straight to sit up and reach for your feet
common_mistakes: Going too far back too soon; Doing high volume on the first try
safety: Start with low reps and a short range; overuse can cause rhabdo or back strain.

name: Rotary torso machine
form_cues: Sit tall with legs locked in; Rotate through your trunk, not your arms; Return slowly to centre
common_mistakes: Jerking the weight; Too much range
safety: Use a moderate load; avoid with disc issues aggravated by twisting.
aliases: Seated torso rotation; Torso twist machine; Oblique machine

name: Heel-to-toe walk
form_cues: Walk in a straight line, heel touching the toes of the back foot; Keep your eyes forward, not on your feet; Move slowly and steadily
common_mistakes: Rushing the steps; Arms flailing for balance
progressions: Heel-to-toe walk backwards; Heel-to-toe walk, eyes closed
safety: Walk beside a wall or counter until confident.
aliases: Tandem walk; Tightrope walk; Line walk

name: Single-leg stand
form_cues: Stand tall and lift one foot just off the floor; Spread your toes and keep a slight bend in the standing knee; Fix your eyes on a point ahead
common_mistakes: Locking the standing knee; Hip dropping on the lifted side
regressions: Tandem stance hold; Fingertip support on a wall
progressions: Single-leg stand, eyes closed; BOSU single-leg balance
safety: Stand near a wall or counter in case you lose balance.
aliases: Single-leg balance; Stork stand; One-leg stand
notes: Great for ankle sprain rehab and fall prevention.

name: Single-leg stand, eyes closed
form_cues: Get steady on one leg with eyes open first; Close your eyes and keep the standing knee soft; Let the ankle make small corrections
common_mistakes: Locking the knee; Grabbing for support too early
safety: Always do this next to a wall or sturdy support.
aliases: Eyes-closed single-leg balance; Blind stork stand
notes: Removing vision makes the ankle and inner ear work harder.

name: Single-leg toe touch
form_cues: Stand on one leg with a soft knee; Hinge forward and reach your hand toward the floor; Squeeze the glute to stand back up tall
common_mistakes: Rounding the back to reach; Standing knee caving in
safety: Reach to a box or chair if the floor is too far.
aliases: Single-leg reach to floor; Single-leg balance reach; Single-leg touchdown

name: Star excursion balance
form_cues: Balance on one leg in a quarter squat; Reach the free toe as far as you can along each direction like a clock; Tap lightly, return to the centre and keep the standing heel down
common_mistakes: Putting weight on the reaching foot; Standing knee caving inward
progressions: Y-balance reach; Star excursion on a BOSU
safety: Keep reaches within a range you can control.
aliases: Star excursion; Single-leg clock reach; Single-leg reach
notes: Used by physios to test and train ankle and knee stability.

name: Tandem stance hold
form_cues: Place one heel directly in front of the other foot's toes; Stand tall with arms relaxed; Hold, then switch which foot is in front
common_mistakes: Looking down at the feet; Leaning to one side
safety: Stand in a corner or by a counter for safety.
aliases: Heel-to-toe stance; Tightrope stance; Romberg tandem stance
notes: Common in falls-prevention programmes for older adults.

name: Y-balance reach
form_cues: Stand on one leg at the centre of a Y; Reach the free foot forward, then back-left, then back-right; Touch lightly and return without losing balance
common_mistakes: Leaning heavily on the reaching foot; Standing heel lifting
safety: Mark the lines with tape; stay near support if needed.
aliases: Y-balance; Y-balance test drill; Three-way single-leg reach
notes: Compare reach distances side to side to spot imbalances.

name: Single-leg airplane
form_cues: Hinge forward on one leg until your torso is near horizontal; Rotate your pelvis open toward the ceiling; Rotate back down so hips face the floor, staying balanced
common_mistakes: Rotating the shoulders instead of the hips; Losing the hinge and standing up
safety: Hold a wall or rack with one hand until you've mastered it.
aliases: Hip airplane; Airplane balance; Standing airplane
notes: Builds hip control for running and lifting.

name: BOSU single-leg balance
form_cues: Step onto the centre of the dome with one foot; Keep a soft knee and lift the other foot; Look ahead and let the ankle make small corrections
common_mistakes: Locking the knee; Knee caving inward
progressions: BOSU single-leg balance, eyes closed; Star excursion on a BOSU
safety: Start next to a wall or rack for support.
aliases: Single-leg stand on BOSU; BOSU stork stand
notes: A foam balance pad is a good alternative.

name: BOSU squat
form_cues: Stand on the dome with feet hip-width; Sit back into a squat with knees tracking over toes; Stand back up without wobbling
common_mistakes: Knees caving in; Going too deep and losing balance
progressions: BOSU squat on the flat side (dome down)
safety: Use the dome side up; standing on the flat side is advanced.

name: Stability ball kneeling balance
form_cues: Start with hands and knees on the ball beside a wall; Lift your hands off and kneel upright; Keep hips forward and eyes on a fixed point
common_mistakes: Sitting back on the heels; Tensing up and over-correcting
safety: Clear the area and use a wall or partner nearby; falls are possible.
aliases: Kneeling on Swiss ball; Ball kneel

name: Stability ball seated balance
form_cues: Sit tall on the ball, feet hip-width, knees at 90°; Lift one foot slightly off the floor and hold; Switch feet without wobbling; progress to marching
common_mistakes: Slouching; Feet too close together
safety: Use a ball sized so your hips are level with your knees.
aliases: Swiss ball seated march; Seated ball balance

name: Acceleration sprint
form_cues: Start from a split stance, leaning forward.; Push the ground back hard with powerful, full strides.; Rise gradually to upright over the first 10–15 m.
common_mistakes: Popping upright immediately; Short choppy steps; Starting cold without a warm-up
progressions: Hill sprint; Sled sprint; Broad jump into sprint
safety: Warm up thoroughly; rest 1–2 min between reps to stay fast.
aliases: 10 m sprint; 20 m sprint; Short sprint
notes: Track times if you can; stop when speed drops.

name: Backpedal to sprint
form_cues: Backpedal low with weight on the balls of your feet.; On the cue or line, open the hips and turn.; Accelerate forward hard for 10 m.
common_mistakes: Standing tall while backpedalling; Slow, rounded turn
safety: Use a clear, flat area; start slowly.

name: Broad jump into sprint
form_cues: Do one maximal broad jump.; Land in an athletic stance with a forward lean.; Immediately sprint out 10 m, pushing hard on the first steps.
common_mistakes: Stalling or standing up after the landing; Landing off balance
safety: Land softly with knees soft and tracking over toes; skip if you have acute knee or ankle pain.
aliases: Broad jump to sprint; Jump and sprint
notes: Links jumping power to acceleration.

name: Falling start sprint
form_cues: Stand tall and lean forward from the ankles as one straight line.; When you feel you will fall, explode into a sprint.; Keep the lean for the first few strong steps.
common_mistakes: Bending at the waist; Stepping out too far in front of the body
safety: Warm up first; use a surface with good grip.
aliases: Lean and go; Falling sprint start

name: Flying sprint
form_cues: Build up over 20–30 m to near top speed.; Sprint the marked zone at full speed, running tall.; Stay relaxed in face and shoulders; strike under your hips.
common_mistakes: Tensing up and over-striding; Too short a build-up zone
safety: Only do these fresh and fully warmed up; hamstring strains happen at top speed.
notes: Trains maximum velocity; rest 3+ min between reps.

name: Medicine ball chest pass
form_cues: Stand in an athletic stance, ball at your chest.; Step and throw the ball hard and straight at the wall.; Catch on the rebound and go again with control.
common_mistakes: Pushing slowly instead of throwing; Throwing with only the arms and no leg drive
progressions: Medicine ball supine chest throw; Rotational medicine ball throw
safety: Use a ball that bounces (not a slam ball) for wall throws; keep your face clear on the rebound.
aliases: Med ball chest throw; Chest pass
notes: 3–5 kg suits most people.

name: Devil press
form_cues: Do a burpee with your hands on the dumbbells.; Jump the feet in and swing both weights back between your legs.; Snap the hips to swing them straight overhead in one motion.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back on the swing; Pressing with the arms
safety: Start light; the swing should come from the hips, not the lower back.

name: Dumbbell clean and press
form_cues: Hang-clean the dumbbells to your shoulders.; Re-set your feet and brace.; Press or push-press overhead, then lower to the thighs.
common_mistakes: Rushing the press before you're stable; Arching the back overhead
regressions: Dumbbell hang clean; Standing dumbbell shoulder press
safety: Lower the weights in two steps to protect your back.
aliases: DB clean and jerk; Dumbbell clean to press

name: Dumbbell high pull
form_cues: Hold dumbbells in front of your thighs, hinge slightly.; Drive your hips forward explosively.; Let the pop carry the weights up, elbows high and out.
common_mistakes: Pulling with the arms only; Rounding the back
safety: Keep the weights close to your body and your back flat.

name: Dumbbell push press
form_cues: Hold dumbbells at your shoulders, feet hip-width.; Dip a few inches at the knees, then drive up hard.; Use the leg drive to press overhead; lower with control.
common_mistakes: Dipping too deep like a squat; Pressing before the legs finish
safety: Keep the dip short and the knees tracking over your toes.
notes: Lets you handle more weight overhead than a strict press.

name: Man maker
form_cues: Push-up on the dumbbells, then row each side once.; Jump the feet in and clean the weights to your shoulders.; Squat and press overhead (thruster); that's one rep.
common_mistakes: Sagging hips in the plank; Rushing the clean with a round back
safety: Use hex dumbbells and a modest weight; form fades fast as you tire.

name: 5-10-5 pro agility drill
form_cues: Start straddling the middle line in a low stance.; Sprint 5 m one way, touch, then 10 m the other way.; Touch and sprint 5 m back through the middle.
common_mistakes: Standing up during the turns; Crossing the feet on the first step
safety: Use a grippy surface; rest fully between timed reps.
notes: Standard combine test (5-10-5 yards); metres work fine.

name: Band-resisted sprint
equipment: Long resistance band or harness; Partner or anchor
form_cues: Loop the band round your waist with a partner holding behind.; Lean forward and drive hard with powerful steps.; Keep strong arm drive and a straight body line.
common_mistakes: Bending at the waist; Partner pulling so hard your form breaks
safety: Check the band for wear and anchor it securely.
notes: Can also be done in place against an anchored band.

name: Box drill
form_cues: Set four cones in a 5 m square.; Sprint forward, shuffle sideways, backpedal, then shuffle back.; Stay low and keep your hips facing forward.
common_mistakes: Crossing the feet in the shuffle; Rising up at each cone
safety: Use a non-slip surface.
notes: Trains changes between forward, lateral and backward movement.

name: Dumbbell cluster
form_cues: Clean the dumbbells from the floor into a front squat.; Drive straight up out of the squat.; Use the momentum to press overhead in one motion.
common_mistakes: Pausing at the bottom; Pulling with a round back
safety: Very demanding; scale weight and reps to keep form crisp.
notes: A CrossFit staple: a squat clean flowing into a thruster.

name: Dumbbell hang clean
form_cues: Hold dumbbells at mid-thigh with a flat back.; Jump the hips forward and shrug the weights up.; Drop under and catch them on your shoulders, knees soft.
common_mistakes: Reverse-curling the weights; Catching with locked knees
progressions: Dumbbell squat clean; Dumbbell clean and press
safety: Keep the dumbbells close to your body on the way up.

name: Dumbbell jump squat
form_cues: Hold light dumbbells at your sides or a kettlebell at your chest.; Dip to a quarter squat and jump as high as you can.; Land softly and reset before the next rep.
common_mistakes: Going too heavy so jumps barely leave the floor; Landing stiff-legged
safety: Keep the load light (10–30% of body weight); land softly with knees soft and tracking over toes; skip if you have acute knee or ankle pain.
aliases: Weighted jump squat; Kettlebell jump squat; Loaded squat jump

name: Dumbbell split jump
form_cues: Hold light dumbbells at your sides in a lunge stance.; Jump up, switching legs in the air.; Land softly in a lunge with the front knee over the foot.
common_mistakes: Using weights that are too heavy; Back knee hitting the floor
safety: Keep loads light and stop when landings get sloppy.
aliases: Weighted jumping lunge; Loaded split jump

name: Dumbbell squat clean
