form_cues: Start with dumbbells on the floor beside your feet.; Pull explosively and drop into a front squat to catch them.; Stand up tall with the weights on your shoulders.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back off the floor; Catching too high and stiff
safety: Brace before every pull and keep a flat back.

name: Dumbbell sumo deadlift high pull
form_cues: Stand wide holding one dumbbell by the head with both hands.; Drive through your legs and hips explosively.; Pull the dumbbell to chin height, elbows high, then lower.
common_mistakes: Pulling with the arms only; Rounding the back
safety: Keep the dumbbell close and stop the pull below your chin.

name: Dumbbell thruster
form_cues: Hold dumbbells at your shoulders and squat down.; Drive up hard and use the momentum to press overhead.; Lower to the shoulders as you sink into the next squat.
common_mistakes: Pressing before you stand; Elbows dropping in the squat
regressions: Dumbbell front squat; Standing dumbbell shoulder press
safety: Keep your core braced and don't arch at the top.

name: L-drill
form_cues: Set three cones in an L, 5 m apart.; Sprint out and back, then go round the far cone in a figure eight.; Stay low and tight round the cones; sprint home.
common_mistakes: Running wide round the cones; Standing tall through the bends
safety: Use a grippy surface; rest fully between reps.
notes: NFL combine 3-cone drill.

name: Parachute sprint
form_cues: Clip the chute on and start with a strong forward lean.; Sprint hard so the chute opens behind you.; Keep your form tall and relaxed once the chute fills.
common_mistakes: Leaning back against the pull; Over-striding
safety: Use only in open space with no wind gusts that could yank you.
aliases: Speed chute sprint; Resistance parachute run
notes: No gear id for a speed chute; req is empty.

name: Shuttle run
form_cues: Sprint to the line and touch it with your hand.; Drop your hips and plant the outside foot to turn.; Push off hard and accelerate back.
common_mistakes: Turning tall and slow; Rounding wide turns instead of planting
safety: Wear grippy shoes on a non-slip surface.
notes: No cones? Use court or field lines. No gear id for cones, so req is empty.

name: Single-arm dumbbell snatch
form_cues: Start with the dumbbell between your feet, hips back, flat back.; Explode up through the hips and pull the dumbbell high and close.; Punch it overhead and stand tall; lower in stages.
common_mistakes: Pressing it up instead of pulling; Rounding the back at the start
regressions: Dumbbell high pull; Dumbbell hang clean
safety: Learn it light; lower the weight to the shoulder first, then the floor.
notes: Alternate arms each rep for conditioning work.

name: T-drill
form_cues: Sprint forward 10 m to the middle cone.; Shuffle 5 m left, 10 m right, 5 m back to the middle.; Backpedal to the start, staying low throughout.
common_mistakes: Crossing feet while shuffling; Standing tall in the shuffle
safety: Use a flat, non-slip surface.
notes: Cones laid out in a T; no gear id for cones, so req is empty.

name: Wall ball
form_cues: Hold the ball at your chest and squat to parallel.; Drive up and throw it to a target about 3 m high.; Catch it and go straight into the next squat.
common_mistakes: Partial squats; Throwing with the arms only; Catching with locked arms
regressions: Goblet squat; Medicine ball chest pass
safety: Use a soft wall ball; stand about an arm's length from the wall.
aliases: Wall ball shot; Wall balls; Med ball thruster
notes: CrossFit standard: 9 kg / 6 kg to 3 m / 2.7 m.

name: Zig-zag cone drill
form_cues: Set cones 3–5 m apart in a zig-zag.; Sprint to each cone and cut sharply off the outside foot.; Lower your hips before each cut.
common_mistakes: Rounding off the cuts; Leaning the body the wrong way on the cut
safety: Use a grippy surface; build up speed gradually.

name: Overhead backward medicine ball throw
form_cues: Hold the ball low between your legs, hips hinged.; Explode through the hips and throw the ball up and back over your head.; Let arms follow straight through.
common_mistakes: Squatting instead of hinging; Throwing with bent arms only
safety: Make sure the area behind you is completely clear.
aliases: Backward med ball toss; Granny toss; Reverse scoop throw
notes: Excellent hip-extension power drill; measure throw distance.

name: Underhand forward medicine ball throw
form_cues: Hinge with the ball held low between your legs.; Drive hips forward and throw the ball out and up.; Let the throw pull you into a step or jump forward.
common_mistakes: Using arms instead of hips; Rounding the back at the bottom
progressions: Overhead backward medicine ball throw; Broad jump
safety: Throw into open space away from people.
aliases: Forward scoop toss; Underhand med ball toss; Forward granny throw

name: Medicine ball shot-put throw
form_cues: Hold the ball at your shoulder, side-on to the wall.; Rotate the hips and push the ball out with one arm.; Follow through fully and reset each rep.
common_mistakes: Pushing with the arm before the hips turn; Elbow dropping under the ball
safety: Keep the wrist behind the ball; use a soft ball.
aliases: Med ball shot put; Single-arm rotational put

name: Medicine ball slam
form_cues: Lift the ball overhead, rising onto your toes.; Slam it down hard in front of your feet using your abs and lats.; Squat to pick it up with a flat back.
common_mistakes: Using a ball that bounces back into the face; Rounding the back to pick it up
safety: Use a dead (non-bounce) slam ball and keep the face away from the bounce.
aliases: Med ball slam; Overhead slam; Slam ball

name: Overhead medicine ball throw
form_cues: Stand or kneel with the ball overhead, arms long.; Brace the abs and pull the ball forward hard.; Release in front of the head into a wall or partner.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back to wind up; Throwing with elbows only
safety: Keep ribs down; use a soft ball for wall throws.
aliases: Soccer throw; Overhead forward throw; Med ball overhead pass

name: Rotational medicine ball slam
form_cues: Lift the ball overhead, then rotate towards one side.; Slam it down outside your foot, pivoting the back foot.; Pick up and alternate sides.
common_mistakes: Twisting through the lower back only; Not pivoting the back foot
safety: Use a dead slam ball; keep the spine long.
aliases: Side slam; Lateral med ball slam

name: Rotational medicine ball throw
form_cues: Stand side-on to a wall, ball at the back hip.; Drive the back hip round and let the arms follow.; Release hard into the wall and catch the rebound.
common_mistakes: Throwing with the arms instead of the hips; Rounding the lower back
safety: Use a soft or rebounding ball; check the wall can take impact.
aliases: Med ball side throw; Rotational scoop toss; Hip toss
notes: Great for golf, tennis, baseball and combat sports.

name: Clean and press
form_cues: Power clean to front rack; Stand and brace; Strictly press overhead
common_mistakes: Leaning back; Reverse-curling; Rushing
safety: Moderate loads.

name: Muscle snatch
form_cues: Extend fully on your toes first; Pull elbows high and out, then turn the bar over; Punch overhead without rebending your knees
common_mistakes: Dipping under the bar; Bar swinging out; Rushing the turnover
safety: Light weights only; it's a technique and upper-back builder.

name: Power jerk
equipment: Olympic barbell; Bumper plates; Squat rack
form_cues: Dip and drive hard; Jump feet out to squat stance; Catch with locked arms in a quarter squat
common_mistakes: Pressing out; Feet too wide; Lazy drive
safety: Use a rack and bumpers.

name: Push jerk
equipment: Olympic barbell; Bumper plates; Squat rack
form_cues: Dip and drive like a push press; Drop under into a partial squat; Catch with locked arms, then stand
common_mistakes: Pressing the bar out; Heels rising early; Leaning forward
safety: Use a rack and bumpers.

name: Push press
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Squat rack
form_cues: Bar on front delts, short dip; Drive with the legs; Press to lockout
common_mistakes: Deep dip; Leaning back; Slow transfer
safety: Use a rack; keep ribs down.

name: Split jerk
equipment: Olympic barbell; Bumper plates; Squat rack
form_cues: Dip straight down with the bar on your shoulders; Drive up hard, then split your feet; Lock the arms and recover feet together
common_mistakes: Pressing out; Dipping forward; Short split
safety: Use a rack and bumpers; miss forward.

name: Barbell jump squat
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Squat rack
form_cues: Use a light bar, around 20–30% of your squat; Dip quickly and jump as high as you can; Land softly and reset before the next rep
common_mistakes: Going too heavy; Landing stiff-legged; Bar bouncing on the neck
safety: Hold the bar tightly to your back; stop if your landings get sloppy.
notes: Trap bar jumps are safer for most people.

name: Barbell thruster
equipment: Olympic barbell; Weight plates; Squat rack
form_cues: Front-rack the bar; Squat to depth; Drive up and press overhead in one motion
common_mistakes: Pressing too early; Elbows dropping; Heels lifting
safety: Moderate loads.

name: Clean and jerk
form_cues: Clean the bar to a front squat and stand up; Reset your grip and breath; Dip, drive and split under to lock the bar overhead
common_mistakes: Rushing the jerk; Dipping forward; Soft elbows overhead
safety: Learn from a coach; drop the bar forward on a missed jerk.

name: Clean high pull
form_cues: Clean grip, start from floor or hang; Extend fully, then drive elbows high; Bar rises close to chest height
common_mistakes: Pulling early with arms; Bar swinging out; Not finishing hips
safety: Control the lowering.

name: Clean pull
form_cues: Set up like your clean; Push the floor away and keep the bar close; Finish tall with a strong shrug
common_mistakes: Bending the arms; Hips rising first; Leaning back
safety: Use straps if grip limits you.
notes: Usually loaded at 90–110% of your best clean.

name: Hang clean
form_cues: Start standing, hinge to just above the knees; Explode up and pull under; Catch in a full front squat
common_mistakes: Arms bending early; Hips swinging into the bar; Slow elbows
safety: Use bumpers; drop forward on a miss.

name: Hang power clean
form_cues: Hinge with the bar at mid-thigh; Jump and shrug; Whip elbows forward and catch above parallel
common_mistakes: Using the arms to lift; Wrists catching the bar; Leaning back
safety: Bumpers and a clear platform.
notes: Great entry point to Olympic lifting.

name: Hang power snatch
secondary_muscles: Shoulders; Upper back; Core; Calves; Triceps
form_cues: Lower the bar to mid-thigh with a flat back; Jump and shrug hard; Punch under and catch high with locked arms
common_mistakes: Pressing out the catch; Reverse-curling the bar up; Landing with feet too wide
safety: Use bumpers and drop the bar forward on a miss.
notes: A great first snatch variation to learn timing and speed.

name: Hang snatch
secondary_muscles: Shoulders; Upper back; Core; Calves; Triceps
form_cues: Start standing, lower the bar to just above the knees; Stay over the bar, then extend explosively; Drop into a full overhead squat to catch
common_mistakes: Bending the arms early; Hips hitting the bar out forward; Slow pull under
safety: Use bumpers on a platform; reset your back before each rep.
notes: Hang position can be mid-thigh, above knee or below knee.

name: Power clean
form_cues: Start like a deadlift with a flat back; Jump when the bar passes your knees; Fast elbows and catch high in a quarter squat
common_mistakes: Reverse-curling the bar; Catching with low elbows; Hips going forward early
safety: Use bumper plates and a platform.
notes: Popular with athletes for explosive power.

name: Power snatch
secondary_muscles: Shoulders; Upper back; Core; Calves; Triceps
form_cues: Start like a snatch with a wide grip; Extend fully, then pull under fast; Catch above parallel with arms locked
common_mistakes: Catching with bent arms (press-out); Jumping forward; Starting the pull too fast off the floor
safety: Use bumpers and a clear platform; miss by pushing the bar away and stepping back.

name: Snatch
secondary_muscles: Shoulders; Upper back; Core; Calves; Triceps
form_cues: Wide grip, bar over mid-foot, chest up and back flat; Push the floor away, then explode through hips and knees; Pull yourself under and catch in a deep overhead squat
common_mistakes: Pulling early with the arms; Bar swinging away from the body; Soft elbows in the catch
regressions: Power snatch; Hang snatch; Overhead squat
safety: Learn from a qualified coach and use bumper plates on a platform; drop the bar forward if you miss.

name: Snatch balance
equipment: Olympic barbell; Bumper plates; Squat rack
form_cues: Bar on your back with a snatch grip; Dip slightly, then push yourself under the bar fast; Catch in a full overhead squat with locked arms
common_mistakes: Pressing the bar instead of dropping under; Bar drifting forward; Feet landing too wide
safety: Practise bailing; use bumpers and a platform.

name: Snatch high pull
form_cues: Snatch grip, start from floor or hang; Extend fully, then pull elbows high and out; Keep the bar close to your body
common_mistakes: Pulling with the arms too early; Bar swinging out; Not finishing the extension
safety: Control the bar on the way down.

name: Snatch pull
form_cues: Set up exactly like your snatch; Push the floor away keeping the bar close; Finish fully extended with a shrug, arms straight
common_mistakes: Bending the arms; Leaning back excessively; Hips rising first
safety: Use straps if needed; keep the bar close.
notes: Often done at 90–110% of your best snatch.

name: Squat clean
form_cues: Bar over mid-foot, shoulder-width grip, back flat; Explode through the legs and hips, keeping the bar close; Pull under and catch in a deep front squat
common_mistakes: Pulling with the arms early; Catching with elbows down; Bar crashing on the shoulders
regressions: Power clean; Hang clean; Front squat
safety: Learn with a coach on a platform with bumpers; drop forward on a miss.

name: Sumo deadlift high pull
form_cues: Wide stance, narrow grip; Drive up with legs; Pull elbows high
common_mistakes: Pulling early; Rounding; Elbows low
safety: Moderate loads.

name: Trap bar jump
form_cues: Use about 20–30% of your trap bar deadlift; Dip quickly and jump as high as possible; Land softly, reset and repeat
common_mistakes: Going too heavy; Stiff landings; Rounding the back
safety: Land with soft knees and keep the bar under control.

name: Sled sprint
form_cues: Attach the harness at the waist and lean forward.; Sprint with powerful pushes and strong arm drive.; Keep the load light enough to keep good sprint form.
common_mistakes: Loading so heavy it becomes a walk; Bending at the waist
safety: Use a harness at the waist and a light load; rest fully between reps.
aliases: Resisted sled sprint; Sled tow sprint; Sled drag sprint
notes: Light (10–20% body weight) for speed; heavier for acceleration strength.

name: Clap push-up
form_cues: Lower to just above the floor with a tight body.; Explode up high enough to clap once.; Get hands back under shoulders and land softly.
common_mistakes: Not getting enough height and landing on the face; Body sagging in the air
safety: Practise on a soft mat; only progress once plyo push-ups are high and controlled.

name: Incline plyo push-up
form_cues: Hands on a wall, bench or counter, body straight.; Lower quickly, then push hard so your hands leave the surface.; Catch yourself with soft elbows and go again.
common_mistakes: Sagging hips; Landing with locked elbows
safety: Use a stable surface that will not slide.
aliases: Wall plyo push-up; Bench plyometric push-up
notes: The higher the hands, the easier it is.

name: Kneeling plyo push-up
form_cues: Kneel with hands under shoulders and a straight line knees to head.; Lower, then push explosively so hands leave the floor.; Land with soft elbows and flow into the next rep.
common_mistakes: Hips piking up; Flaring elbows wide
safety: Use a mat for the knees; stop if wrists hurt.

name: Plyo push-up
tags: Calisthenics; Chest; Compound; Home-friendly; Plyometric; Power
form_cues: Start in a strong plank, hands under shoulders.; Lower under control, then push hard so hands leave the floor.; Land with soft elbows and go straight into the next rep.
common_mistakes: Hips sagging or piking; Landing on locked elbows; Rushing with poor depth
progressions: Clap push-up; Depth push-up; Medicine ball chest pass
safety: Warm up wrists and shoulders; stop if you land with pain.
aliases: Explosive push-up; Plyometric push-up; Pop-up push-up

name: 180-degree jump squat
form_cues: Squat down and swing arms to start the turn.; Jump and rotate 180 degrees in the air.; Land facing the other way in a soft squat, then reverse.
common_mistakes: Twisting the knees on landing instead of turning fully in the air; Landing with feet too narrow
safety: Land with feet and knees pointing the same way; land softly with knees soft and tracking over toes; skip if you have acute knee or ankle pain.
aliases: 180 jump; Rotational jump squat; Half-turn jump

name: A-skip
form_cues: Skip forward, driving one knee to hip height.; Pull the foot down to strike under your hips.; Opposite arm drives with each knee; stay tall.
common_mistakes: Leaning back; Reaching the foot out in front; Arms crossing the body
safety: Use a flat surface and warm up first.
notes: Classic sprint mechanics drill; walk it as an A-march to learn it.

name: Alternate-leg bounding
form_cues: Push off one leg and drive the other knee forward and up.; Swing the opposite arm hard with each stride.; Cover as much ground per bound as you can, landing under hips.
common_mistakes: Turning it into a run with short strides; Landing heel-first far ahead of the body
safety: Use grass or a track; build up volume slowly to protect shins and Achilles.

name: B-skip
form_cues: Start like an A-skip, knee up to hip height.; Extend the lower leg forward, then paw it down and back.; Strike under your hips and keep a steady rhythm.
common_mistakes: Kicking the leg out and landing in front; Losing the skip rhythm; Slumping forward
safety: Stop if you feel hamstring tightness; warm up first.
notes: Teaches the active pull-back of the foot used in sprinting.

name: Broad jump
tags: Compound; Glutes; Home-friendly; Legs; Plyometric; Power
form_cues: Swing arms back and hinge at the hips.; Drive arms forward and jump as far out as you can.; Land in a quarter squat and hold the landing for a second.
common_mistakes: Landing with straight legs; Falling forward or backward on landing; Jumping too high instead of out
progressions: Consecutive broad jumps; Single-leg broad jump; Broad jump into sprint
safety: Land softly with knees soft and tracking over toes; skip if you have acute knee or ankle pain.
aliases: Standing long jump; Standing broad jump
notes: Measure distance from toes to heels to track progress.

name: Carioca
form_cues: Move sideways, crossing the trail leg in front then behind.; Rotate the hips while the shoulders stay square.; Stay on the balls of your feet and speed up as you get it.
common_mistakes: Turning the shoulders with the hips; Tripping over crossing feet by going too fast too soon
safety: Start slowly; use a flat, clear surface.
notes: Great dynamic warm-up for field and court sports.

name: Consecutive broad jumps
form_cues: Do one broad jump, then rebound straight into the next.; Spend as little time on the ground as possible.; Keep the arm swing rhythmic and powerful.
common_mistakes: Stopping fully between jumps; Collapsing knees on each landing
safety: Use a flat, non-slip surface; land softly with knees soft and tracking over toes; skip if you have acute knee or ankle pain.
aliases: Continuous broad jumps; Bunny hops; Repeated broad jumps

name: Countermovement jump
form_cues: Dip quickly into a quarter squat while swinging arms back.; Throw arms up hard and extend hips, knees and ankles together.; Reach as high as you can, then land quietly.
common_mistakes: Dipping too deep and slowly; Not using the arm swing
safety: Land softly with knees soft and tracking over toes; skip if you have acute knee or ankle pain.
aliases: Vertical jump; CMJ; Max vertical jump
notes: Rest fully between reps; quality over fatigue. Jump-and-reach against a wall to measure progress.

name: Dot drill
form_cues: Mark five dots like the five on a die.; Hop between dots in the set pattern as fast as you can.; Stay on the balls of your feet with quick contacts.
common_mistakes: Looking down at your feet; Big, slow hops
safety: Use tape on a non-slip floor.
notes: Do two-foot, then single-foot patterns.

name: Forward-backward line hops
form_cues: Stand behind a line with feet together.; Hop forward and back over it quickly.; Keep knees soft and contacts short.
common_mistakes: Landing heavy on the heels; Leaning too far forward
safety: Use a non-slip surface.
notes: Do single-leg for more challenge.

name: Frog jump
form_cues: Start in a wide, deep squat with fingers near the floor.; Jump up and forward, swinging arms overhead.; Land back in the deep squat and go again.
common_mistakes: Knees caving in when landing; Rounding the back at the bottom
safety: Only squat as deep as you can with a flat back; land softly with knees soft and tracking over toes; skip if you have acute knee or ankle pain.

name: Jump squat
tags: Cardio; Compound; Home-friendly; Legs; Plyometric; Power
form_cues: Sit back to a quarter or half squat, arms swinging back.; Drive through the whole foot and jump straight up.; Land softly and sink straight into the next rep.
common_mistakes: Landing stiff-legged with a loud thud; Knees caving in on take-off or landing; Rushing reps and losing height
regressions: Bodyweight squat; Squat to calf raise
progressions: Tuck jump; Dumbbell jump squat; Box jump
safety: Land softly with knees soft and tracking over toes; skip if you have acute knee or ankle pain.

name: Lateral bound
tags: Agility; Glutes; Home-friendly; Legs; Plyometric; Power; Unilateral
form_cues: Load on one leg and push hard sideways off it.; Jump as far as you can to the side.; Land on the opposite leg and stick it for a second.
common_mistakes: Landing with knee caving inward; Jumping up instead of out; Not controlling the landing
progressions: Continuous lateral bounds; Single-leg lateral hop
safety: Land softly with knees soft and tracking over toes; skip if you have acute knee or ankle pain.
notes: Make it continuous for conditioning; stick each landing for strength and control.

name: Lateral line hops
form_cues: Stand beside a line with feet together.; Hop side to side over it as fast as you can.; Stay on the balls of your feet with quick, light contacts.
common_mistakes: Hopping too high; Looking down and hunching over
progressions: Single-leg lateral hop; Lateral box jump
safety: Use a non-slip surface; ease in if ankles are stiff.
aliases: Side-to-side hops; Two-foot lateral hops; Lateral hops

name: Pause squat jump
form_cues: Lower to a half squat and hold still for 2–3 seconds.; Explode straight up without dipping first.; Stick the landing, reset, then repeat.
common_mistakes: Dipping before the jump, which defeats the pause; Holding too deep a squat
progressions: Dumbbell jump squat; Seated box jump
safety: Land softly with knees soft and tracking over toes; skip if you have acute knee or ankle pain.
notes: Trains starting strength by removing the stretch-shortening cycle.

name: Pike jump
form_cues: Jump straight up with a strong arm drive.; Lift straight legs forward and reach hands toward toes.; Drop legs back under you before you land.
common_mistakes: Bending the knees instead of piking; Landing off balance
safety: Needs good hamstring flexibility; land softly with knees soft and tracking over toes; skip if you have acute knee or ankle pain.

name: Pogo jumps
form_cues: Stand tall with almost-straight knees.; Bounce off the balls of your feet using only your ankles.; Keep ground contact quick and stiff, like a spring.
common_mistakes: Bending the knees too much; Landing on the heels; Letting the ankles collapse
progressions: Single-leg hop; Hurdle hops; Depth jump
safety: Build up slowly if you have Achilles or calf issues.
aliases: Pogo hops; Ankle hops; Ankling hops
notes: Great warm-up for running and jumping; builds ankle stiffness.

name: Power skip
form_cues: Skip, pushing hard off the ground for height.; Drive the knee and opposite arm up together.; Land softly and go straight into the next skip.
common_mistakes: Skipping low and fast instead of high; Weak arm drive
safety: Use a non-slip surface and build up gradually.
notes: Do it for distance instead of height as a variation.

name: Single-leg broad jump
form_cues: Stand on one leg, hinge and swing arms back.; Jump forward off one leg as far as you can.; Land on the same leg and hold it for two seconds.
common_mistakes: Knee caving on landing; Jumping further than you can control
safety: Master two-leg landings first; stop if knee feels unstable.
aliases: Single-leg standing long jump; Single-leg forward hop for distance
notes: Common return-to-sport hop test.

name: Single-leg hop
form_cues: Balance on one leg with a soft knee.; Hop forward a short distance and land on the same foot.; Keep the knee over the toes and hips level.
common_mistakes: Knee caving inward; Hip dropping on the free-leg side
progressions: Single-leg broad jump; Single-leg lateral hop
safety: Stop if the landing knee wobbles or hurts.

name: Single-leg lateral hop
form_cues: Stand on one leg beside a line.; Hop sideways over it and back on the same leg.; Land quietly with the knee tracking over the toes.
common_mistakes: Knee wobbling inward; Losing balance between hops
safety: Stop if the ankle or knee feels unstable.
aliases: Single-leg side hops; Lateral single-leg hop

name: Snap down
form_cues: Rise onto your toes with arms overhead.; Snap arms down and drop fast into an athletic quarter squat.; Freeze in the landing: chest up, hips back, knees over toes.
common_mistakes: Landing with knees caving; Too deep and slow a drop
safety: Teaches safe landing mechanics; keep the drop quick but controlled.
aliases: Drop squat; Snap-down drill; Drop and stick
notes: Use as a warm-up before any jumping session.

name: Split jump
tags: Cardio; Home-friendly; Legs; Plyometric; Power; Unilateral
form_cues: Start in a lunge, chest up, front knee over mid-foot.; Jump up and switch legs in the air.; Land softly back into a lunge and go straight away.
common_mistakes: Back knee slamming the floor; Front knee caving inward; Short, choppy stance on landing
progressions: Dumbbell split jump; Bulgarian split jump
safety: Land softly with knees soft and tracking over toes; skip if you have acute knee or ankle pain.
aliases: Jumping lunge; Plyo lunge; Lunge jump; Scissor jump

name: Straight-leg bound
form_cues: Keep knees nearly straight and stay tall.; Sweep each leg down and back, striking under your hips.; Pull the ground behind you with quick, active feet.
common_mistakes: Leaning back; Reaching the foot out in front
safety: Warm up well first; stop if you feel any hamstring tightness.
notes: Sprint drill that teaches a fast, backward-pulling foot strike.

name: Tuck jump
form_cues: Jump straight up from a quick dip.; Pull your knees up toward your chest at the top.; Untuck before landing and land softly on the balls of your feet.
common_mistakes: Landing while still tucked; Leaning forward instead of jumping vertically; Pausing too long between reps
safety: Land softly with knees soft and tracking over toes; skip if you have acute knee or ankle pain.

name: Wall drill
form_cues: Lean into a wall at about 45 degrees, hands on it.; Hold one knee up, toe pulled up, body in a straight line.; Switch legs explosively, striking down under your hips.
common_mistakes: Bending at the hips instead of leaning as a straight line; Feet drifting forward under the wall
safety: Wear shoes with grip so your feet do not slip.
aliases: Acceleration wall drill; Wall march; Wall run
notes: Teaches the body angle and leg action of acceleration.

name: Agility ladder: single-leg hops
form_cues: Hop on one foot into each square.; Land softly on the ball of the foot, knee slightly bent.; Keep the hip level and the knee over the toes.
common_mistakes: Knee caving on landing; Hopping too far and losing control
safety: Lay the ladder flat on a non-slip surface so it cannot slide.
aliases: Single-leg ladder hops; One-foot ladder hops
notes: Agility ladder has no gear id, so req is empty; tape on the floor works too.

name: Hurdle hops
form_cues: Line up 4–6 low hurdles about a stride apart.; Jump over each with both feet, tucking knees slightly.; Rebound quickly off each landing, staying tall.
common_mistakes: Long, sinking ground contacts; Clipping hurdles by not lifting the knees
safety: Use collapsible hurdles or cones that fall over if clipped.
notes: No gear id for hurdles; req is empty.

name: Agility ladder crossover
form_cues: Move sideways along the ladder.; Cross the trail foot over into each square, then step out.; Turn the hips, keep the shoulders square.
common_mistakes: Turning the whole body; Stepping on rungs
safety: Lay the ladder flat on a non-slip surface so it cannot slide.
notes: Agility ladder has no gear id, so req is empty; tape on the floor works too.

name: Agility ladder: hopscotch
form_cues: Hop with both feet into a square, then land one foot either side of the next.; Alternate in and out all the way down.; Keep contacts quick and quiet.
common_mistakes: Landing heavy on the heels; Losing rhythm halfway
regressions: Agility ladder: two feet in each
safety: Lay the ladder flat on a non-slip surface so it cannot slide.
notes: Agility ladder has no gear id, so req is empty; tape on the floor works too.

name: Agility ladder: lateral in-in-out-out
form_cues: Face the side of the ladder.; Step in, in, then out, out, moving down one square each time.; Keep your hips low and facing forward.
common_mistakes: Crossing the feet; Standing too tall
regressions: Agility ladder: two feet in each
safety: Lay the ladder flat on a non-slip surface so it cannot slide.
aliases: Lateral in and out; Lateral two-in ladder
notes: Agility ladder has no gear id, so req is empty; tape on the floor works too.

name: Agility ladder: one foot in each
form_cues: Run through, placing one foot in each square.; Stay on the balls of your feet, arms pumping.; Speed up only as long as you stay clean.
common_mistakes: Stepping on the rungs; Looking straight down the whole time
progressions: Agility ladder: two feet in each
safety: Lay the ladder flat on a non-slip surface so it cannot slide.
aliases: Quick feet ladder; Ladder run-through; One-in ladder
notes: Agility ladder has no gear id, so req is empty; tape on the floor works too.

name: Agility ladder: two feet in each
form_cues: Step both feet into each square, one after the other.; Keep steps short, light and fast.; Drive arms in rhythm with your feet.
common_mistakes: Heavy, flat-footed steps; Rushing and kicking the ladder
regressions: Agility ladder: one foot in each
safety: Lay the ladder flat on a non-slip surface so it cannot slide.
aliases: Two-in ladder; Two feet in each square
notes: Agility ladder has no gear id, so req is empty; tape on the floor works too.

name: Icky shuffle
form_cues: Step in-in, then out to the side, moving forward each square.; Alternate the outside step from side to side.; Stay light and rhythmic, eyes up.
common_mistakes: Losing the in-in-out rhythm; Big slow steps
safety: Lay the ladder flat on a non-slip surface so it cannot slide.
notes: Agility ladder has no gear id, so req is empty; tape on the floor works too.

name: Depth push-up
form_cues: Hold a plank with hands on two low boxes.; Drop hands to the floor between them, landing with soft elbows.; Push explosively back up onto the boxes.
common_mistakes: Landing on locked elbows; Hips sagging on the drop
safety: Only attempt once clap push-ups are solid; keep the boxes low.

name: Box jump
form_cues: Stand a foot from the box, swing arms back and dip.; Jump and land softly on the box in a quarter squat.; Stand tall, then step down rather than jumping off.
common_mistakes: Choosing a box so high you land in a deep squat; Jumping down repeatedly; Knees caving on landing
progressions: Seated box jump; Depth jump; Single-leg box jump
safety: Use a stable box; step down to protect Achilles and knees.
notes: Height of jump, not box, is the goal.

name: Depth drop
form_cues: Step off a low box, do not jump off.; Land on both feet at once in an athletic quarter squat.; Freeze the landing for two seconds.
common_mistakes: Landing loudly on the heels; Knees caving in; Stepping off a box too high
safety: Start at 30–45 cm; stop if knees ache.
notes: Teaches landing before you add depth jumps.

name: Depth jump
form_cues: Step off a low box and land on both feet.; Spend as little time on the ground as possible.; Rebound straight up as high as you can.
common_mistakes: Sinking too deep on landing; Box too high so you cannot rebound quickly; Jumping off the box instead of stepping
safety: Advanced shock drill: do it fresh, low volume, with a 30–60 cm box and good landing mechanics first.
notes: Rest 1–2 min between reps.

name: Lateral box jump
form_cues: Stand side-on to a low box.; Dip and jump sideways onto it, landing with both feet.; Step down and repeat, switching sides each set.
common_mistakes: Clipping the box edge; Landing with feet too narrow
safety: Start with a low box; step down each rep.
aliases: Side box jump; Lateral jump onto box

name: Power step-up
form_cues: Place one foot fully on a knee-height box.; Drive through that foot to jump up, swinging the other knee high.; Land softly with the same foot on the box and repeat.
common_mistakes: Pushing off the back foot; Box too high so the hip sinks below the knee
safety: Use a stable box that won't tip; keep the working knee over the foot.
aliases: Explosive step-up; Plyo step-up; Box step-up jump
notes: Alternating version switches feet in the air.

name: Seated box jump
form_cues: Sit on a bench facing the box, feet flat.; Swing arms and explode up off the seat onto the box.; Land softly and step down.
common_mistakes: Rocking back for momentum; Choosing too high a box
safety: Start with a low box; step down after each rep.
notes: Removes the countermovement to build starting strength.

name: Single-leg box jump
form_cues: Stand on one leg facing a low box.; Swing arms and jump onto the box off one leg.; Land on the same leg, stabilise, step down.
common_mistakes: Using too high a box; Knee caving on landing
safety: Use a low box; step down every rep.

name: Sandbag load to platform
form_cues: Lap the bag onto your thighs.; Hug it tight and extend the hips hard.; Drive the bag onto the platform without pressing it.
common_mistakes: Using the arms to throw the bag; Standing too far from the platform
safety: Use a stable platform at waist to chest height and keep fingers clear.
aliases: Sandbag over bar; Sandbag to platform
notes: Popular in strongman events and medleys.

name: Sandbag shouldering
form_cues: Lap the bag first by squatting and pulling it to your thighs.; Explode hips and pop the bag onto one shoulder.; Stand tall, then lower it under control.
common_mistakes: Lifting with the lower back alone; Not alternating shoulders
safety: A rounded back is normal on stone-style lifts but keep it braced; start light.

name: Sandbag bear-hug carry
form_cues: Hug the bag tight to your chest, hands clasped.; Stand tall and keep your chin over the bag.; Walk with short, quick steps and steady breathing.
common_mistakes: Leaning back excessively; Letting the bag slide down
safety: Lift the bag from the floor with a hinge, not a rounded back.

name: Suitcase carry
form_cues: Hold one weight at your side like a suitcase.; Stay perfectly upright; don't lean either way.; Walk slowly, then switch hands.
common_mistakes: Leaning away from or toward the weight; Hiking the hip
safety: Brace hard and pick the weight up with a hinge.

name: Atlas stone load
form_cues: Straddle the stone and wrap your arms deep around it.; Lap it onto your thighs, then re-grip high.; Extend hips explosively to roll it onto the platform.
common_mistakes: Pulling with straight legs; Stone too far from the body
safety: Use tacky and forearm sleeves, start light, and keep your feet clear of the drop.
notes: No gear id for stones; req uses sandbag, the closest home substitute.

name: Axle deadlift
equipment: Axle bar or barbell with thick grips; Weight plates
form_cues: Set up like a normal deadlift, double overhand grip.; Squeeze the thick bar hard before you pull.; Drive through the floor and lock out tall.
common_mistakes: Mixed grip to avoid grip work; Bar drifting away from the shins
safety: Use a hook or double overhand grip and lower with control; the axle doesn't spin.
notes: Thick grips on a regular barbell mimic an axle.

name: Sled rope pull
form_cues: Sit or stand in an athletic stance holding the rope.; Pull hand over hand, keeping the sled moving.; Brace your core and don't round your back.
common_mistakes: Pulling with a rounded back; Pausing between pulls
safety: Clear the rope path and keep fingers out of the sled hardware.

name: Log press
form_cues: Clean the log onto your chest, elbows high.; Dip and drive with the legs.; Press through to lockout with the head forward.
common_mistakes: Pressing with elbows low; Leaning back on the press
regressions: Sandbag overhead press; Standing barbell overhead press
safety: Learn the clean light and drop the log in front, never behind you.
notes: No log gear id; req uses barbell as nearest. Neutral grip suits sore shoulders.

name: Backward sled drag
form_cues: Hold the straps facing the sled, arms long.; Sit slightly and walk backward on the balls of your feet.; Keep tension in the straps and take steady steps.
common_mistakes: Standing too upright; Pulling with the arms
safety: Check the path behind you is clear before you start.
notes: Knee-friendly quad builder; often used for rehab.

name: Forward sled drag
form_cues: Clip the harness or hold the straps behind you.; Lean forward and drive each leg back powerfully.; Keep a tall spine and steady pace.
common_mistakes: Leaning too far and losing balance; Shuffling short steps
safety: Use a harness that sits at the waist or chest, not the neck.

name: Sled push
tags: Compound; Endurance; Legs; Power; Strength; Strongman
form_cues: Grip the poles with arms long and lean in at 45 degrees.; Drive knees forward and push through the balls of the feet.; Keep your back flat and steps powerful.
common_mistakes: Hips too high; Short, choppy steps
safety: Use a clear lane and a surface the sled slides evenly on.
notes: No eccentric load, so it is easy to recover from.

name: Tyre flip
form_cues: Squat down, chest against the tyre, fingers under the tread.; Drive forward and up with the legs, not the arms.; Pop a knee in, flip hands, and push it over.
common_mistakes: Deadlifting with a rounded back; Curling the tyre with the arms (biceps tear risk)
safety: Keep arms long (never curl the tyre) and stay clear of where it lands.
notes: No gear id for a tyre; req uses sled as the nearest strongman-area id.

name: Yoke carry
form_cues: Set under the yoke bar like a back squat.; Brace hard and stand it up.; Take short, fast steps, keeping the yoke level.
common_mistakes: Taking long strides that swing the yoke; Losing the brace and folding forward
safety: Learn with light loads on a flat surface and drop the yoke forward or back if you lose control.
notes: No yoke? A barbell in a rack can be walked out for short distances (bar walk). req uses barbell as nearest gear id.

name: Backstroke
secondary_muscles: Core; Glutes; Hip flexors; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Lie flat with your ears in the water, eyes up.; Enter little-finger first, arms straight overhead.; Kick steadily from the hips with loose ankles.
common_mistakes: Sitting in the water with hips low; Bending the knees too much on the kick
safety: Count strokes from the flags so you don't hit the wall.
notes: Good for posture: opens the chest. Needs pool access.

name: Bear crawl
secondary_muscles: Chest; Triceps; Hip flexors; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Hands under shoulders, knees under hips, knees hovering just off the floor.; Move opposite hand and foot together.; Keep your back flat like a tabletop.
common_mistakes: Hips shooting up high; Big, sloppy steps
safety: Use a clear, non-slip floor and stop if wrists hurt.
notes: Crawl forward and backward, or log distance (e.g. 4 × 10 m) in notes.

name: Breaststroke
secondary_muscles: Shoulders; Glutes; Latissimus dorsi; Heart and lungs
equipment: Swimming pool or open water; Goggles
form_cues: Pull, breathe, kick, glide—in that order.; Snap your heels round in a whip kick.; Glide with arms extended before the next stroke.
common_mistakes: Skipping the glide; Keeping the head up the whole time
safety: Breaststroke kick can strain the inner knee; ease in if you have knee issues.
notes: Needs pool access; no app gear id for a pool.

name: Brisk walking
form_cues: Walk tall with your eyes ahead, not at your feet.; Swing your arms naturally from the shoulders.; Pick a pace where you can talk but not sing.
common_mistakes: Strolling too slowly to raise your heart rate; Overstriding and landing hard on the heel
safety: Wear supportive shoes and start with shorter walks if you're new to exercise.
notes: Great daily base for fat loss and recovery days. Count your walk to the gym here.

name: Burpee broad jump
secondary_muscles: Chest; Hamstrings; Calves; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Do a burpee, then jump forward as far as you can.; Swing your arms and land softly on both feet.; Go straight into the next burpee where you land.
common_mistakes: Landing with knees caving in; Rushing so the burpee gets sloppy
safety: Needs clear space ahead and a non-slip surface.
notes: Popular in CrossFit and HYROX training; can also be logged by distance.

name: Burpees
secondary_muscles: Glutes; Shoulders; Triceps; Calves; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Squat, hands down, jump feet back to a plank.; Jump feet back in, then jump up with arms overhead.; Land softly and flow into the next rep.
common_mistakes: Belly flopping with a saggy back; Landing stiff-legged from the jump
safety: Scale to stepping if you have wrist, shoulder or low-back pain.

name: Butt kicks
secondary_muscles: Quadriceps; Hip flexors; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Flick your heels up toward your glutes.; Keep your knees pointing down at the floor.; Stay quick and light on your toes.
common_mistakes: Knees swinging forward; Leaning the torso forward
safety: Stop if you feel a cramp or pull in the hamstring.

name: Butterfly
secondary_muscles: Chest; Triceps; Glutes; Lower back; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Move in a wave from chest to hips to feet.; Sweep both arms together, out of the water and forward.; Use two dolphin kicks per arm stroke.
common_mistakes: Lifting the head too high to breathe; Bending the knees for a big kick instead of a body wave
safety: Very demanding on the shoulders and lower back—build up slowly.
notes: Needs pool access.

name: Fartlek run
form_cues: Mix fast bursts with easy running, no fixed plan needed.; Pick landmarks: surge to the next lamppost, then recover.; Keep the easy bits genuinely easy.
common_mistakes: Making every surge an all-out sprint; Stopping to walk instead of jogging the recovery
safety: Warm up well before surges to protect your hamstrings and calves.
notes: Swedish for 'speed play'. A fun way to add speed without a track.

name: Freestyle swimming
secondary_muscles: Triceps; Core; Glutes; Hip flexors; Heart and lungs
equipment: Swimming pool or open water; Goggles
form_cues: Keep your head down and body long and flat.; Rotate your body and reach long with each stroke.; Breathe to the side every 2–3 strokes.
common_mistakes: Lifting the head to breathe so the legs sink; Kicking from the knees instead of the hips; Crossing hands over the midline
safety: Swim in supervised areas; avoid open water alone.
notes: No app gear id exists for a pool, so 'req' is left empty—needs pool access.

name: High knees
form_cues: Drive each knee up to hip height.; Stay light on the balls of your feet.; Pump your arms in time with your legs.
common_mistakes: Leaning back to lift the knees; Landing heavy on the heels
safety: Use a softer surface or march instead if you have knee or ankle pain.
aliases: Running in place with high knees

name: Hiking
form_cues: Take shorter steps going uphill.; Lean slightly forward on climbs and use your glutes.; Go slow and controlled on descents.
common_mistakes: Locking the knees on descents; Starting too fast up the first climb
safety: Check weather, carry water, and use poles if your knees struggle downhill.
notes: Log elevation gain in notes if your watch tracks it.

name: Hill sprints
secondary_muscles: Hamstrings; Hip flexors; Core; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Lean slightly into the hill from your ankles.; Take short, powerful steps and pump your arms.; Walk back down slowly as your recovery.
common_mistakes: Running back down fast and pounding the knees; Looking at your feet instead of up the hill
safety: Choose a moderate grade (5–10%) and a non-slippery surface.
notes: Sprint 10–20 sec up; count each climb as one rep. Easier on the hamstrings than flat sprints.

name: Interval repeats (400 m)
secondary_muscles: Hip flexors; Core; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Run each repeat at a hard but even pace.; Jog or walk 200 m (or 90 sec) between repeats.; Aim to run the last repeat as fast as the first.
common_mistakes: Blasting the first repeat and dying on the rest; Too little recovery between repeats
safety: Warm up for 10–15 minutes first; skip if you have a calf or hamstring strain.
notes: Log each repeat as a set. Works on a track, road or treadmill.

name: Jogging
secondary_muscles: Hip flexors; Core; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Keep an easy, conversational pace.; Land lightly with your foot under your hips.; Relax your shoulders and keep your hands loose.
common_mistakes: Starting too fast and fading early; Long, heavy heel-striking strides
safety: Build weekly distance gradually (about 10% a week) to avoid shin and knee niggles.
notes: Couch-to-5K beginners can alternate 1 min jog / 2 min walk.

name: Jumping jacks
secondary_muscles: Glutes; Adductors; Abductors; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Jump feet wide as your arms sweep overhead.; Land softly with knees slightly bent.; Keep a steady rhythm and breathe.
common_mistakes: Landing stiff-legged; Half-reaching with the arms
safety: Step side to side instead of jumping if you have knee, ankle or pelvic floor issues.

name: Lateral shuffle
form_cues: Sink into a half squat with your chest up.; Push off the trailing foot and slide sideways.; Don't let your feet click together.
common_mistakes: Standing up tall between steps; Crossing the feet
safety: Wear shoes with lateral support; avoid slippery floors.

name: March in place
form_cues: Lift each knee to a comfortable height.; Swing your opposite arm with each step.; Stand tall and breathe steadily.
common_mistakes: Slouching forward; Shuffling with tiny lifts
safety: Hold a counter or wall for balance if you're unsteady.
aliases: Marching on the spot; Standing march
notes: Zero-impact option for beginners, older adults or small spaces.

name: Plank jacks
secondary_muscles: Adductors; Abductors; Calves; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Hold a straight plank on your hands.; Hop your feet wide, then back together.; Keep hips level and don't bounce them.
common_mistakes: Hips piking up; Sagging lower back
safety: Step feet out one at a time if your wrists or shoulders complain.

name: Push-up burpee
secondary_muscles: Triceps; Shoulders; Glutes; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Jump back to a plank and do a full push-up.; Keep your body in a straight line on the push-up.; Jump feet in, stand, and jump with a clap overhead.
common_mistakes: Worming up from the floor hips-first; Skipping the push-up range
safety: Drop the push-up when form slips; protect your shoulders and lower back.
aliases: Chest-to-floor burpee; Full burpee; Military burpee

name: Run-walk intervals
form_cues: Jog for a set time, then walk briskly to recover.; Keep the jog easy enough to repeat every round.; Walk with purpose; don't stop completely.
common_mistakes: Running the jog bits too hard; Cutting walk breaks short before you've recovered
safety: Ease off if you feel sharp pain in shins, knees or feet.
notes: Classic start: 1 min jog / 1–2 min walk, repeated 8–10 times. Lengthen the jog each week.

name: Running
secondary_muscles: Hip flexors; Core; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Stand tall with a slight forward lean from the ankles.; Take quick, light steps landing under your hips.; Drive your elbows back and keep your hands relaxed.
common_mistakes: Overstriding and braking with each step; Tensing the shoulders and clenching fists; Running every run hard
progressions: Tempo run; Trail running; Sprint intervals
safety: Increase distance slowly and replace worn-out shoes to protect knees and shins.
notes: Log distance and time; the app can work out your pace.

name: Sprint intervals
secondary_muscles: Calves; Hip flexors; Core; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Drive your knees up and arms hard, elbows at 90°.; Stay on the balls of your feet.; Walk back slowly to recover fully before the next one.
common_mistakes: Sprinting without a proper warm-up; Leaning back and reaching with the feet; Resting too little so quality drops
safety: Warm up thoroughly with jogging and drills; hamstring pulls are common with cold sprints.
notes: Typical session: 6–10 × 15–30 sec all-out, 1–2 min walk recovery.

name: Squat thrusts
form_cues: Squat down and plant your hands outside your feet.; Jump both feet back into a plank, then back in.; Stand up tall to finish each rep.
common_mistakes: Hips sagging in the plank; Rounding the back when you squat
safety: Step back instead of jumping to protect wrists and lower back.

name: Stair runs
form_cues: Run up every step, landing on the balls of your feet.; Pump your arms and keep your chest up.; Walk down carefully, holding the rail if needed.
common_mistakes: Rushing the way down; Hunching over and looking at your feet
safety: Use dry, well-lit stairs and always walk—never run—back down.
aliases: Stadium stairs; Stair sprints; Bleacher runs
notes: Take every second step for a glute-focused version.

name: Step jacks
form_cues: Step one foot out to the side as arms rise overhead.; Bring the foot back in and lower the arms.; Alternate sides at a brisk tempo.
common_mistakes: Moving too slowly to raise the heart rate; Shrugging the shoulders
safety: Fine for most joint issues since there's no jumping.
aliases: Low-impact jumping jacks; Side step jacks

name: Step-back burpee
form_cues: Squat and place your hands on the floor.; Step one foot back, then the other, into a plank.; Step back in and stand up tall.
common_mistakes: Rushing and letting the hips sag; Not standing all the way up
safety: Put your hands on a bench or step to shorten the range if needed.

name: Tempo run
secondary_muscles: Hip flexors; Core; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Warm up with 10 minutes of easy jogging first.; Hold a pace you could keep for about an hour—comfortably hard.; Breathe rhythmically and stay relaxed.
common_mistakes: Turning it into a race; Skipping the warm-up and cool-down
safety: Only do tempo work once or twice a week, with easy days in between.
notes: You should be able to speak a few words, not full sentences.

name: Trail running
secondary_muscles: Core; Hip flexors; Ankles; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Shorten your stride on uneven ground.; Look 2–3 metres ahead, not at your feet.; Power-hike steep climbs; it's often just as fast.
common_mistakes: Overstriding downhill; Chasing road pace on rough terrain
safety: Tell someone your route, carry water, and watch for roots and rocks.

name: Alternate-foot jump rope
form_cues: Jog in place, one foot per rope turn.; Keep the knees low and the steps light.; Turn the rope from the wrists.
common_mistakes: Lifting the knees too high and catching the rope; Rushing the rope speed
safety: Wear supportive shoes and build up time gradually.
aliases: Running step; Jogging step; Alternate foot step

name: Boxer skip
secondary_muscles: Shoulders; Forearms; Core; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Shift your weight side to side, one foot lightly tapping.; Keep the bounce tiny and rhythmic.; Stay relaxed so you can go for full rounds.
common_mistakes: Landing on both feet evenly so it's just a basic bounce; Tense shoulders
safety: Ease in if your calves or Achilles are tight.
notes: Boxers' staple: lets you skip for 3-min rounds with less fatigue.

name: Criss-cross jump rope
form_cues: Cross your arms at the waist on every second turn.; Push your hands past your hips when crossed.; Jump slightly higher on the crossing turn.
common_mistakes: Crossing the arms too high at the chest; Hands not wide enough so the loop is too small
safety: Use a slightly longer rope while learning.

name: Double unders
secondary_muscles: Shoulders; Forearms; Core; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Jump a little higher with straight, tight legs.; Flick the wrists hard so the rope passes twice.; Keep elbows in and hands at hip height.
common_mistakes: Piking or kicking the feet back; Swinging the arms wide; Jumping far too high
safety: Use a speed rope and expect whipped shins while learning.
notes: Practise with single-double-single combinations.

name: High-knee jump rope
form_cues: Drive each knee up to hip height as the rope passes.; Turn the rope fast to keep up with your feet.; Stay tall and land on the balls of your feet.
common_mistakes: Leaning back; Slowing the rope so the knees can't lift
safety: Stop if your hip flexors or calves feel strained.

name: Jump rope
secondary_muscles: Shoulders; Forearms; Quadriceps; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Turn the rope with your wrists, elbows close to your sides.; Jump just high enough to clear the rope.; Land softly on the balls of your feet.
common_mistakes: Jumping too high; Swinging the rope from the shoulders; Landing flat-footed
safety: Use a rope sized to your height and jump on a forgiving surface, not concrete.
notes: Can also be logged as reps (skips).

name: Rucking
secondary_muscles: Calves; Hamstrings; Core; Trapezius; Heart and lungs
equipment: Backpack or rucksack with weight; Weighted vest (optional)
form_cues: Wear the pack high and tight on your back.; Walk tall; don't lean far forward.; Keep a brisk, steady pace.
common_mistakes: Starting with a pack that's too heavy; Loose straps letting the load bounce
safety: Start around 10% of body weight and add load slowly to protect your back and feet.
aliases: Ruck march; Weighted walking; Backpack walk
notes: A loaded backpack works fine; 'weightvest' is the nearest app gear id.

name: Side-to-side jump rope
form_cues: Jump a few centimetres side to side with feet together.; Keep your shoulders square to the front.; Stay light and quick.
common_mistakes: Jumping too wide; Rolling the ankles on landing
safety: Avoid if you have unstable ankles.
aliases: Skier jump rope; Lateral jump rope

name: Single-leg jump rope
secondary_muscles: Quadriceps; Glutes; Core; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Hop on one foot with the other knee lifted slightly.; Keep the hops small and springy.; Hold your hips level.
common_mistakes: Hips dropping to one side; Landing heavy on the heel
safety: Build up slowly to avoid overloading the Achilles.

name: 12-3-30 treadmill workout
form_cues: Set the incline to 12% and speed to about 5 km/h.; Walk for 30 minutes without holding the rails.; Keep your chest up and strides natural.
common_mistakes: Gripping the handrails; Jumping straight in without building up
safety: Build up from shorter durations or lower incline; stop if calves or shins ache.
notes: Popular viral protocol: 12% incline, 3 mph (~4.8 km/h), 30 minutes.

name: 2,000 m row test
secondary_muscles: Glutes; Hamstrings; Core; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Plan an even split and stick to it.; Settle into rhythm after a strong first 10 strokes.; Empty the tank in the last 250 m.
common_mistakes: Going out way too fast; Losing technique in the middle 1,000 m
safety: A maximal effort—only do it when fully warmed up and healthy.
notes: Benchmark test for rowing fitness; repeat every 6–8 weeks.

name: Air bike
secondary_muscles: Chest; Back; Triceps; Hamstrings; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Push and pull the handles while you pedal.; Sit tall and keep a steady rhythm.; Remember: the harder you go, the harder it gets.
common_mistakes: Using only the legs; Starting too hard and blowing up
safety: Fan resistance rises fast—build up gradually.
aliases: Assault bike; Fan bike; Echo bike; Airdyne
notes: Can also log calories in notes.

name: Air bike intervals
secondary_muscles: Chest; Back; Hamstrings; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Sprint hard using arms and legs together.; Recover with slow, easy pedalling.; Keep each sprint the same quality.
common_mistakes: Going too hard on the first sprint; Hunching over the handles
safety: Extremely demanding—warm up well and stop if dizzy.
aliases: Assault bike sprints; Fan bike intervals
notes: Examples: 10 sec on / 50 sec off × 10, or 30/30.

name: Battle rope alternating waves
secondary_muscles: Core; Biceps; Quadriceps; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Sit back in a half squat, chest up.; Drive one arm up as the other goes down, fast.; Keep the waves travelling all the way to the anchor.
common_mistakes: Standing up straight and using only arms; Waves dying halfway down the rope
progressions: Battle rope double waves; Battle rope slams
safety: Anchor the rope securely and keep a neutral spine.
notes: Classic 20–30 sec on / 30–40 sec off.

name: Battle rope circles
secondary_muscles: Chest; Upper back; Core; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Make big circles with both arms, in sync.; Switch direction—inward, then outward.; Keep your stance athletic and core tight.
common_mistakes: Tiny circles from the wrists; Shrugging the shoulders
safety: Reduce range if you feel shoulder pinching.

name: Battle rope double waves
secondary_muscles: Core; Forearms; Glutes; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Hold a half squat with a braced core.; Raise and lower both arms together.; Make big, even waves to the anchor.
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back; Small, choppy waves
safety: Hinge at the hips rather than bending through the back.

name: Battle rope grappler throws
secondary_muscles: Glutes; Quadriceps; Forearms; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Hold both rope ends together at one hip.; Pivot and swing them across to the other hip in an arc.; Drive the turn from your legs and hips.
common_mistakes: Twisting the lower back without pivoting the feet; Using only the arms
safety: Pivot your back foot to protect your knees and lower back.

name: Battle rope slams
secondary_muscles: Glutes; Quadriceps; Triceps; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Raise both ropes overhead as you rise onto your toes.; Slam them down hard, dropping into a squat.; Reset quickly and repeat.
common_mistakes: Only using the arms with no leg drive; Rounding the back on the slam
safety: Keep your back neutral; don't overreach the arms behind the head.

name: Elliptical
secondary_muscles: Hamstrings; Calves; Chest; Back; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Stand tall with your weight through the whole foot.; Push and pull the handles to involve the upper body.; Use resistance so you're not just gliding.
common_mistakes: Leaning on the handles; Zero resistance, high speed
safety: A low-impact choice for sore knees or hips.

name: Incline treadmill walk
form_cues: Set an incline of 5–15% and a steady pace.; Stand upright and push through the whole foot.; Hands off the rails, arms swinging.
common_mistakes: Leaning back on the handrails; Cranking the incline so high you hunch
safety: Lower the incline if your lower back or Achilles feel strained.

name: Outdoor cycling
form_cues: Set saddle height so your knee is slightly bent at the bottom.; Spin smoothly; shift gears to keep your cadence up.; Relax your grip and keep elbows soft.
common_mistakes: Grinding a big gear at low cadence; Saddle too low causing knee pain
safety: Always wear a helmet and use lights in low visibility.
notes: No outdoor-bike gear id exists, so 'bike' (stationary bike) is used as the nearest match. Counts commuting too.

name: Recumbent bike
form_cues: Slide the seat so your knee is slightly bent at full reach.; Sit back against the backrest.; Push through the whole foot smoothly.
common_mistakes: Seat too close so knees come up high; Pedalling with no resistance
safety: Good option for back pain or balance issues since you're supported.
notes: No separate gear id; uses 'bike'.

name: Rowing intervals
secondary_muscles: Glutes; Hamstrings; Core; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Row each piece at a hard, steady split.; Keep your stroke rate controlled (26–32).; Rest 1–2 min between pieces.
common_mistakes: Spiking the stroke rate and losing power; Collapsing posture when tired
safety: Keep a neutral back throughout; stop if your lower back aches.

name: Rowing machine
secondary_muscles: Glutes; Hamstrings; Biceps; Core; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Legs, hips, then arms on the drive.; Arms, hips, then legs on the return.; Keep the handle level and wrists flat.
common_mistakes: Pulling with the arms first; Rounding the back at the catch; Damper set to 10
safety: Keep a neutral spine; set the damper around 3–5.
notes: Roughly 60% legs, 20% hips/back, 20% arms.

name: Spin bike intervals
secondary_muscles: Hamstrings; Calves; Core; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Alternate seated sprints with standing climbs.; Add resistance rather than spinning out of control.; Keep hips steady and core engaged out of the saddle.
common_mistakes: Too little resistance so you bounce; Bobbing the upper body when standing
safety: Set up the bike properly and use clipped or caged pedals.

name: Stationary bike
form_cues: Set the saddle at hip height when standing beside it.; Keep a slight knee bend at the bottom of the pedal stroke.; Pedal smoothly at 80–100 rpm.
common_mistakes: Saddle too low so knees ache; Bouncing on the saddle at high cadence
safety: Easy on knees and great for rehab—adjust the seat properly first.
notes: Log distance too if your bike shows it.

name: Tabata bike
equipment: Air bike, spin bike or stationary bike
form_cues: Sprint all-out for 20 seconds.; Pedal easy for 10 seconds.; Repeat 8 rounds without stopping.
common_mistakes: Pacing it like steady cardio; Skipping a proper warm-up
safety: Very intense—skip if you have heart or blood pressure concerns without medical clearance.
aliases: Tabata intervals on the bike; 20/10 bike intervals
notes: Original Tabata protocol: 8 × 20 sec all-out / 10 sec rest. Warm up for 5–10 min first.

name: Treadmill intervals
secondary_muscles: Hip flexors; Core; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Alternate fast running with easy jogging or walking.; Change speed with the buttons, not by jumping off.; Keep form tall and relaxed at speed.
common_mistakes: Straddling the belt on/off at high speed; Setting the sprint speed beyond control
safety: Use the safety key; build sprint speed gradually.
notes: Example: 1 min fast / 1–2 min easy × 8.

name: Treadmill run
secondary_muscles: Hip flexors; Core; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Set a 1% incline to mimic outdoor running.; Run in the middle of the belt with quick, light steps.; Look ahead, not down at the console.
common_mistakes: Holding the rails; Overstriding and landing far in front
safety: Use the safety key and step onto the side rails to stop.

name: Treadmill walk
form_cues: Walk tall in the middle of the belt.; Swing your arms; let go of the handrails.; Use a brisk pace, around 5–6 km/h.
common_mistakes: Holding the handrails the whole time; Walking too close to the front
safety: Clip on the safety key and straddle the belt before starting.

name: Arm bike
secondary_muscles: Biceps; Triceps; Chest; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Sit tall with the crank at shoulder height.; Pedal smoothly with your hands.; Switch direction halfway through.
common_mistakes: Hunching forward; Too much resistance so you jerk the cranks
safety: Useful when legs are injured; keep resistance low if shoulders are sore.
aliases: Upper body ergometer; UBE; Arm ergometer
notes: No arm-ergometer gear id; 'bike' used as nearest.

name: Curved treadmill run
secondary_muscles: Hip flexors; Core; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Move forward on the curve to speed up, back to slow down.; Run tall with quick, light steps.; Stay near the middle to hold a steady pace.
common_mistakes: Drifting too far forward and accelerating; Heavy heel-striking
safety: Use the handrails to get on and off safely; the belt keeps moving.
aliases: Assault Runner; Manual treadmill run; Woodway Curve

name: Curved treadmill sprints
secondary_muscles: Calves; Hip flexors; Core; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Lean into the curve and drive hard with your arms.; Stay on the balls of your feet.; Step back onto the rails to stop and rest.
common_mistakes: Sprinting cold without warm-up; Looking down at the belt
safety: Hold the rails when stepping off; the belt freewheels for a few seconds.
notes: Example: 8 × 20 sec all-out / 40 sec rest.

name: Ski erg
secondary_muscles: Shoulders; Glutes; Hamstrings; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Reach tall, then drive the handles down by hinging hips.; Finish with hands past your hips.; Let the arms float back up as you stand tall.
common_mistakes: Squatting deep instead of hinging; Pulling with arms only
safety: Hinge with a neutral back; don't crunch your spine forward.

name: Stair climber
form_cues: Stand tall and step through the whole foot.; Hold the rails lightly for balance only.; Pick a speed you can sustain without leaning.
common_mistakes: Hunching and leaning on the rails; Taking tiny steps on the toes
safety: Use the stop button rather than jumping off a moving machine.

name: VersaClimber
secondary_muscles: Latissimus dorsi; Calves; Core; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Move opposite arm and leg together.; Use long, full strokes before speeding up.; Stay upright, close to the machine.
common_mistakes: Short, choppy strokes; Leaning back away from the machine
safety: Brutally intense; start with short intervals.
notes: No VersaClimber gear id; 'stairs' (stair climber) used as nearest.

name: Front kick
form_cues: Lift the knee high, then push through the ball of the foot.; Lean back only slightly and keep your guard up.; Retract the leg quickly back to stance.
common_mistakes: Snapping the knee straight; Letting the hands drop
safety: Don't lock out the knee hard on air kicks.

name: Knee strikes
secondary_muscles: Glutes; Quadriceps; Calves; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Reach your hands forward as if gripping a head.; Drive the knee up and forward, hips through.; Rise onto the toes of the standing foot.
common_mistakes: Leaning back away from the knee; Lifting the knee without driving the hips
safety: Keep the standing knee soft; alternate legs to balance the load.

name: Roundhouse kick
form_cues: Pivot on the ball of your standing foot.; Swing the hip through and strike with the shin.; Bring the leg back to stance with your hands up.
common_mistakes: Not pivoting the standing foot; Kicking with just the leg, no hip turn
safety: Warm up hips and hamstrings first; kick low until mobility allows higher.

name: Shadow kickboxing
secondary_muscles: Hip flexors; Quadriceps; Obliques; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Mix punches with kicks and knees, hands always up.; Turn your hips over on every kick.; Return to stance after each combination.
common_mistakes: Leaning way back on kicks; Dropping the guard while kicking
safety: Kick only as high as your hips allow; warm up the hips first.

name: Shadowboxing
secondary_muscles: Chest; Triceps; Calves; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Stay in stance with hands up guarding your chin.; Throw crisp punches and snap them back.; Keep moving your feet between combinations.
common_mistakes: Dropping the hands after punching; Fully locking the elbows on every punch; Standing flat-footed
safety: Don't snap your elbows straight; keep a tiny bend at full extension.
notes: Rounds are usually 3 min work / 1 min rest. Light hand weights are optional but go easy.

name: Speed punches
secondary_muscles: Chest; Triceps; Core; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Square up with a slight bend in the knees.; Punch straight ahead, alternating as fast as you can.; Keep your core tight and shoulders down.
common_mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders up; Locking the elbows hard
safety: Keep a soft bend in the elbows to protect the joints.
notes: Common finisher in cardio kickboxing classes; works well as 20–30 sec intervals.

name: Sprawls
secondary_muscles: Chest; Shoulders; Glutes; Heart and lungs
form_cues: From a fighting stance, drop hands to the floor.; Shoot your legs back and drive hips down to the mat.; Snap your feet back under you and return to stance.
common_mistakes: Landing on straight arms and jarring the elbows; Hips staying high instead of pressing down
safety: Use a mat; build speed only once the movement is smooth.
notes: Takedown defence from wrestling/MMA and a brutal conditioning drill.

name: Heavy bag front kick
form_cues: Chamber the knee high before extending.; Push through the ball of the foot into the bag.; Keep your hands up and recover to stance.
common_mistakes: Kicking with toes and jamming them; Locking out the knee hard
safety: Strike with the ball of the foot, toes pulled back.
aliases: Bag teep; Push kick on bag

name: Heavy bag hooks
equipment: Punching bag; Gloves or hand wraps
form_cues: Bend the arm about 90° and keep the elbow up.; Turn the hips and pivot the lead foot into the punch.; Bring the hand straight back to guard.
common_mistakes: Swinging wide with an open arm; Punching with arm only, no hip turn
safety: Keep the wrist straight to avoid sprains.

name: Heavy bag jab-cross
equipment: Punching bag; Gloves or hand wraps
form_cues: Snap the lead hand straight out, then back to the chin.; Pivot the back foot and turn the hip for the cross.; Keep the non-punching hand guarding your face.
common_mistakes: Winding up before punching; Not rotating the back foot on the cross
safety: Punch with the first two knuckles and a straight wrist.

name: Heavy bag jab-cross-hook
secondary_muscles: Triceps; Core; Calves; Heart and lungs
equipment: Punching bag; Gloves or hand wraps
form_cues: Jab, cross, then lead hook in one smooth flow.; Let the cross's hip turn load the hook.; Reset to stance with hands up after each combo.
common_mistakes: Pausing between punches; Dropping the rear hand during the hook
safety: Stay in range so you don't overreach and strain the shoulder.
notes: Count each full combination as one rep.

name: Heavy bag knees
secondary_muscles: Glutes; Quadriceps; Shoulders; Heart and lungs
form_cues: Grip the top of the bag as if clinching.; Pull the bag in as you drive the knee up and through.; Rise onto the toes of your standing foot.
common_mistakes: Kneeing with hips pushed back; Not alternating sides
safety: Keep a firm grip; a swinging bag can catch you off balance.

name: Heavy bag punch-outs
secondary_muscles: Chest; Triceps; Core; Heart and lungs
equipment: Punching bag; Gloves or hand wraps
form_cues: Square up close to the bag.; Throw fast, straight punches non-stop.; Keep punches short and snappy, not wild.
common_mistakes: Wild, looping punches that hurt wrists; Leaning on the bag
safety: Use proper gloves and wraps; stop if a wrist or knuckle hurts.
notes: Great finisher: 20 sec all-out / 40 sec rest.

name: Heavy bag roundhouse kicks
form_cues: Step out, pivot on the standing foot, and turn the hip over.; Strike with the shin, not the foot.; Return quickly to a guarded stance.
common_mistakes: Kicking with the foot and hurting the instep; Leaning too far back
safety: Start light; shins need time to condition.
aliases: Bag round kicks; Thai kicks on the bag

name: Heavy bag uppercuts
equipment: Punching bag; Gloves or hand wraps
form_cues: Dip slightly with the knees, then drive up.; Punch upward with the palm facing you.; Keep the other hand guarding your chin.
common_mistakes: Dropping the hand low before punching; Leaning back as you punch
safety: An uppercut bag or teardrop bag is best; go lighter on a straight hanging bag.

name: Kickboxing bag rounds
secondary_muscles: Hip flexors; Quadriceps; Core; Heart and lungs
equipment: Punching bag (long/standing); Gloves or hand wraps
form_cues: Mix punches, kicks and knees in combinations.; Finish each combo with a step or angle change.; Pace yourself to last the full round.
common_mistakes: Throwing single strikes with no flow; Dropping the guard on kicks
safety: Wrap hands, warm up the hips, and start with light kicks.

name: Punching bag rounds
secondary_muscles: Chest; Triceps; Obliques; Calves; Heart and lungs
equipment: Punching bag; Gloves or hand wraps
form_cues: Wrap your hands and stand at arm's length from the bag.; Throw combinations, then move around the bag.; Return your hands to your face after every punch.
common_mistakes: Pushing the bag instead of snapping punches; Hands dropping as you tire; Holding your breath
progressions: Kickboxing bag rounds; Heavy bag punch-outs
safety: Always wear wraps and gloves; build intensity gradually to protect wrists.
notes: Typical: 3 × 3 min rounds with 1 min rest.

name: Speed bag
form_cues: Set the bag at mouth or chin height.; Hit in a steady rhythm with small circular motions.; Let the bag rebound three times before the next hit.
common_mistakes: Hitting too hard and losing rhythm; Arms too far from the bag
safety: Wear light gloves or wraps to protect your knuckles.
notes: No speed-bag gear id exists; 'bag' (punching bag) is used as nearest. Mostly a timing and shoulder endurance drill.

name: 90/90 hip switch
form_cues: Sit with both knees bent to 90°, one leg in front and one to the side.; Keep feet planted and rotate both knees to the other side.; Sit tall; use hands behind you only if needed.
common_mistakes: Slumping the lower back; Lifting the feet off the floor
safety: Use hand support if knees or hips are irritated.
aliases: Shin box switch; Windshield wiper hip switch

name: Active straight leg raise
form_cues: Lie on your back with both legs straight.; Raise one straight leg as high as you can without help.; Press the other leg firmly into the floor.
common_mistakes: Bending the raised knee; Bottom leg lifting off the floor
safety: Keep the lower back flat; useful as a hamstring mobility check.
aliases: ASLR; Lying leg raise for mobility

name: Adductor rock-back
form_cues: Kneel on all fours and straighten one leg out to the side.; Rock hips back toward your heel.; Keep your back flat and return forward.
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back; Rotating the foot up
safety: Keep the range comfortable on the groin.

name: Ankle circles
form_cues: Lift one foot off the floor or sit with the leg extended.; Draw slow, full circles with your toes.; Change direction halfway.
common_mistakes: Moving the whole leg instead of the ankle; Rushing small circles
safety: Move only in a pain-free range after ankle sprains.

name: Arm circles
form_cues: Stand tall with arms straight out to the sides.; Draw small circles, then gradually make them bigger.; Reverse direction halfway through.
common_mistakes: Shrugging shoulders up to the ears; Arching the lower back
safety: Keep circles pain-free; shrink them if anything pinches.

name: Deep squat hold
form_cues: Sit down into the bottom of a squat, feet flat.; Push knees out with your elbows and lift your chest.; Shift side to side gently to explore the range.
common_mistakes: Heels rising off the floor; Collapsing the chest forward
regressions: Box squat hold; Hold a doorframe for support
safety: Hold onto something if heels lift; skip if deep knee flexion hurts.
aliases: Bodyweight squat hold; Asian squat; Prying squat
notes: Raise heels on a plate if ankle mobility limits depth.

name: Frankenstein walk
form_cues: Walk forward kicking one straight leg up.; Reach the opposite hand toward the toes.; Keep your chest up and standing leg tall.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back to reach the toes; Kicking higher than your hamstrings allow
safety: Kick only to a comfortable height; this is a warm-up, not a max test.

name: Front-to-back leg swing
form_cues: Hold a wall and stand tall on one leg.; Swing the free leg forward and back like a pendulum.; Let the range grow gradually with each swing.
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back to fake range; Swinging wildly from the first rep
safety: Start small and build range; keep the swing controlled.
aliases: Forward leg swings; Sagittal leg swings
notes: Classic pre-run and pre-leg-day drill.

name: Hip CARs
tags: Balance; Home-friendly; Mobility; Rehab; Unilateral; Warm-up
form_cues: Brace your core and lift one knee to hip height.; Rotate the knee out, open it to the side, then sweep the leg back.; Move as slowly as possible with zero movement in the torso.
common_mistakes: Leaning or twisting the trunk; Moving fast to get through sticky spots
safety: Stay in a pain-free range and keep the trunk locked.
aliases: Hip controlled articular rotations; Standing hip circles (controlled)
notes: From Functional Range Conditioning; also done on all fours.

name: Inchworm
form_cues: Hinge forward and place hands on the floor, bending knees as needed.; Walk hands out to a plank, keeping hips level.; Walk hands back toward the feet and stand up.
common_mistakes: Letting the hips sag in the plank; Walking hands out too far for your strength
safety: Bend the knees as much as needed to protect your lower back.
notes: Add a push-up at the plank for a fuller warm-up.

name: Knee-to-wall ankle mobilization
form_cues: Stand facing a wall in a split stance, front toes a few cm away.; Drive the front knee toward the wall over the middle toes.; Keep the heel glued to the floor.
common_mistakes: Heel lifting; Knee caving inward
safety: Move the foot back as you improve; stop with sharp front-of-ankle pain.
notes: Doubles as a dorsiflexion test: aim for about 10 cm toe-to-wall.

name: Lateral leg swing
form_cues: Face a wall with both hands on it.; Swing one leg across your body and out to the side.; Keep your hips and chest facing the wall.
common_mistakes: Twisting the torso with each swing; Locking the standing knee
safety: Keep swings controlled; ease off if you feel groin pinching.
aliases: Side-to-side leg swings; Frontal leg swings

name: Lumbar rotations
form_cues: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.; Let both knees fall slowly to one side.; Keep shoulders flat and return through the middle.
common_mistakes: Lifting the opposite shoulder; Dropping the knees too fast
safety: Move within a pain-free range; great gentle option for stiff backs.

name: Open book
form_cues: Lie on your side with knees bent to hip height and arms out front.; Open the top arm across, following it with your eyes.; Keep the knees stacked on the floor.
common_mistakes: Knees lifting apart; Forcing the arm to the floor
safety: Squeeze a pillow between knees to keep the lower back still.
aliases: Side-lying thoracic rotation; Open book stretch

name: Quadruped thoracic rotation
form_cues: Kneel on all fours and sit the hips slightly back.; Place one hand behind your head.; Rotate that elbow down under the body, then up toward the ceiling.
common_mistakes: Rotating from the lower back; Shifting hips side to side
